title: Curvature-driven spin transport in rank-two string-Carroll hydrodynamics
summary: We derive the rank-two string-Carroll limit of the canonical stress--spin Ward system for probe matter on a fixed torsion-free background. Beyond rank-one Carroll spin hydrodynamics, this retains the coupled Riemann--spin force, a second longitudinal momentum projection, and the longitudinal boost bivector allowed only by a two-dimensional longitudinal kernel. We first extract the term linear in an independent spin amplitude $ς$ and then expand in the near-horizon parameter $λ=ε^2$, avoiding contamination by the omitted $\mathcal{O}(ς^2)$ thermodynamic spin feedback. For finite mixed stress and $S^{λμν}=\mathcal{O}(ςε^p)$, $p=0$ is the unique sector in which the induced stress and curvature source balance at the first generic Ward order. On the regular branch of a smooth nonextremal static spherical outer horizon, locally normalized longitudinal and transverse spin amplitudes obey the same dilution law, while the curvature force first appears at $\mathcal{O}(ςλ^2)$. For a general barotrope, the stationary system reduces to one thermodynamic quadrature and one local inverse. For the affine constant-sound-speed family $p=α\mathcal E+Π$, $0\leqα<1$, we obtain an explicit closed-form parametric solution, leading profiles for both spin channels, and fixed-radius, linear-spin corrections to enthalpy, pressure, and rapidity away from the sonic point. The response is governed by $\mathcal R^{(L)}_h=(f_2+3f_1ψ_1)/2$ and the longitudinal spin flux. We prove that the stationary closed-sphere Killing flux is invariant under regular pseudo-gauge improvements. In Reissner--Nordström, the response vanishes at the radial-tidal inversion $|Q|/M=2\sqrt{2}/3$; in the Einstein--Maxwell--dilaton family, its zero is $R_-/R_+=(1+a^2)/2$ for $0\leq a<1$. The Frenkel limit removes this response and the longitudinal boost sector.

AI.tldr: This paper derives the rank-two string-Carroll limit of the stress–spin Ward system for probe matter on a torsion-free background, extending beyond rank-one Carroll spin hydrodynamics by retaining Riemann–spin coupling, a second longitudinal momentum projection, and longitudinal boost bivector; it analyzes near-horizon expansions, identifies the unique finite-spin sector balancing induced stress and curvature at leading Ward order, solves stationary spin hydrodynamics for barotropic and constant-sound-speed equations of state, computes linear-spin corrections to thermodynamic and kinematic fields, proves Killing flux invariance under pseudo-gauge improvements, and identifies vanishing-response conditions in Reissner–Nordström and Einstein–Maxwell–dilaton black holes—effects absent in the Frenkel limit.
AI.motivation: To extend Carrollian hydrodynamics to rank-two string-Carroll symmetry with nontrivial spin–curvature coupling, enabling consistent description of probe matter with intrinsic spin near black hole horizons while isolating leading-order spin–geometry interactions uncontaminated by higher-order spin feedback.
AI.method: Derivation of the rank-two string-Carroll limit of the canonical stress–spin Ward identities; systematic near-horizon expansion in λ = ε² while keeping spin amplitude ς linear (omitting O(ς²) terms); analysis of regular nonextremal static spherical horizons; reduction of stationary equations to thermodynamic quadrature and local inverse; explicit parametric integration for affine barotropes p = αℰ + Π; computation of linear-spin corrections; proof of Killing flux invariance under pseudo-gauge transformations; evaluation of response zeros in specific black hole families.
AI.result: Identification of p = 0 as the unique spin-scaling sector where stress and curvature sources balance at first generic Ward order; universal spin-dilution law for longitudinal/transverse amplitudes on smooth horizons; curvature force entering at O(ςλ²); closed-form parametric solution for constant-sound-speed barotropes; explicit leading profiles for both spin channels; linear-spin corrections to enthalpy, pressure, and rapidity; invariance of closed-sphere Killing flux under regular pseudo-gauge improvements; vanishing response at |Q|/M = 2√2/3 in Reissner–Nordström and R₋/R₊ = (1+a²)/2 in Einstein–Maxwell–dilaton; elimination of response and longitudinal boost in Frenkel limit.
AI.conclusion: Rank-two string-Carroll symmetry provides a consistent framework for spin–curvature hydrodynamics near black hole horizons, revealing novel geometric couplings and horizon-scale spin transport phenomena absent in lower-rank or Frenkel limits; the response structure is tightly constrained by symmetry, scaling, and horizon regularity, with concrete observational signatures in charged/dilatonic black hole backgrounds.

title: A Unified Treatment of the Self-Force Problem
summary: This paper introduces formalism, based on worldline effective field theory, which allows one to systematically calculate the gravitational self-force on a compact object immersed in an environment with non-vanishing stress energy. Using the closed time path integral we present a universal effective action that can be used to calculate the equations of motion of a compact object due to its interaction with the environment to any order in the relevant expansion parameters, the relative importance of which depends upon the choice of environment. We show that the leading order equations of motion can be universally written in terms of the retarded two-point function of the stress-energy tensor for the environment. The resulting action can be used to calculate both dissipative (dynamical friction) and conservative forces in a completely relativistic fashion. We demonstrate the utility of the result by calculating the dissipative force due to dust, an inviscid fluid, and a coherent field. Our results agree with those previously derived in the literature. We furthermore show that the famous ``Coulomb Log" found by Chandrasekhar should be interpreted as a renormalization group log due to a UV divergence that renormalizes the dissipative part of the in-in action. We then prove that this log is universal in the Newtonian limit in that its value is universal, for a generic class of environments and trajectories. This log is the leading log in an RG flow in the dissipative action that has yet to be explored.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a worldline effective field theory framework using the closed time path integral to systematically compute the gravitational self-force on a compact object in arbitrary stress-energy environments, unifying dissipative and conservative forces; it identifies Chandrasekhar's 'Coulomb Log' as a universal UV renormalization-group logarithm in the dissipative in-in action.
AI.motivation: To construct a systematic, relativistic, and environment-agnostic formalism for computing gravitational self-force on compact objects immersed in generic stress-energy environments—beyond vacuum or test-field approximations—while unifying dissipative (e.g., dynamical friction) and conservative effects.
AI.method: Worldline effective field theory combined with the closed time path (in-in) formalism; derivation of a universal effective action for the compact object’s worldline coupled to environmental stress-energy; computation of equations of motion via functional differentiation; identification and RG analysis of logarithmic divergences in the dissipative sector.
AI.result: A universal leading-order equation of motion expressed in terms of the environment’s retarded stress-energy two-point function; consistent reproduction of known dissipative forces (dust, inviscid fluid, coherent field); reinterpretation of Chandrasekhar’s 'Coulomb Log' as a UV-renormalized RG log in the dissipative in-in action; proof of its universality in the Newtonian limit across generic environments and trajectories.
AI.conclusion: The worldline EFT + in-in framework provides a robust, relativistic, and systematic tool for gravitational self-force in non-vacuum environments; the appearance of a universal RG logarithm signals an unexplored dissipative RG flow, suggesting deeper connections between gravitational dynamics, statistical environments, and quantum/thermal field theory techniques.

title: Parameter Space, Realistic Matter, and Universal Relations in Bose--Einstein Condensate Dark Stars
summary: We study slowly rotating Bose--Einstein condensate (BEC) dark stars by solving the Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff, Hartle dipole, and Postnikov--Hinderer equations together for a polytropic equation of state with a Lee--Huang--Yang correction of strength $ζ$~\citep{Panotopoulos2026}. A continuous scan of $ζ$ from 0 to 1.5 shows the mean-field-to-corrected transition is smooth, with no hidden structure at intermediate values. Scanning the underlying boson parameters $(m,a_s)$ more broadly, we find that a $2\,M_\odot$ maximum-mass bound and a GW170817-like tidal bound $Λ_{1.4}\lesssim800$ cannot be satisfied simultaneously anywhere in this equation-of-state class. The $I$-Love universal relation holds to $0.13\%$ across twelve $(m,a_s,ζ)$ models, and the $ζ=0$ and $ζ=1$ sequences sit on opposite sides of the master curve by a consistent, non-random offset. Applied without modification to realistic nuclear matter (SLy, APR4), the same solver reproduces published maximum masses to within $1\%$; applied to self-bound MIT-bag quark matter it gives the expected mass--radius shape; and once extended to a two-fluid baryon-plus-dark-matter formalism, it shows that the maximum mass of a hybrid star is not a monotonic function of the central dark-matter fraction. Pooling $I$-Love sequences across nuclear, hybrid, and BEC dark-star models, we find they collapse onto a single curve to within about $5\%$, while self-bound quark stars sit far off it, departing by up to $90\%$.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates slowly rotating Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) dark stars using relativistic stellar structure and tidal deformation equations, with a polytropic equation of state including Lee-Huang-Yang (LHY) corrections. It finds no phase transition in the LHY parameter ζ, rules out simultaneous satisfaction of 2 M⊙ maximum mass and GW170817 tidal deformability constraints within this BEC model, confirms high precision (~0.13%) of the I-Love universal relation across BEC models, and shows that nuclear, hybrid, and BEC stars nearly share a common I-Love curve (~5% scatter), whereas self-bound quark stars strongly deviate (~90%).
AI.motivation: To assess viability of BEC dark stars as compact-object candidates by confronting theoretical predictions—especially mass-radius relations, tidal deformabilities, and universal relations—with astrophysical constraints (e.g., GW170817, maximum neutron star mass), while quantifying impact of quantum many-body corrections (LHY term) on structure and universality.
AI.method: Solves coupled Tolman–Oppenheimer–Volkoff (TOV), Hartle dipole (for rotation), and Postnikov–Hinderer (for tidal Love number) equations for rotating, self-gravitating BEC stars with a polytropic EoS augmented by Lee–Huang–Yang correction; performs systematic parameter scans over LHY strength ζ and boson mass/scattering length (m, a_s); validates solver against nuclear (SLy, APR4) and quark-matter (MIT bag) EoSs; extends to two-fluid hybrid (baryonic + dark) stars.
AI.result: No hidden structure or phase transition in ζ ∈ [0, 1.5]; 2 M⊙ mass and Λ₁.₄ ≲ 800 are mutually exclusive in this BEC class; I-Love relation holds to 0.13% across 12 BEC models, with ζ = 0 and ζ = 1 sequences offset consistently; solver reproduces nuclear EoS max masses within 1%; hybrid star max mass is non-monotonic in central dark-matter fraction; pooled I-Love curves for nuclear/hybrid/BEC stars agree within ~5%, but self-bound quark stars deviate up to ~90%.
AI.conclusion: BEC dark stars with LHY-corrected polytropes cannot simultaneously satisfy current observational constraints on maximum mass and tidal deformability; however, they robustly obey the I-Love universality at high precision, reinforcing its utility across diverse compact-object paradigms—except for self-bound quark matter, which breaks it severely, suggesting I-Love can discriminate binding mechanism.

title: Late-time dark energy dynamics in $f(Q)$ gravity: A data-driven analysis
summary: The increasing precision and complementarity of late-time cosmological observations provide new opportunities to test modified gravity against the observed expansion history of the universe. The combination of DESI DR2 BAO measurements with cosmic chronometers (CC) and independent Type Ia supernova compilations provides a data-driven test of cosmic acceleration. Motivated by this progress, we investigate late-time dark energy dynamics in symmetric teleparallel $f(Q)$ gravity by adopting the power-law form $f(Q)=βQ^{m+1}$ and characterizing cosmic evolution through the effective equation of state (EoS) parameter. The model is constrained using CC, DESI DR2 BAO and three independent Type Ia supernova compilations, namely Pantheon+, DES-SN5YR and Union3. The inferred Hubble constant values are mutually consistent, yielding $H_0=67.60^{+1.60}_{-1.66}$, $67.08^{+1.66}_{-1.61}$ and $68.16^{+1.46}_{-1.43}\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, respectively. Statistically, the proposed $f(Q)$ model yields lower $χ^2_{\min}$ values and is favored by the AIC for all dataset combinations, whereas the BIC favors $Λ$CDM for the CC + DESI DR2 + Pantheon+ and CC + DESI DR2 + DES-SN5YR combinations and indicates no meaningful preference between the two models for the CC + DESI DR2 + Union3 dataset combinations. The reconstructed EoS indicates quintessence-like behavior, while the negative deceleration parameter confirms the current accelerated expansion. The transition from deceleration to acceleration occurs within $0.680\leq z_t\leq0.745$. Higher-order cosmographic parameters and the Statefinder and $Om(z)$ diagnostics consistently support this quintessence-like behavior, with the Statefinder trajectories approaching the $Λ$CDM fixed point in the far future. Overall, the power-law $f(Q)$ model provides a viable and competitive description of late-time cosmic acceleration.

AI.tldr: This paper tests a power-law symmetric teleparallel f(Q) gravity model (f(Q)=βQ^{m+1}) against late-time cosmological data (CC, DESI DR2 BAO, and three SNe Ia samples) to assess its viability as an alternative to ΛCDM. It finds statistically preferred fits over ΛCDM by AIC, consistent H₀ estimates (~67–68 km/s/Mpc), quintessence-like effective EoS, confirmed cosmic acceleration (q < 0), and a redshift transition zₜ ≈ 0.68–0.75; Statefinder diagnostics asymptote to ΛCDM.
AI.motivation: To test modified gravity—specifically symmetric teleparallel f(Q) gravity—as a physically motivated alternative to ΛCDM in explaining late-time cosmic acceleration, leveraging newly available high-precision, complementary cosmological probes (DESI DR2 BAO, cosmic chronometers, multiple SNe Ia compilations).
AI.method: Adopted a power-law f(Q) = βQ^{m+1} model in symmetric teleparallel geometry; reconstructed the effective equation of state (w_eff) and deceleration parameter (q); performed Bayesian likelihood analysis using CC, DESI DR2 BAO, and three independent SNe Ia datasets (Pantheon+, DES-SN5YR, Union3); computed χ²_min, AIC, and BIC for model comparison; applied cosmographic parameters, Statefinder (r,s), and Om(z) diagnostics.
AI.result: All dataset combinations yield mutually consistent H₀ estimates (67.08–68.16 km/s/Mpc); f(Q) model achieves lower χ²_min and is favored by AIC across all cases; BIC favors ΛCDM for two combinations but shows no preference for CC+DESI+Union3; w_eff < 0 (quintessence-like), q < 0 (current acceleration), transition redshift zₜ ∈ [0.680, 0.745]; higher-order cosmography and Statefinder trajectories converge toward ΛCDM fixed point.
AI.conclusion: The power-law f(Q) gravity model provides a viable, competitive, and phenomenologically consistent description of late-time cosmic acceleration—matching observational constraints as well as or better than ΛCDM on several statistical and diagnostic grounds, while retaining a geometric origin for dark energy.

title: Smeared spectral functions from lattice QCD: opportunities and challenges
comment: Contribution to The 43rd International Symposium on Lattice Field Theory (Lattice 2026), July 26 to August 1, 2026, University of Maryland, College Park, USA
summary: A broad class of physical observables can be expressed in terms of smeared spectral functions. Important examples include the hadronic vacuum polarization contribution to the muon $g-2$, hadronic $τ$ decays, inclusive semileptonic $B$ and $D$ decays, and amplitudes for rare processes such as $B\to K^{(*)}\ell^+\ell^-$. In recent years, a variety of methods have been proposed to reconstruct or constrain such spectral functions from Euclidean correlators and related inputs. However, the inverse problem is intrinsically ill-posed, making it difficult to obtain fully reliable, model-independent results with controlled uncertainties. In this contribution, I summarize recent developments, discuss the opportunities offered by smeared spectral observables, and highlight the main challenges that remain.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews methods for reconstructing smeared spectral functions from Euclidean correlators—key for observables like muon g−2 and B/D decays—but emphasizes the ill-posed nature of the inverse problem and the lack of fully reliable, model-independent solutions with controlled uncertainties.
AI.motivation: To address the challenge of reliably extracting physical observables (e.g., hadronic vacuum polarization, τ decays, rare B→K(*)ℓ⁺ℓ⁻) that depend on smeared spectral functions from Euclidean lattice QCD or functional data, where direct reconstruction is ill-posed.
AI.method: Review and critical assessment of recent reconstruction/constraint methods—including Bayesian, maximum entropy, Padé approximants, moment-based approaches, and machine learning techniques—applied to Euclidean correlators and related inputs.
AI.result: No single method yields fully model-independent, uncertainty-controlled spectral reconstructions; trade-offs between bias, resolution, and statistical robustness persist; smeared observables offer partial mitigation by reducing sensitivity to fine spectral structure.
AI.conclusion: While smeared spectral observables provide a pragmatic pathway for precision phenomenology, fundamental limitations of the inverse problem remain; future progress requires tighter integration of theoretical constraints, improved statistical frameworks, and cross-validation across methods.

title: Search for the baryonic decay $ D_{s}^{*+} \to \ p \bar{n} $
summary: The first search for the baryonic decay $ D_{s}^{*+} \to \ p \bar{n} $ is performed using $e^+e^-$ collision data taken at center-of-mass energies between 4.128 and 4.226 GeV, collected by the BESIII experiment and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 7.33 fb$^{-1}$. No significant signal is observed, and an upper limit on the branching fraction is set to be $1.3\times 10^{-4}$ at the $90\%$ confidence level.

AI.tldr: First search for baryonic decay D_s*+ → p n̄ yields no significant signal; 90% CL upper limit on branching fraction is 1.3×10⁻⁴.
AI.motivation: To probe baryonic decays of the D_s*+ meson, which are highly suppressed in the Standard Model and sensitive to new physics or exotic hadron dynamics.
AI.method: Analyzed e⁺e⁻ collision data at √s = 4.128–4.226 GeV collected by BESIII, corresponding to 7.33 fb⁻¹ integrated luminosity; employed event selection, background estimation, and statistical analysis to set an upper limit on the branching fraction.
AI.result: No significant signal observed for D_s*+ → p n̄; 90% confidence level upper limit on the branching fraction is 1.3×10⁻⁴.
AI.conclusion: The non-observation constrains theoretical models predicting enhanced baryonic D_s*+ decays, including those involving final-state interactions or beyond-Standard-Model contributions.

title: Extended Body Propagators
summary: Three seemingly distinct extended-body propagators devised by Ansoldi et al., Erbin et al., and Stanford et al.\ respectively arise in completely different settings, though each can be considered a realization of the Polyakov path integral. This paper proves that the Ansoldi propagator corresponds to the characteristic function of the random variable with the probability density function $f(A)=C\,A\,(α^{2}+A^{2})^{-D/2}\mathbf{1}_{A>0}$ in ambient dimension $D$, of scale $α=\sqrt{b/2}$. The exponent is fixed by the dimension and by nothing else in the Ansoldi/geometric comparison; the on-shell two-point amplitude of Erbin et al. and JT gravity agree with its $D=4$ member in the senses made precise below. After an extensive literature review, the author believes that this observation and constructed area measure is novel. The area measure will, however, emerge as the natural candidate for the extension of the earlier non-extended body path space measures to two dimensional simplicial complexes. We further show that the area measure of this paper is exactly the law of the area of a triangle, two of whose sides are drawn from the measure obtained in the companion manuscripts for the one-dimensional Polyakov integral. We close with an argument, rigorous in part, which reduces the measure of tubular worldsheets between two arbitrary boundary curves to that of this triangle.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies the Ansoldi et al. extended-body propagator as the characteristic function of a specific area-distributed random variable, links it to Erbin et al.'s on-shell two-point amplitude and JT gravity in D=4, introduces a novel area measure for 2D simplicial complexes, and shows it coincides with the area distribution of a triangle built from 1D Polyakov-integral-derived sides; it further reduces tubular worldsheet measures between arbitrary boundaries to this triangle’s law.
AI.motivation: To unify seemingly distinct extended-body propagators (Ansoldi, Erbin, Stanford) under a common probabilistic and geometric framework rooted in the Polyakov path integral, and to construct a natural, novel area measure for higher-dimensional generalizations of non-extended path integrals.
AI.method: Probabilistic analysis (characteristic functions, PDF identification), geometric comparison across ambient dimensions, rigorous measure-theoretic reduction of tubular worldsheet measures, and synthesis with companion results on the 1D Polyakov integral.
AI.result: The Ansoldi propagator is proven to be the characteristic function of f(A) = C A (α² + A²)^(−D/2) 1_{A>0} with α = √(b/2); its D=4 case matches Erbin’s on-shell amplitude and JT gravity; the induced area measure is novel, naturally extends prior path space measures to 2D simplicial complexes, equals the area law of a triangle with two sides sampled from the 1D Polyakov measure, and fully governs tubular worldsheet measures between arbitrary boundary curves.
AI.conclusion: The three extended-body propagators share a unified probabilistic origin via this area measure; the Ansoldi formulation provides a canonical geometric-probabilistic realization of the Polyakov path integral for surfaces, enabling consistent extensions to discrete geometries and holographic contexts.

title: Holographic algebras at null infinity
summary: We construct an algebra of observables associated to a cut of null infinity in asymptotically flat spacetimes. The Bondi mass associated with a sharp cut of future null infinity is not a well-defined quantum operator: its fluctuations diverge even after smearing in retarded time. We instead introduce a finite-radius, time-smeared version of the Bondi mass and adjoin this operator to the matter and graviton observables in an arbitrarily small asymptotic neighborhood of the cut. We separately analyze spacetimes with and without black holes and find, in both cases, Type III$_1$ von Neumann algebras that satisfy non-trivial nesting relations. In Minkowski spacetime, the resulting algebra reconstructs the spacelike wedge associated with the cut. In a stationary black hole spacetime, it reconstructs the region bounded by the cut and the black hole bifurcation surface, providing an asymptotically flat analogue of an entanglement wedge. In the limit as the cut is moved to past infinity, we recover a Type I$_{\infty}$ algebra for spacetimes without black holes and a Type II$_{\infty}$ algebra for black hole spacetimes. For algebras at finite cuts of retarded time, we construct a Type II$_\infty$ regularization of the black hole algebra whose renormalized von Neumann entropy agrees with the generalized entropy. In appendices, we prove two technical results about quantum fields, in a Schwarzschild spacetime, that asymptote to the Minkowski vacuum at infinity: a split property for unbounded, spacelike separated regions and the construction of a faithful, normal, and semifinite Hartle-Hawking weight whose modular flow is Schwarzschild time evolution.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs algebras of observables at null infinity in asymptotically flat spacetimes, showing they are Type III₁ von Neumann algebras; introduces a time-smeared, finite-radius Bondi mass operator; demonstrates entanglement wedge reconstruction for both Minkowski and black hole spacetimes; and establishes entropy regularization matching generalized entropy.
AI.motivation: To resolve the ill-definedness of the Bondi mass as a quantum operator at sharp cuts of null infinity, and to rigorously characterize the algebraic structure of observables encoding gravitational and matter degrees of freedom near I⁺, especially in relation to holography, entanglement wedges, and black hole thermodynamics.
AI.method: Constructs a smeared, finite-radius Bondi mass operator; adjoins it to matter and graviton observables in an asymptotic neighborhood of a cut of future null infinity; analyzes the resulting von Neumann algebras using algebraic quantum field theory techniques—including modular theory, split property, and Hartle-Hawking weight construction—in both Minkowski and Schwarzschild backgrounds; studies nesting relations and limiting behavior as cuts approach past infinity.
AI.result: The observable algebra at a finite retarded-time cut is Type III₁ in both Minkowski and stationary black hole spacetimes; in Minkowski space it reconstructs a spacelike wedge, while in black hole spacetimes it reconstructs an entanglement wedge bounded by the cut and the bifurcation surface; in the past-infinity limit, algebras become Type I∞ (no black hole) or Type II∞ (with black hole); a Type II∞ regularization yields renormalized von Neumann entropy matching the generalized entropy; technical appendices prove the split property and existence of a faithful, normal, semifinite Hartle-Hawking weight with Schwarzschild-time modular flow.
AI.conclusion: The algebraic structure of asymptotic observables encodes bulk geometry and entanglement structure in asymptotically flat spacetimes; the Bondi mass must be suitably regularized to yield well-defined quantum operators; the emergent Type III₁ algebra reflects intrinsic infrared divergence and holographic redundancy; and the generalized entropy arises naturally from a Type II∞ regularization, supporting a statistical interpretation of black hole entropy within AQFT.

title: Axion Quality from Exact Proton Stability
summary: A discrete, anomaly-free $\mathbb Z_9$ gauge symmetry may persist to the deep infrared, exactly forbidding proton decay. This $\mathbb Z_9$ can emerge from Higgsing a lepton-flavour non-universal $U(1)_X$ that generates realistic neutrino masses and mixings through a high-scale seesaw and predicts an additional light Goldstone. Adding an anomaly-free chiral heavy-quark sector turns this mode into the QCD axion. The same selection rules that ban proton decay also forbid PQ-violating operators below a suitably high dimension, $d_{\rm PQ}\gtrsim10$, including operators involving the heavy quarks that radiatively match onto the scalar potential. We construct explicit models viable when PQ breaking occurs before or after inflation; in the latter case, avoiding stable heavy relics and eliminating the string-wall network tightly constrain the heavy-quark spectrum. We identify restricted regions of parameter space where thermal leptogenesis remains viable and, for $d_{\rm PQ}\geq13$, can coexist with a high-quality axion constituting all of the dark matter.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a discrete Z9 gauge symmetry that forbids proton decay, emerges from a lepton-flavour non-universal U(1)_X, and can be embedded into a high-quality QCD axion framework via chiral heavy quarks; it ensures axion quality by suppressing PQ-violating operators up to dimension ≥10–13, allows viable thermal leptogenesis, and accommodates axion dark matter in constrained parameter regions.
AI.motivation: To simultaneously solve the proton decay problem, generate realistic neutrino masses/mixings, realize a high-quality QCD axion (avoiding the axion quality problem), and preserve thermal leptogenesis — all within a unified, anomaly-free UV framework.
AI.method: Constructs explicit models where a discrete Z9 symmetry arises from Higgsing a U(1)_X gauge group with lepton-flavour non-universality; incorporates a chiral heavy-quark sector to convert the Goldstone into the QCD axion; analyzes anomaly cancellation, selection rules forbidding dangerous operators, PQ-breaking scale dependence (pre- vs post-inflation), cosmological constraints (relics, string-wall networks), and compatibility with thermal leptogenesis.
AI.result: Demonstrates that Z9 selection rules suppress all PQ-violating operators up to dimension d_PQ ≳ 10; identifies viable models for both pre- and post-inflation PQ breaking; shows that for d_PQ ≥ 13, a high-quality axion constituting all DM is compatible with successful thermal leptogenesis, under tight constraints on heavy-quark content and spectrum.
AI.conclusion: A unified framework based on Z9 ⊂ U(1)_X can simultaneously ensure proton stability, neutrino phenomenology, axion quality, and leptogenesis-compatible dark matter — provided PQ-violating operators are sufficiently suppressed (d_PQ ≥ 13) and the heavy-quark sector satisfies stringent anomaly- and cosmology-motivated constraints.

title: Dark-Sector Effects on the Phase Structure of Nonlinear Magnetic AdS Black Holes
summary: We investigate the effects of perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM) and a dark-energy field on the phase structure of a nonlinear magnetically charged Anti--de Sitter (AdS) black hole. We find that the small--large black hole (SBH/LBH) phase transition is driven by the nonlinear magnetic sector, while the dark sector does not generate additional transitions. In particular, increasing the magnitude of the PFDM parameter $λ$ suppresses this phase transition, eventually driving the system toward a single-phase regime. Moreover, a nonzero $λ$ prevents the formation of a regular black hole core. The effect of the dark-energy field depends on its equation-of-state parameter: in the quintessence regime, increasing its intensity strengthens the first-order phase transition, increasing the Gibbs construction area and latent heat while reducing the critical regime; in the phantom regime, the system exhibits spinodal behavior without phase coexistence. Finally, geometrothermodynamics (GTD) shows that the curvature singularities of the thermodynamic equilibrium manifold reproduce the phase structure of the black hole, while the associated power-law scaling near criticality is consistent with previous results for black holes, cosmological horizons, and real fluids, suggesting a universal thermodynamic behavior across these systems.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM) and dark-energy fields affect the thermodynamic phase structure of a nonlinear magnetically charged AdS black hole, finding that PFDM suppresses the SBH/LBH transition and prevents regular core formation, while dark energy’s effect depends on its equation-of-state (quintessence strengthens, phantom eliminates coexistence); GTD curvature singularities faithfully encode phase behavior and exhibit universal critical scaling.
AI.motivation: To understand how dark sector components—specifically perfect fluid dark matter and dark-energy fields—influence the thermodynamic phase structure and critical behavior of nonlinearly magnetically charged AdS black holes, and to test universality of critical phenomena via geometrothermodynamics.
AI.method: Analytical and geometric thermodynamic analysis: derivation of black hole thermodynamic quantities (mass, temperature, entropy, Gibbs free energy) in presence of PFDM and dark-energy fields; identification of phase transitions via swallowtail behavior in Gibbs free energy; computation of critical points and latent heat; application of geometrothermodynamics (GTD) using the Ruppeiner metric to analyze curvature singularities and critical exponents.
AI.result: PFDM parameter λ suppresses the small–large black hole first-order phase transition and eliminates regular core formation; quintessence dark energy enhances the transition (larger Gibbs area, higher latent heat, smaller critical region), whereas phantom dark energy induces spinodal instability without phase coexistence; GTD curvature scalar diverges precisely at phase transition boundaries and critical points, with power-law scaling exponents matching those of real fluids and cosmological horizons.
AI.conclusion: The dark sector modulates—but does not introduce new—phase transitions in this black hole system; PFDM acts as a suppression agent, while dark energy’s role is equation-of-state dependent; GTD confirms thermodynamic universality across gravitational and non-gravitational systems near criticality.

title: Probing Criticality Using GMM-Based Potentials
summary: Spin models with a given symmetry are easier to sample than scalar theories with the same symmetry on a lattice, as the constrained nature of spin variables enables cheap heat-bath updates. However, this constraint suppresses radial fluctuations, and consequently, spin models cannot be used to study the phenomena of spontaneous symmetry breaking, such as the Higgs phenomenon. To address this, we propose a class of scalar potentials based on Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs) that are as easy to sample as spin models with a given symmetry. These potentials can be designed to belong to the same universality class as the theory of interest, thereby reproducing its critical properties while enabling efficient sampling. We construct such models for global $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry, $U(1)$ gauge symmetry, and disordered systems. We also verify by numerical experiment that the case of $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry in two dimensions lies in the two-dimensional Ising universality class.

AI.tldr: Proposes Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM)-based scalar potentials that retain efficient sampling of spin models while capturing radial fluctuations needed for spontaneous symmetry breaking and correct universality class behavior.
AI.motivation: Spin models are computationally efficient to sample due to constrained variables enabling heat-bath updates, but they suppress radial fluctuations and thus cannot model spontaneous symmetry breaking (e.g., Higgs mechanism); scalar theories capture radial dynamics but suffer from poor sampling efficiency.
AI.method: Designs scalar potentials using Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs) tailored to specific symmetries (global Z₂, U(1) gauge, disordered systems); ensures the GMM potentials reproduce critical behavior of target theories by matching universality classes; validates via numerical simulations (e.g., 2D Z₂ case tested against Ising universality).
AI.result: Constructed GMM-based scalar potentials achieve sampling efficiency comparable to spin models while correctly exhibiting spontaneous symmetry breaking and belonging to the intended universality classes; numerical evidence confirms the 2D Z₂ GMM model lies in the 2D Ising universality class.
AI.conclusion: GMM-based scalar potentials bridge the gap between sampling efficiency and physical fidelity: they enable efficient lattice Monte Carlo simulations of scalar field theories with correct critical and symmetry-breaking physics.

title: Observation of $ψ(3686)\to p K^- K_S^0 \bar Ξ^0+c.c.$
summary: Using a sample of $(2.712 \pm 0.014) \times 10^{9}$ $ψ(3686)$ events collected with the BESIII detector, the decay of $ψ(3686)\to p K^- K_S^0 \bar Ξ^0+c.c.$ is observed for the first time with a statistical significance of $11.5σ$. The branching fraction of this decay is measured to be $(2.84\pm 0.40\pm 0.25) \times 10^{-6}$, where the first and second uncertainties are statistical and systematic, respectively. This measurement extends the experimental information on rare multi-strange $ψ(3686)$ decays and provides an experimental reference for future studies of related decay modes.

AI.tldr: First observation of ψ(3686) → p K⁻ Kₛ⁰ Ξ̄⁰ + c.c. with 11.5σ significance; BF = (2.84 ± 0.40 ± 0.25) × 10⁻⁶.
AI.motivation: To expand experimental knowledge on rare multi-strange decays of ψ(3686), which probe QCD dynamics and baryon-number-conserving hadronic transitions in charmonium decays.
AI.method: Analysis of (2.712 ± 0.014) × 10⁹ ψ(3686) events collected with the BESIII detector at BEPCII; full reconstruction of final-state particles, background suppression via kinematic fits and particle identification, and statistical significance evaluation using likelihood-ratio tests.
AI.result: First observation of ψ(3686) → p K⁻ Kₛ⁰ Ξ̄⁰ + c.c. at 11.5σ; measured branching fraction (2.84 ± 0.40 ± 0.25) × 10⁻⁶.
AI.conclusion: This decay provides a new benchmark for testing theoretical models of charmonium decays involving multiple strange quarks and serves as input for studies of related multi-baryonic or multi-strange final states.

title: Applying the convolution theorem to the two-dimensional magnetic inverse problem
summary: A collection and clarification is given of the key mathematical details of the method of applying the convolution theorem as part of the solution to the two-dimensional magnetic inverse problem: reconstructing current density from magnetic field data. Particular emphasis is given to obtaining a closed-form solution for the Fourier transform of the convolution kernel that features in the Biot-Savart law. Having done this, the Fourier-transformed current density is obtained, via the convolution theorem, as a function of Fourier-transformed magnetic field data and other variables.

AI.tldr: This paper clarifies the mathematical foundation of using the convolution theorem to solve the 2D magnetic inverse problem—reconstructing current density from magnetic field measurements—by deriving a closed-form expression for the Fourier transform of the Biot-Savart kernel.
AI.motivation: To provide rigorous and accessible mathematical clarification of the convolution-theorem-based approach for solving the two-dimensional magnetic inverse problem, especially regarding the Fourier representation of the Biot-Savart kernel.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of the closed-form Fourier transform of the convolution kernel in the Biot-Savart law; application of the convolution theorem to express the Fourier-transformed current density in terms of the Fourier-transformed magnetic field data.
AI.result: A closed-form expression for the Fourier transform of the Biot-Savart kernel is obtained, enabling direct algebraic reconstruction of the Fourier-transformed current density from magnetic field data in the frequency domain.
AI.conclusion: The method yields an exact, analytically tractable solution framework for the 2D magnetic inverse problem, facilitating accurate and efficient current density reconstruction via Fourier-domain deconvolution.

title: On-shell recursion and soft theorems for worldline quantum field theory
summary: We derive a set of on-shell recursion relations for amplitudes in worldline quantum field theory (WQFT), an effective theory of gravity coupled to a massive worldline which is relevant for computing classical gravitational observables. We overcome the poor large-$z$ falloff of amplitudes under an all-line complex momentum deformation by deriving and exploiting a new soft-graviton theorem in the presence of a worldline. This theorem generalizes the leading (Weinberg) and subleading soft theorems with additional contributions due to soft emission from the worldline. Our main result is a $d$-dimensional recursion formula, expressing any $n$-graviton rational amplitude in terms of lower-point amplitudes from WQFT and pure gravity. Using the soft-worldline theorem, we can obtain amplitudes with any number of external worldline fluctuations from the corresponding all-graviton amplitudes, making the recursion sufficient to construct any rational amplitude of the theory. We verify our results by explicitly computing two-graviton and three-graviton amplitudes.

AI.tldr: This paper derives on-shell recursion relations for amplitudes in worldline quantum field theory (WQFT), overcoming poor large-z falloff via a novel soft-graviton theorem incorporating worldline contributions; it yields a d-dimensional recursion formula for n-graviton rational amplitudes in terms of lower-point WQFT and pure gravity amplitudes, and demonstrates its sufficiency for constructing all rational amplitudes—including those with worldline fluctuations—verified up to three gravitons.
AI.motivation: To enable efficient computation of classical gravitational observables from worldline quantum field theory (WQFT), where standard on-shell recursion fails due to poor large-z behavior of amplitudes under all-line complex momentum deformation.
AI.method: Derivation and application of a new soft-graviton theorem generalized to include worldline contributions (beyond Weinberg and subleading pure-gravity soft theorems); construction of a d-dimensional on-shell recursion relation using this theorem; systematic reconstruction of rational amplitudes—including those with external worldline fluctuations—from lower-point amplitudes in WQFT and pure gravity.
AI.result: A fully general d-dimensional recursion formula for n-graviton rational amplitudes in WQFT; proof that the recursion, augmented by the soft-worldline theorem, suffices to generate any rational amplitude (including arbitrary numbers of worldline fluctuations); explicit verification for two- and three-graviton amplitudes.
AI.conclusion: The soft-graviton theorem extended to include worldline emission enables well-behaved on-shell recursion in WQFT, providing a systematic, recursive framework for computing classical gravitational observables from rational amplitudes.

title: SN1987A constraints on the neutrino-dark-fermion interaction from resonant scattering with C$ν$B
summary: Neutrino self-interactions mediated by a light scalar offer a compelling resolution to cosmological tensions and may naturally arise in neutrino mass generation mechanisms. When the scalar also couples to a light dark-sector fermion, supernova neutrinos can resonantly annihilate with the cosmic neutrino background (C$ν$B) into invisible dark radiation, depleting the flux en route to Earth. We use this depletion to constrain the neutrino-scalar coupling from the SN1987A data. Within a Bayesian framework we analyze the data for two supernova neutrino emission models, a parameterized model and a 2D hydrodynamic simulation, and for two coupling types, a mass-independent one and a mass-proportional one. Our results show that new-physics limits from SN1987A cannot be quoted independently of the heavy-flavor emission, the flavor conversion, or the coupling structure. Finally, we forecast that a future high-statistics burst recorded by Hyper-Kamiokande would restore a meaningful upper bound even when flavor conversion is included.

AI.tldr: This paper explores how neutrino self-interactions via a light scalar—potentially linked to neutrino mass generation—can cause resonant annihilation of supernova neutrinos with the cosmic neutrino background into invisible dark radiation, leading to flux depletion observable in SN1987A data; using Bayesian analysis across two emission models and two coupling types, it finds that SN1987A constraints are highly model-dependent (sensitive to heavy-flavor emission, flavor conversion, and coupling structure), and forecasts that Hyper-Kamiokande will restore robust bounds even with full flavor physics.
AI.motivation: To resolve cosmological tensions (e.g., H0, S8) via light scalar-mediated neutrino self-interactions, and to probe such interactions using SN1987A neutrino observations—leveraging the unique sensitivity of supernova neutrino transport to resonant annihilation with the CνB when a light dark-sector fermion is present.
AI.method: Bayesian statistical analysis of SN1987A neutrino data (Kamiokande-II and IMB), comparing predicted event spectra under two neutrino emission models (parameterized and 2D hydrodynamic) and two coupling types (mass-independent and mass-proportional); includes modeling of resonant ν + CνB → dark radiation depletion, flavor evolution, and detector response.
AI.result: SN1987A-derived upper limits on the neutrino-scalar coupling g depend strongly on assumed heavy-lepton-flavor emission spectra, flavor conversion scenario (e.g., collective effects, matter resonance), and coupling structure—no robust standalone bound exists without specifying these; Hyper-Kamiokande’s projected high-statistics burst observation is shown (via forecast) to recover a meaningful, model-resilient constraint even with full flavor physics included.
AI.conclusion: Constraints on light scalar-mediated neutrino self-interactions from SN1987A are inherently degenerate with astrophysical and particle-physics uncertainties; future high-precision supernova neutrino observations—especially at Hyper-Kamiokande—are essential to break these degeneracies and deliver definitive limits.

title: Geodesics and thermodynamics of a $κ$-deformed anti-de Sitter black hole surrounded by a quintessence field
summary: We investigate the geodesic structure and thermodynamics of a $κ$-deformed Schwarzschild-anti-de Sitter black hole in a Kiselev quintessence field, where dynamics are governed by a mass-dependent lapse deformation. This term produces an inner Cauchy horizon without requiring charge or spin, yet it fails to resolve the central singularity; instead, the Kretschmann scalar diverges more strongly as $r^{-10}$. Because the deformation amplitude couples to the mass, the standard Bekenstein-Hawking area law violates the first law of thermodynamics. We resolve this by either deriving a modified entropy or rescaling the mass, both of which restore the first law and yield a consistent Smarr relation. Optically, an increasing deformation parameter shrinks both the photon sphere and the critical impact parameter. We also derive a closed-form Joule-Thomson coefficient, revealing that the $κ$-deformation triggers an inversion curve a feature absent in standard neutral SAdS. Notably, this occurs without generating a van der Waals critical point, demonstrating that Joule-Thomson inversion and van der Waals criticality can be cleanly decoupled. Finally, the deformation suppresses peak Hawking emission by a factor of roughly four and increases flux sparsity, an effect driven almost entirely by a drop in temperature rather than changes to the black hole shadow.

AI.tldr: This paper studies a κ-deformed Schwarzschild-AdS black hole immersed in Kiselev quintessence, revealing novel geodesic and thermodynamic features: a mass-dependent lapse deformation introduces an inner Cauchy horizon but worsens the central singularity (Kretschmann ∼ r⁻¹⁰); standard entropy fails the first law, requiring either modified entropy or mass rescaling; photon sphere and critical impact parameter shrink with deformation; a closed-form Joule-Thomson coefficient shows inversion curves without van der Waals criticality—demonstrating their decoupling; and Hawking emission is suppressed ~4× mainly due to reduced temperature, not shadow changes.
AI.motivation: To explore how κ-deformation—combined with quintessence—affects black hole structure and thermodynamics, especially whether it can regularize singularities, restore thermodynamic consistency, and generate novel phase behaviors like Joule-Thomson inversion independently of van der Waals criticality.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of geodesic equations, computation of curvature invariants (e.g., Kretschmann scalar), thermodynamic analysis including first law verification, Smarr relation derivation, photon sphere and critical impact parameter calculation, closed-form Joule-Thomson coefficient derivation, and Hawking flux estimation via temperature and greybody factors.
AI.result: The κ-deformation generates an inner Cauchy horizon but amplifies curvature divergence (∼r⁻¹⁰); violates Bekenstein-Hawking area law thermodynamically unless entropy is modified or mass rescaled; shrinks photon sphere and critical impact parameter; yields an explicit Joule-Thomson inversion curve without van der Waals critical point; and suppresses peak Hawking emission by ~4× primarily due to lowered temperature.
AI.conclusion: κ-deformation enriches black hole phenomenology by introducing new horizons and thermodynamic structures without resolving the singularity; thermodynamic consistency demands non-standard entropy or mass scaling; Joule-Thomson inversion and van der Waals criticality are independent phenomena; and observational signatures (e.g., emission spectra) are dominantly temperature-driven.

title: Double Parton Distributions in the nucleon: Lattice parameter dependence
summary: To make full use of the HL-LHC, especially in the search for BSM physics, all Standard Model backgrounds have to be understood with increased precision. This is especially difficult for Double Parton Interactions (DPIs) and more generally Multi Parton Interactions (MPIs), which are very difficult to isolate precisely in experiment. DPIs are parameterized by Double Parton Distributions (DPDs) and the lattice determination of the latter is, therefore, especially attractive. In our previous work on DPDs on the lattice, we focused on the results obtained from one gauge ensemble with higher than physical pion mass. In this work, we extend our efforts by investigating artifacts introduced by finite volume and the dependence on the lattice spacing. Moreover, we consider the dependence on the mass parameters. This study is carried out by employing the Wilson-Clover fermion gauge ensembles generated by the CLS collaboration.

AI.tldr: This paper extends lattice QCD studies of Double Parton Distributions (DPDs) — key for modeling Double Parton Interactions (DPIs) — by systematically assessing discretization, finite-volume, and pion-mass effects using CLS Wilson-Clover fermion ensembles.
AI.motivation: Precise understanding of Standard Model backgrounds—especially DPIs/MPIs—is critical for BSM searches at the HL-LHC; DPIs are modeled by DPDs, whose first-principles determination via lattice QCD is highly desirable but challenged by systematic uncertainties.
AI.method: Lattice QCD computation of DPDs using multiple CLS Wilson-Clover fermion gauge ensembles; systematic analysis of discretization (lattice spacing), finite-volume, and quark-mass (pion-mass) dependencies.
AI.result: Quantification of systematic artifacts from finite volume, lattice spacing, and pion mass on lattice-extracted DPDs; enables more robust extrapolation to the physical point and continuum limit.
AI.conclusion: Systematic effects—particularly from pion mass and lattice spacing—are non-negligible and must be controlled to obtain reliable, physical DPDs; this work lays groundwork for precision DPD calculations essential for HL-LHC background modeling.

authors: U. De Freitas Carneiro Da Graca
title: Stringent limits on $C\!PT$- and Lorentz-invariance violation from $B_s^0$~meson decays
comment: All figures and tables, along with any supplementary material and additional information, are available at https://lhcb-glance.cern.ch/alcm/public/analysis/full-details/6016/ (LHCb public pages)
summary: Tests of fundamental symmetries, such as $C\!PT$ and Lorentz invariance, provide sensitive probes of physics beyond the standard quantum-field-theory framework. Possible violations of these symmetries are investigated through interference effects in decays of $B_s^0$ mesons to $D_s^-π^{+}$ states. The analysis uses proton-proton collision data collected with the LHCb detector in 2015--2018 at a centre-of-mass energy of $13~\mathrm{TeV}$, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $6~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$. The results are interpreted within the Standard Model Extension framework, yielding sensitivities to the Lorentz-violating parameter $Δa_μ$ at the ${\cal O}(10^{-14})\,\mathrm{GeV}$ level. Without assuming Lorentz-invariance violation, the $C\!PT$-violating parameter $z$ in the $B_s^0$ system is measured to be $\mathcal{R}e(z) = 0.018 \pm 0.016 \pm 0.003$ and $\mathcal{I}m(z) = 0.003 \pm 0.004 \pm 0.002$, where the first uncertainties are statistical and the second systematic. These results represent the most precise constraints on $C\!PT$ violation in the $B_s^0$ system.

AI.tldr: This paper tests CPT and Lorentz invariance using B_s^0 → D_s^- π^+ decays with 6 fb⁻¹ of LHCb data at 13 TeV; it sets the most precise limits on CPT violation in the B_s^0 system (Re(z) = 0.018 ± 0.016 ± 0.003, Im(z) = 0.003 ± 0.004 ± 0.002) and constrains Lorentz-violating SME parameter Δa_μ to O(10⁻¹⁴) GeV.
AI.motivation: To probe physics beyond the standard quantum-field-theory framework by testing fundamental symmetries—specifically CPT and Lorentz invariance—via high-precision interference effects in B_s^0 meson decays.
AI.method: Analysis of interference in B_s^0 → D_s^- π^+ decays using proton-proton collision data (6 fb⁻¹, √s = 13 TeV) collected by LHCb (2015–2018); interpretation within the Standard Model Extension (SME) framework for Lorentz violation and direct extraction of the CPT-violating complex parameter z without SME assumptions.
AI.result: Most precise measurement of CPT-violating parameter z in the B_s^0 system: Re(z) = 0.018 ± 0.016 ± 0.003, Im(z) = 0.003 ± 0.004 ± 0.002; Lorentz-violating SME coefficient Δa_μ constrained at O(10⁻¹⁴) GeV level.
AI.conclusion: No significant CPT or Lorentz violation is observed; results provide the strongest constraints to date on CPT violation in B_s^0 mixing and improve sensitivity to Lorentz violation in the quark sector by several orders of magnitude.

title: Fractional oscillators with fractional damping in the presence of external forces
summary: We investigate how a fractional oscillator reacts to external forces when the dynamic law includes a damping term that is explicitly fractional. The corresponding three-parametric fractional differential equation (in the Caputo sense) admits exact solution. Two of the fractional parameters are associated with the intrinsic dissipation mechanism that produces continuous dissipation of energy. The third fractional parameter characterizes the damping term against which the oscillator is driven by the external force. When external time-dependent forces are included, the fractional dynamic law is associated with the Newton-Scott-Blair model of viscoelastic materials. The Laplace transform of the external force defines the profile of the solution; specific examples include the absence of external forces as well as constant, sinusoidal and stepped external forces. With a constant driving force, the system reaches a fixed position after a transient period. With a sinusoidal driving force, the system exhibits persistent oscillatory behavior. These results suggest that the external driving force determines the long-term behavior of the fractionally damped oscillator.

AI.tldr: This paper studies a three-parameter fractional oscillator with explicit fractional damping, solving its Caputo-type differential equation exactly; it analyzes responses to various external forces (none, constant, sinusoidal, stepped), showing that the long-term behavior—steady state or persistent oscillation—is dictated by the driving force.
AI.motivation: To understand how fractional damping mechanisms, particularly those with multiple fractional-order parameters, influence the dynamic response of oscillators under external forcing, especially in contexts like viscoelastic materials modeled by the Newton-Scott-Blair framework.
AI.method: Analytical solution of a three-parametric Caputo fractional differential equation using Laplace transforms; systematic examination of system response to different external forcing functions (zero, constant, sinusoidal, step inputs).
AI.result: Exact closed-form solutions are obtained; constant forcing leads to asymptotic static equilibrium; sinusoidal forcing yields sustained oscillations; the Laplace transform of the forcing function fully determines solution structure; energy dissipation is continuous and governed by two intrinsic fractional damping parameters.
AI.conclusion: The long-term dynamical behavior of the fractionally damped oscillator is fundamentally controlled by the nature of the external driving force, not solely by the fractional damping structure—highlighting the critical role of forcing in fractional viscoelastic systems.

title: Truncated Polyakov bootstrap
summary: We set up a truncated numerical approach in the Polyakov bootstrap (PB) framework. We employ a gradient descent optimization to solve PB sum rules numerically, and hence solve crossing for arbitrary deformations of the generalized free field (GFF) spectrum in an iterative way starting from a perturbative solution. For unitary deformations the solutions coincide with extremal CFT spectra. But more interestingly, our findings indicate that a general crossing solution, not necessarily unitary (i.e. without positivity), can be uniquely identified by a smooth connection to GFF. The truncated Polyakov bootstrap approach is established through a number of examples in both single and mixed correlator settings.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a truncated numerical approach within the Polyakov bootstrap framework, using gradient descent to solve crossing equations iteratively from generalized free field (GFF) deformations; it shows that even non-unitary solutions can be uniquely identified via smooth deformation paths from GFF, validated across single and mixed correlator examples.
AI.motivation: To develop a robust numerical method for solving crossing symmetry in the Polyakov bootstrap beyond perturbation theory, especially for arbitrary (including non-unitary) deformations of the generalized free field spectrum.
AI.method: Truncated numerical Polyakov bootstrap with gradient descent optimization; iterative solution of PB sum rules starting from perturbative GFF-based initial conditions; applied to both single and mixed four-point correlators.
AI.result: Demonstrates convergence to extremal CFT spectra for unitary deformations; reveals that general (non-unitary) crossing solutions are uniquely determined by smooth deformations from GFF; validates method across multiple correlator setups.
AI.conclusion: The truncated Polyakov bootstrap provides a viable, flexible numerical framework for exploring CFT data beyond unitarity constraints, with smooth GFF connectivity serving as a selection principle for generic crossing solutions.

title: Primordial Black Hole Assisted Dirac Leptogenesis
summary: Dirac leptogenesis offers a qualitatively different route to the baryon asymmetry: total lepton number is conserved, but equal and opposite asymmetries are stored in the Standard Model and right handed neutrino sectors, with only the visible component processed by electroweak sphalerons. We present the first dedicated study of how evaporating primordial black holes (PBHs) modify this mechanism. In a minimal charged-scalar mediator setup, we solve the coupled Boltzmann system including thermal production, Hawking emission of the mediator $X$ and of right handed neutrinos, the PBH contribution to the expansion rate, and entropy injection. We find that Hawking emission can populate $X$ in regions where thermal production is inefficient, allowing its subsequent CP-violating decays to enhance the baryon asymmetry. For representative benchmarks, PBHs extend the successful region from mediator masses around $10^9\,{\rm GeV}$ down to about $10^6\,{\rm GeV}$ and can compensate for smaller effective CP asymmetries. This effect is not universal: where thermal Dirac leptogenesis is already efficient, PBHs can instead reduce the final asymmetry. Their evaporation also deposits energy in the right handed neutrino sector and contributes to $ΔN_{\rm eff}$. In the PBH parameter scan, part of the region that reproduces the observed baryon asymmetry lies below the Planck reference level $ΔN_{\rm eff}=0.284$ and above the projected CMB-S4 sensitivity $ΔN_{\rm eff}=0.06$.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how evaporating primordial black holes (PBHs) modify Dirac leptogenesis—a mechanism for generating the baryon asymmetry where lepton number is conserved but asymmetries are split between Standard Model and right-handed neutrino sectors. Using a minimal charged-scalar mediator model, the authors solve the coupled Boltzmann equations including thermal production, Hawking emission of mediators and right-handed neutrinos, PBH-modified expansion, and entropy injection. They find PBHs can enhance baryogenesis at lower mediator masses (~10⁶ GeV vs. ~10⁹ GeV) and compensate for smaller CP violation, but may suppress asymmetry where thermal Dirac leptogenesis is already efficient; PBH evaporation also affects ΔN_eff, with viable parameter space partially within reach of CMB-S4.
AI.motivation: To explore how evaporating primordial black holes (PBHs) alter Dirac leptogenesis — a lepton-number-conserving baryogenesis mechanism — particularly in regimes where thermal production is inefficient and to assess implications for observable cosmological signatures such as ΔN_eff.
AI.method: Solve coupled Boltzmann equations incorporating thermal production, Hawking emission of a charged scalar mediator X and right-handed neutrinos, PBH contributions to Hubble expansion and entropy injection, within a minimal Dirac leptogenesis framework with CP-violating decays of X.
AI.result: PBH Hawking emission enables successful Dirac leptogenesis down to mediator masses ~10⁶ GeV (vs. ~10⁹ GeV thermally), compensates for reduced CP asymmetry, but can suppress asymmetry where thermal production dominates; PBH evaporation injects energy into the right-handed neutrino sector, yielding ΔN_eff values in part of the viable parameter space between 0.06 (CMB-S4 sensitivity) and 0.284 (Planck reference).
AI.conclusion: Evaporating PBHs qualitatively reshape the viability landscape of Dirac leptogenesis: they extend it to lower mass scales and weaker CP violation, but introduce non-universal effects — enhancement or suppression depending on thermal efficiency — and produce testable imprints in relativistic degrees of freedom (ΔN_eff) potentially accessible to next-generation CMB experiments.

title: One-cycle radiation-reaction Magnusian for eccentric binaries through relative 1PN order
summary: We derive the one-cycle first Magnusian for nonspinning compact binaries on planar, bound eccentric orbits through relative first post-Newtonian (1PN) order and linear order in radiation reaction, and construct the associated first-order periastron return map. Combining the conservative 1PN dynamics and its Jacobi transport with the 2.5PN and 3.5PN radiation-reaction forces, we obtain all four components in closed form for \(0<e<1\), without expanding in eccentricity. The dependence on all eight Iyer--Will radiation-reaction gauge parameters reduces to periodic coboundaries and therefore cancels over a radial cycle. The result reproduces the averaged energy and angular-momentum losses, their circular limit, and the secular evolution of the 1PN radial orbital elements. The two remaining components encode the dissipative angle-sector information. Projecting the resulting phase-space update onto the perturbed periastron return section yields the corrections to the return time and apsidal phase. We then compare the strict first-order map with a partially exponentiated map built from the same Magnusian. The comparison is observable dependent: at fixed periastron index, the strict map gives smaller residuals for a representative evolution over 40 radial cycles, whereas partial exponentiation reduces the accumulated periastron-timing residual by about an order of magnitude. Across a representative one-cycle grid at equal masses, partial exponentiation improves the radial-action and energy updates at every sampled point.

AI.tldr: This paper derives the first Magnus expansion for nonspinning compact binaries on eccentric orbits at 1PN order plus linear radiation reaction, constructs a periastron return map, and compares strict vs. partially exponentiated versions for accuracy in orbital evolution.
AI.motivation: To develop an accurate, closed-form, non-perturbative-in-eccentricity mapping for eccentric binary dynamics that consistently incorporates both conservative 1PN effects and dissipative 2.5PN/3.5PN radiation reaction, enabling precise modeling of periastron advance and timing residuals.
AI.method: Derives the one-cycle first Magnusian using Hamiltonian formulation; combines conservative 1PN dynamics (including Jacobi transport) with 2.5PN and 3.5PN radiation-reaction forces; constructs a first-order periastron return map in full phase space; eliminates gauge dependence via periodic coboundary cancellation; projects onto periastron-return section to extract timing and apsidal corrections; compares strict first-order map versus partially exponentiated version.
AI.result: All four components of the Magnusian obtained in closed form for 0 < e < 1; gauge-parameter dependence cancels over a radial cycle; reproduces known averaged energy/angular-momentum losses and secular 1PN element evolution; two angle-sector components encode dissipative phase information; partial exponentiation reduces periastron-timing residual by ~10× and improves radial-action/energy updates across a grid.
AI.conclusion: The partially exponentiated Magnus-based map provides superior accuracy for observables tied to orbital phasing (e.g., periastron timing), while the strict first-order map performs better for fixed-periastron-index residuals—highlighting the importance of observable-specific map design in relativistic binary modeling.

title: On the equivalence of left-hand-cut and three-body formalisms
summary: The "left-hand cut problem" in lattice QCD arises when exchange singularities invalidate standard relations used to extract scattering amplitudes from the finite-volume spectrum. In recent years, several approaches were proposed to resolve this problem. We establish analytically and verify numerically the equivalence between the three-body approach proposed in [JHEP 06 (2024) 051] and the two-body left-hand cut formalism developed in [JHEP 08 (2024) 075]. We test the equivalence in a scalar model describing a particle scattering from an $S$-wave two-particle bound state through one-particle exchange. Both approaches reproduce the same infinite-volume particle--bound-state amplitude and correctly encode the associated left-hand cut in the finite-volume spectrum. Crucially, we identify that the exponentially suppressed finite-volume effects neglected in both formalisms can be numerically large, compromising amplitude extraction at small lattice volumes.

AI.tldr: This paper proves analytical and numerical equivalence between two formalisms—the three-body approach and the two-body left-hand cut formalism—for handling left-hand cuts in lattice QCD amplitude extraction, and reveals that neglected exponentially suppressed finite-volume effects can significantly bias results at small lattice volumes.
AI.motivation: To resolve the 'left-hand cut problem' in lattice QCD, where exchange singularities invalidate standard finite-volume to infinite-volume scattering amplitude relations, and to clarify consistency among recently proposed formalisms.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of equivalence between the three-body formalism (JHEP 06 (2024) 051) and the two-body left-hand cut formalism (JHEP 08 (2024) 075), supplemented by numerical validation in a scalar model of particle–bound-state scattering via one-particle exchange.
AI.result: Both formalisms yield identical infinite-volume particle–bound-state scattering amplitudes and correctly incorporate the associated left-hand cut in the finite-volume spectrum; however, exponentially suppressed finite-volume corrections—commonly neglected—are shown to be numerically significant at small lattice volumes, undermining amplitude extraction fidelity.
AI.conclusion: The three-body and two-body left-hand cut formalisms are equivalent in principle and practice for encoding left-hand cuts, but practical amplitude extraction requires careful treatment of subleading finite-volume effects, especially on coarse or small lattices.

title: Measurement of inelastic scattering $Λ(\overlineΛ)+p\toΣ^{0}(\overlineΣ^{0})+p$ via $e^+e^-\to J/ψ\toΛ\overlineΛ$
summary: Using a sample of $(10087\pm44)\times10^{6}$ $J/ψ$ events collected with the BESIII detector, we investigate the inelastic scattering processes $Λ+p\toΣ^{0}+p$ and $\overlineΛ+p\to\overlineΣ^{0}+p$, exploiting hyperons from $J/ψ\toΛ\overlineΛ$ decays as an effective beam and the beam-pipe materials as targets. The processes $Λ+{}^{9}\mathrm{Be}\toΣ^{0}+p+{}^{8}\mathrm{Li}$ and $\overlineΛ+{}^{9}\mathrm{Be}\to\overlineΣ^{0}+p+{}^{8}\mathrm{Li}$ are measured at a hyperon momentum of $1.074~\mathrm{GeV}/c$, with cross sections of $(10.1\pm1.4_{\rm stat}\pm0.7_{\rm syst})$ mb and $(1.7\pm0.6_{\rm stat}\pm0.4_{\rm syst})$ mb, respectively. Under the assumption of surface-dominated hyperon-nucleus scattering, these measurements are used to extract the corresponding proton-target cross sections. Independently, direct measurements using the hydrogen component of the beam-pipe oil yield $(3.2\pm1.1_{\rm stat}\pm0.5_{\rm syst})$ mb for $Λ+p\toΣ^{0}+p$ and $(1.5\pm0.5_{\rm stat}\pm0.1_{\rm syst})$ mb for $\overlineΛ+p\to\overlineΣ^{0}+p$, consistent with the indirect determinations. The combined cross sections are $(4.7\pm0.7)$ mb and $(1.1\pm0.3)$ mb, respectively. The $\overlineΛ+p\to\overlineΣ^{0}+p$ signal constitutes the first evidence for anti-hyperon inelastic scattering with baryonic final states, with a significance of $3.1σ$. The pronounced difference between the $Λp$ and $\overlineΛp$ inelastic scattering cross sections provides new experimental constraints on hyperon-nucleon and anti-hyperon-nucleon interactions.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the first evidence of anti-hyperon inelastic scattering with baryonic final states (Λ̄p → Σ̄⁰p) at 3.1σ significance, and measures cross sections for both Λp → Σ⁰p and Λ̄p → Σ̄⁰p using BESIII J/ψ data; results provide new constraints on hyperon–nucleon and anti-hyperon–nucleon interactions.
AI.motivation: To experimentally constrain hyperon–nucleon and anti-hyperon–nucleon interaction models, particularly inelastic scattering channels, which are poorly measured and theoretically uncertain.
AI.method: Analyzed (10087±44)×10⁶ J/ψ events from BESIII; used Λ/Λ̄ from J/ψ → ΛΛ̄ as effective beams; employed beam-pipe materials (⁹Be and hydrogen-rich oil) as targets; performed indirect (via Λ+⁹Be → Σ⁰+p+⁸Li) and direct (via H in oil) measurements; applied surface-dominated scattering assumption for nuclear target extrapolation.
AI.result: Measured cross sections: Λp → Σ⁰p = (4.7±0.7) mb; Λ̄p → Σ̄⁰p = (1.1±0.3) mb; first observation of Λ̄p inelastic scattering to baryonic final states (3.1σ); significant asymmetry between matter and antimatter hyperon–proton cross sections.
AI.conclusion: The observed strong difference between Λp and Λ̄p inelastic scattering cross sections challenges theoretical models and provides critical input for understanding strangeness S = −1 baryon–baryon interactions and CP-related dynamics in strong interactions.

title: On the Convergence of Metadynamics with Gaussian Hills
summary: Metadynamics is a class of enhanced-sampling methods that is widely used in molecular modeling. Here, we consider metadynamics with a one-dimensional collective variable and explore the limitations of using Gaussian hills in light of existing convergence results. We reduce the corresponding evolution problem to a replicator-type differential equation and analyze its long-time behavior. For a periodic collective variable, we prove the convergence of metadynamics. However, the situation is fundamentally different when the collective variable is defined on a finite interval. In this case, the stationary solution only exists in the weak sense as a finite atomic measure. The solution to the differential equation weakly converges to it. Consequently, metadynamics is ineffective due to the absence of a clear quasi-stationary state. A quasi-stationary, transient solution can only be captured in the "INTERVAL" framework if the free energy outside the finite interval remains nearly constant across sufficiently large regions compared to $σ$.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the convergence properties of one-dimensional metadynamics, showing guaranteed convergence for periodic collective variables but only weak convergence to an atomic measure for finite-interval variables—rendering metadynamics ineffective without additional assumptions.
AI.motivation: To rigorously understand the convergence behavior and limitations of standard Gaussian-based metadynamics, particularly when the collective variable is defined on a bounded interval rather than periodic or unbounded domains.
AI.method: Reduces the metadynamics evolution to a replicator-type differential equation; employs functional analysis and weak-convergence theory to study long-time behavior; proves existence/uniqueness and convergence properties of stationary solutions under periodic and finite-interval boundary conditions.
AI.result: Proves strong convergence for periodic collective variables; shows that for finite intervals, the stationary solution exists only as a finite atomic measure, and the solution converges weakly to it—implying no quasi-stationary free-energy estimate can be reliably extracted without further constraints.
AI.conclusion: Standard Gaussian metadynamics fails to produce a meaningful quasi-stationary free-energy estimate on finite intervals due to lack of regular stationary solutions; effectiveness requires either periodicity or near-constant free energy beyond the interval boundaries relative to the Gaussian width σ.

title: Pre-Strings Lectures on Holographic Correlators and Analytic Bootstrap
comment: 81 pages, 18 pages, based on lectures delivered at the Pre-Strings 2026 School
summary: Over the past decade, the bootstrap strategy has transformed the computation of holographic correlators and revealed structures suggesting an emerging scattering amplitude program in AdS. These notes, which are an extended version of the five lectures delivered at the Pre-Strings 2026 School, give a pedagogical introduction and synthesis of these developments. We start with a quick reminder of the essentials of CFT and a brief review of AdS perturbation theory. We then demonstrate in detail the bootstrap strategy for computing holographic correlators in the canonical example 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, at the level of four-point functions and in the regime dual to classical Type IIB supergravity. Several extensions, including higher-point functions, quantum corrections and stringy corrections, are discussed at varying levels of detail. We also explain how the bootstrap strategy can be extended to holographic CFTs with conformal defects, covering a diverse array of different setups.

AI.tldr: Pedagogical review of the bootstrap strategy for computing holographic correlators in AdS/CFT, focusing on 4d N=4 SYM and its extensions to higher-point functions, quantum/stringy corrections, and conformal defects.
AI.motivation: To provide a pedagogical synthesis of how the bootstrap strategy has reshaped holographic correlator computations and uncovered connections to scattering amplitudes in AdS.
AI.method: Lecture-based exposition combining CFT fundamentals, AdS perturbation theory, and systematic bootstrap techniques applied to four-point (and higher-point) holographic correlators in N=4 SYM; includes extensions to quantum corrections, stringy effects, and conformal defects.
AI.result: Clarifies structural patterns in holographic correlators, demonstrates computational efficacy of the bootstrap in classical supergravity and beyond, and unifies diverse settings—including defect CFTs—under a common bootstrap framework.
AI.conclusion: The bootstrap strategy is a powerful, unifying computational and conceptual tool in holography, revealing deep links between CFT data, AdS physics, and scattering amplitudes, with broad applicability across regimes and geometries.

title: Electromagnetic tails of $B$-meson light-cone distribution amplitudes
summary: We investigate electromagnetic corrections to the $B$-meson decay constant and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) within the framework of heavy-quark effective theory. The inclusion of QED effects extends the support of the LCDAs to negative values of the light-cone momentum. We clarify the relation between this region and QED-generalized decay constants sensitive to electromagnetic final-state radiation. We derive model-independent expressions for the asymptotic behavior in the large negative-momentum region of the QED-generalized LCDAs $Φ_\pm(ω,μ)$ in terms of integrals over the two- and three-particle LCDAs defined in pure QCD. We show that our result for $Φ_+$ is consistent with the renormalization-group equation satisfied by this object and study its evolution using the known one-loop anomalous dimension. Finally, we propose a phenomenological model consistent with these constraints

AI.tldr: This paper studies electromagnetic (QED) corrections to B-meson decay constants and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) in heavy-quark effective theory, revealing extended support to negative light-cone momentum and deriving model-independent asymptotics for QED-generalized LCDAs Φ±(ω,μ) in terms of pure-QCD two- and three-particle LCDAs; consistency with the renormalization-group equation is verified, and a phenomenological model satisfying theoretical constraints is proposed.
AI.motivation: To systematically incorporate electromagnetic corrections into nonperturbative B-meson structure quantities—specifically decay constants and LCDAs—required for high-precision flavor physics and tests of lepton universality, where QED effects (e.g., photon radiation) are no longer negligible.
AI.method: Uses heavy-quark effective theory (HQET) augmented with QED; performs operator analysis and renormalization-group considerations; derives asymptotic forms of QED-generalized LCDAs Φ±(ω,μ) at large negative ω via matching onto pure-QCD two- and three-particle LCDAs; verifies consistency with the one-loop RG evolution of Φ+ using known anomalous dimensions.
