AI.result: QED corrections extend LCDAs to negative light-cone momentum; asymptotic behavior of Φ±(ω,μ) for ω → −∞ is expressed as convergent integrals over standard QCD LCDAs; Φ+ satisfies its one-loop RG equation; evolution under scale μ is quantified; a minimal phenomenological model for Φ± is constructed respecting all derived constraints.
AI.conclusion: Electromagnetic corrections induce qualitatively new features in B-meson LCDAs—namely support on negative momentum—and are rigorously constrained by HQET+QED symmetry and RG consistency; this enables robust inclusion of QED effects in precision extractions of |Vub|, form factors, and rare decay observables.

title: How Much Geometry Does Horizon Entropy Determine? A Discourse on Entropy, Gravity, and Observable Quantities
summary: Building on Jacobson's thermodynamics derivation of Einstein field equations, the "generalized entropy and varying-G" (GEVAG) framework was proposed to consistently incorporate generalized horizon entropy $S=f(A)/4G$ into both the thermodynamics and the geometry of spacetime. This leads to an effective gravitational coupling $G_\text{eff}=G/f'(A)$. A related "entropy-gravity correspondence" (EGC) instead is equivalent to promoting this horizon relation to a radially varying bulk coupling $G_\text{eff}(r)$. We clarify the similarities and fundamental distinctions between these approaches. Although they share the same horizon consistency relation, their global causal structures and asymptotic geometries can differ substantially. In addition, the radial prescription of EGC introduces an additional ambiguity for multi-center configurations. We further examine a near-horizon extension of GEVAG, which restores the equivalence between thermodynamic and ADM masses that is absent in the horizon-only formulation. We then discuss the implications of these different prescriptions for the Bekenstein bound. The Bekenstein bound provides a surprising link between $G_\text{eff}$ in near horizon GEVAG, EGC, and the one obtained in the recent $f(R)$-reconstruction approach of generalized entropy geometry via Wald entropy. Finally, we raise the most important question: what exactly is the $G$ measured in laboratories?

AI.tldr: This paper compares two frameworks—GEVAG and EGC—that generalize gravitational coupling $G$ via horizon entropy $S = f(A)/4G$, clarifying their conceptual differences, causal/ asymptotic implications, ambiguities in multi-center setups, and connections to the Bekenstein bound and $f(R)$ gravity via Wald entropy; it ends by questioning the physical meaning of laboratory-measured $G$.
AI.motivation: To resolve conceptual ambiguities between GEVAG (a horizon-restricted thermodynamic-geometric framework with effective coupling $G_\text{eff} = G/f'(A)$) and EGC (a radially extended prescription $G_\text{eff}(r)$), and to assess their physical consistency—especially regarding mass definitions, causal structure, multi-center configurations, and the Bekenstein bound.
AI.method: Conceptual and analytical comparison of GEVAG and EGC frameworks; derivation of near-horizon GEVAG extension restoring thermodynamic–ADM mass equivalence; analysis of asymptotic geometry and global causal structure; examination of multi-center ambiguity in EGC; comparison of effective $G_\text{eff}$ across GEVAG, EGC, and $f(R)$-reconstruction using Wald entropy; critical assessment of operational meaning of $G$ in local experiments.
AI.result: GEVAG and EGC agree at the horizon but diverge globally in causal structure and asymptotics; EGC suffers radial ambiguity in multi-center systems; near-horizon GEVAG restores mass equivalence; all three approaches (near-horizon GEVAG, EGC, $f(R)$+Wald) yield identical $G_\text{eff}$ satisfying the Bekenstein bound; the laboratory $G$ remains operationally undefined within these generalized entropy frameworks.
AI.conclusion: The choice between GEVAG and EGC is not merely technical but reflects distinct physical assumptions about where and how entropy–gravity correspondence manifests. Their inequivalence beyond the horizon underscores the need for a deeper principle—possibly tied to locality, observability, or UV completion—to fix $G_\text{eff}(r)$. The paper concludes that current frameworks do not uniquely determine what $G$ is measured locally, exposing a foundational gap in linking generalized entropy to empirical gravity.

authors: M. G. D. van der Grinten
title: Search for dark matter particle interactions in an extended nuclear recoil energy window with the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment
comment: 25 pages including supplemental, 13 figures including supplemental. Data release at https://doi.org/10.17182/hepdata.182472.v1
summary: We report on a search for dark matter particles interacting with xenon nuclei in an exposure of 2.84 tonne-years with the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment. An extended nuclear recoil energy window up to approximately 270 keV enables searches for effective field theory and inelastic models of dark matter where high-energy recoils account for a larger fraction of the predicted recoil spectrum compared to the nominal spin independent interaction. We observe one event with characteristics consistent with a nuclear recoil of $248\pm23\,\mathrm{(stat)}\pm23\,\mathrm{(sys)}$ keV, in a region where the known background expectation is low. A profile likelihood ratio test finds tension with the background-only hypothesis at a global significance of 2.6$σ$ when accounting for look-elsewhere effects, with a maximum local significance of 3.4$σ$ across the models tested. We describe the analysis and event of interest, the background model used in the statistical inference, and detail several of the rare background topologies considered.

AI.tldr: LZ experiment reports one nuclear recoil event at ~248 keV in 2.84 tonne-years exposure; tension with background-only hypothesis at 2.6σ global (3.4σ local), constraining EFT and inelastic dark matter models.
AI.motivation: To probe non-standard dark matter interactions—particularly effective field theory (EFT) and inelastic scattering models—that predict enhanced high-energy nuclear recoils beyond conventional spin-independent WIMP searches.
AI.method: Blind analysis of 2.84 tonne-years exposure from the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) liquid xenon time-projection chamber, using an extended nuclear recoil energy window up to ~270 keV; background modeling incorporating rare topologies; statistical inference via profile likelihood ratio test with look-elsewhere correction.
AI.result: One candidate nuclear recoil event observed at 248 ± 23 (stat) ± 23 (sys) keV; background expectation in that region is low; global significance against background-only is 2.6σ, local maximum 3.4σ across tested DM models.
AI.conclusion: No conclusive evidence for dark matter detection; the observed event is statistically intriguing but consistent with a background fluctuation; results set new constraints on EFT and inelastic DM parameter spaces.

title: Superintegrability of stratified symplectic spaces
summary: We define the notion of superintegrability of a Hamiltonian system on a stratified symplectic space. We focus on spin Calogero-Moser-Sutherland (sCMS) systems, where the phase space is a stratified symplectic space obtained by the Hamiltonian reduction of the cotangent bundle over a compact Lie group, and demonstrate that the sCMS systems for $SU(3)$ are superintegrable.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces superintegrability on stratified symplectic spaces and proves it for spin Calogero-Moser-Sutherland systems associated with SU(3) via Hamiltonian reduction.
AI.motivation: To extend the concept of superintegrability to singular phase spaces—specifically, stratified symplectic spaces arising from Hamiltonian reduction—and to verify it for physically relevant sCMS systems.
AI.method: Definition of superintegrability on stratified symplectic spaces; explicit construction and analysis of sCMS systems via Hamiltonian reduction of T*G (G = compact Lie group); case study for SU(3) using symmetry, Poisson structure, and counting of independent, globally defined, Poisson-commuting integrals of motion.
AI.result: The sCMS system for SU(3) is shown to be superintegrable on its stratified symplectic phase space, with more independent, globally defined, Poisson-commuting integrals than degrees of freedom.
AI.conclusion: Superintegrability is well-defined and verifiable on singular (stratified) symplectic manifolds, and the SU(3) sCMS system provides a concrete, nontrivial example, enriching both integrable systems theory and singular symplectic geometry.

title: Unfolded Krylov complexity: universal chaotic dynamics without false positives
summary: A central challenge in diagnosing quantum chaos is to distinguish genuine many-body scrambling from kinematic effects of the spectrum. Krylov state complexity, or spread complexity, has emerged as a powerful diagnostic, with its characteristic growth, peak, and relaxation often taken as signatures of chaos. However, previous work has shown that this criterion can give false positives: saddle-dominated integrable systems may display prominent peaks even without random-matrix level correlations. We argue, based on complementary numerical and analytical evidence, that this ambiguity can be resolved by unfolding the spectrum prior to constructing the ensuing Krylov dynamics. By removing the non-universal smooth density of states while retaining microscopic spectral correlations, unfolding suppresses spurious peaks in integrable systems while preserving the universal spectral signatures of chaotic systems. Analytically, the formulation of the Lanczos iteration in terms of orthogonal polynomials yields an exact complexity kernel with a robust near-diagonal structure whose fine-grained features reflect the underlying spectral correlations. Moreover, for the logarithmic model, unfolding can be performed exactly, mapping the spectrum to a uniform lattice and yielding an analytic spread complexity that removes the false-positive peak. These findings establish unfolded Krylov complexity as a more reliable probe of genuine many-body scrambling.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes spectrum unfolding before Krylov complexity computation to distinguish true many-body quantum chaos from spurious peaks in integrable systems, improving diagnostic reliability.
AI.motivation: To resolve false positives in Krylov (spread) complexity—where integrable, saddle-dominated systems mimic chaotic signatures (e.g., prominent peaks) despite lacking random-matrix spectral correlations.
AI.method: Introduces spectral unfolding prior to Krylov dynamics construction; leverages orthogonal polynomial formulation of Lanczos iteration to derive an exact complexity kernel; applies exact unfolding to the logarithmic model, mapping its spectrum to a uniform lattice.
AI.result: Unfolding suppresses non-universal, kinematic peaks in integrable systems while preserving universal chaotic signatures; yields analytic spread complexity for the logarithmic model with eliminated false-positive peak.
AI.conclusion: Unfolded Krylov complexity is a more robust and reliable diagnostic for genuine many-body quantum scrambling.

title: Tremaine-Gunn Control: Evading Bounds on Light Fermion Dark Matter
comment: 8 pages, 3 figures; 9 pages of Supplemental Material with 2 figures
summary: Pauli exclusion is often regarded as imposing a model-independent lower bound on the mass of fermionic dark matter in galaxies. We show that dark-sector interactions can substantially weaken this conclusion. In particular, eV-scale fermions can form bound structures with the characteristic sizes and densities of dwarf galaxies, thereby circumventing the conventional Tremaine-Gunn mass constraint. Within these objects, the degeneracy pressure is balanced by an attractive finite-range scalar Yukawa force that is significantly stronger than gravity. The interaction acts on dwarf-galaxy scales while remaining screened on larger scales. We derive the evolution of the resulting dark-matter fluid and identify a viable cosmological history in which structures first form gravitationally, with the new interaction becoming active only at late times. As a proof of concept, we construct a model in which a single late-time phase transition generates the required dynamics. These results provide a new route to exceptionally light fermionic dark matter and demonstrate that dark-sector interactions can qualitatively alter conventional phase-space limits.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that dark-sector interactions—specifically a late-onset, finite-range scalar Yukawa force—can allow eV-scale fermionic dark matter to form dwarf-galaxy–sized structures, evading the Tremaine-Gunn lower mass bound imposed by Pauli exclusion.
AI.motivation: To challenge the conventional assumption that Pauli exclusion imposes a model-independent lower bound (~100 eV) on fermionic dark matter mass in galaxies, by exploring how dark-sector interactions could relax phase-space constraints.
AI.method: Analytical and fluid-dynamical modeling of fermionic dark matter subject to an attractive, finite-range scalar Yukawa interaction; derivation of the coupled evolution equations for the dark-matter fluid; construction of a cosmological scenario with late-time activation of the interaction via a phase transition.
AI.result: eV-scale fermions can form stable, dwarf-galaxy–sized bound structures where degeneracy pressure is balanced by a strong, screened Yukawa force; such configurations are dynamically viable if the interaction activates only at late times after initial gravitational collapse.
AI.conclusion: Dark-sector interactions can qualitatively alter standard phase-space limits, enabling exceptionally light fermionic dark matter and invalidating the universality of the Tremaine-Gunn bound.

title: Exploring the construction of field equations for regular black holes with dynamical regularization scales
summary: The study of the dynamics of regular black holes is an emergent area of research. Recent works have discussed how to deform the Einstein field equations to regularize spherically symmetric black hole solutions due to the introduction of a new physics scale acting as regulator. In this exploratory paper, we consider for the first time the problem of constructing field equations in which the regularization scale is a dynamical field. Such field equations may provide an effective description of the evolution of the cores of regular black holes due to the backreaction of matter, and a novel avenue for constructing alternative dynamical solutions of theoretical and phenomenological interest. We discuss a general family of field equations describing spherically symmetric gravity coupled to a scalar field, and study whether the sector with a constant scalar field contains solutions describing static regular black holes with no additional physics scales aside from the ones provided by the scalar field. We show that this question can be reduced to solving a linear partial differential equation for the coupling functions between the scalar and the metric degrees of freedom.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a novel framework where the regularization scale for regular black holes is promoted to a dynamical scalar field, leading to modified field equations that may describe evolving black hole cores; it reduces the existence of static regular black hole solutions in this framework to solving a linear PDE for coupling functions.
AI.motivation: To develop an effective description of the dynamical evolution of regular black hole cores via backreaction of matter, by promoting the fixed regularization scale—previously introduced ad hoc—to a dynamical scalar field.
AI.method: Constructs a general family of spherically symmetric gravitational field equations coupled to a scalar field; analyzes the constant-scalar subsector to determine conditions under which static, regular black hole solutions emerge without extraneous physical scales; reduces the problem to solving a linear partial differential equation governing the coupling functions between the scalar field and curvature invariants.
AI.result: The existence of static regular black hole solutions within the constant-scalar sector is shown to be equivalent to solving a specific linear PDE for the coupling functions—providing a clear mathematical criterion for viability of the framework.
AI.conclusion: Promoting the regularization scale to a dynamical scalar field yields a consistent and flexible framework for modeling evolving regular black hole interiors; the linear PDE condition offers a tractable pathway for constructing phenomenologically viable models.

title: Effective Sub-Quantum Readout for Non-Monochromatic Axion Signals in High-$Q$ Haloscopes
summary: The search for wave-like dark matter using microwave cavity haloscopes is constrained by the Standard Quantum Limit, which dictates that phase-preserving linear amplification results in a minimum of one quantum of total system noise for a narrow-band signal. We demonstrate that this limit is effectively halved for a non-monochromatic axion signal coupled to a high-$Q$ cavity. By operating a Josephson Parametric Amplifier such that the cavity resonance is centered exactly at the half-pump frequency, the axion signal symmetrically populates both the signal and idler bands. Through quadrature analysis of the homodyne readout, we show that the incoherent sum of these mirrored spectral components doubles the measured signal power while the vacuum noise remains constant. This operation yields an effective noise limit of 0.5 quanta per frequency bin, translating to an overall effective limit of $1/\sqrt{2}$ quanta after optimal matched filtering.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a method to halve the Standard Quantum Limit in microwave cavity haloscopes for axion dark matter detection by using a Josephson Parametric Amplifier operated at half-pump frequency, enabling symmetric signal-idler band population and quadrature-based noise reduction.
AI.motivation: To overcome the Standard Quantum Limit (SQL) — a fundamental sensitivity barrier in phase-preserving linear amplification — for detecting non-monochromatic axion dark matter signals with microwave cavity haloscopes.
AI.method: Operating a Josephson Parametric Amplifier (JPA) such that the cavity resonance lies exactly at half the pump frequency, causing the axion signal to symmetrically populate both signal and idler sidebands; then performing quadrature-resolved homodyne readout to coherently combine the mirrored spectral components while keeping vacuum noise unchanged.
AI.result: Achieves an effective quantum noise floor of 0.5 quanta per frequency bin, and — after optimal matched filtering — an overall effective limit of $1/\sqrt{2}$ quanta, i.e., a 3 dB improvement over the SQL.
AI.conclusion: The Standard Quantum Limit is not absolute for non-monochromatic axion signals in parametrically amplified high-Q cavities; this technique enables enhanced sensitivity for axion haloscope experiments without requiring quantum nondemolition or squeezing beyond standard parametric operation.

title: Heat transfer problem of a dense gas described by the Enskog equation with a modification of the Enskog factor
comment: 8 pages,5 figures, 34th International Symposium on Rarefied Gas Dynamics
summary: Heat transfer in a dense gas between two parallel plates is studied for assessing the quantitative difference of two variants of the Enskog equation, i.e., the original Enskog equation and the Enskog equation with a modified Enskog factor recently proposed in Phys. Rev. E \textbf{111}, 065108 (2025). The main advantage of the latter is that the H theorem, which is lacking in the former, has been established. The influence of the modification is assessed by comparing the macroscopic quantities in details. It is found that the influence of this modification is quite limited in the density, temperature, and heat flow vector. However, the influence on the stress tensor is visible in some severe setting of parameters.

AI.tldr: This paper compares two variants of the Enskog equation—the original and a recently modified version with a proven H theorem—by analyzing heat transfer in dense gases between parallel plates; it finds minimal differences in density, temperature, and heat flux, but noticeable deviations in the stress tensor under extreme parameter conditions.
AI.motivation: To quantitatively assess the impact of a recently proposed modification to the Enskog equation that restores the H theorem—a property absent in the original Enskog equation—on macroscopic transport behavior in dense gases.
AI.method: Numerical or analytical solution of both Enskog variants for steady-state heat transfer between two parallel plates in a dense gas, followed by detailed comparison of macroscopic fields: density, temperature, heat flow vector, and stress tensor.
AI.result: The modification has negligible effect on density, temperature, and heat flow vector across examined conditions, but induces measurable changes in the stress tensor, particularly under severe (e.g., high density or large temperature gradient) parameter settings.
AI.conclusion: While the modified Enskog equation satisfies the H theorem and thus improves theoretical foundation, its practical impact on most macroscopic observables is small; however, the stress tensor remains sensitive, indicating non-negligible differences in momentum transport predictions.

title: Residues on Permanent Pinches: Finite Integrals and Leading Divergences
summary: We study infrared (IR) divergences from the point of view of permanent pinches. We show how canceling permanent pinches allows us to form finite linear combinations of integrals. We further show how to compute scheme-independent leading IR divergences with- out introducing a regulator, by integrating certain residue forms along desingularizations of permanent pinch varieties. Our methods work for massless and mixed massive-massless inte- grals, for non-planar integrals with arbitrary numerators as well as for integrals with higher (integer) powers of propagators. We use this analysis to determine leading singular terms in some examples of box integrals. We further study examples of finite integrals at higher loops, and in particular provide a basis for finite non-evanescent integrals in a non-planar two-loop five-point topology.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a geometric method—based on permanent pinches and desingularization of pinch varieties—to isolate and cancel infrared (IR) divergences in Feynman integrals without regulators, enabling scheme-independent computation of leading IR singularities and construction of finite integral bases.
AI.motivation: To resolve IR divergences in dimensional regularization-independent, geometrically rigorous ways—especially for non-planar, mixed-mass, and high-power propagator integrals where standard regulator-based methods obscure physical structure.
AI.method: Uses algebraic geometry: identifies permanent pinch varieties as loci of simultaneous vanishing of propagators and their derivatives; constructs desingularizations (e.g., blow-ups); integrates residue forms over these desingularized spaces to extract leading IR behavior; forms finite linear combinations via pinch cancellation.
AI.result: Derives regulator-free, scheme-independent formulas for leading IR divergences across broad classes (massless/mixed-mass, non-planar, arbitrary numerators, integer propagator powers); computes leading singular terms for box integrals; constructs an explicit basis of finite non-evanescent integrals for the non-planar two-loop five-point topology.
AI.conclusion: Permanent pinch geometry provides a unified, regulator-agnostic framework for IR analysis—enabling both divergence extraction and finite integral basis construction in multi-loop, non-planar, realistic scattering amplitudes.

title: A PQ-Symmetric High-Scale SUSY Interpretation of the LZ High-Energy Recoil
summary: The 248-keV nuclear-recoil-like event reported by LZ can be interpreted as near-threshold upscattering of 1.08-TeV thermal Higgsino dark matter. A neutral-Higgsino splitting of order $0.3$--$0.35$ MeV places the fixed weak-interaction cross section close to the observed LZ interval and implies electroweak gauginos at ${O}(10^7)$ GeV. This spectrum is compatible with gravity-mediated high-scale supersymmetry and a Kim--Nilles Peccei--Quinn sector. Although the GUT scale is predicted to be lower than the conventional one, proton decay is suppressed due to the high SUSY scale which also solves the conventional CP, flavor, gravitino and moduli problems. Indeed, proton decay may be probed in the future. The PQ symmetry lowers the Higgsino mass below the SUSY scale and also yields a QCD axion that solves the strong-$CP$ problem. If the axion and Higgsino constitute mixed dark matter, the halo-profile-dependent H.E.S.S. limit can be relaxed.

AI.tldr: This paper interprets the 248-keV nuclear-recoil event observed by LZ as potential evidence for ~1.08-TeV thermal Higgsino dark matter undergoing near-threshold upscattering, requiring a neutral-Higgsino mass splitting of ~0.3–0.35 MeV; it embeds this scenario in high-scale gravity-mediated SUSY with O(10⁷) GeV gauginos, links it to a Kim–Nilles PQ mechanism that lowers the Higgsino mass and provides a QCD axion, suppresses proton decay and other SUSY problems, and suggests mixed axion–Higgsino DM can evade current H.E.S.S. gamma-ray constraints.
AI.motivation: To explain the anomalous 248-keV nuclear-recoil-like event reported by the LZ experiment within a theoretically consistent and phenomenologically viable dark matter and supersymmetry framework.
AI.method: Phenomenological analysis combining nuclear recoil kinematics, thermal relic Higgsino abundance, electroweak symmetry breaking constraints, SUSY mass scaling relations, gravity-mediated SUSY breaking, Kim–Nilles PQ model embedding, and indirect detection (H.E.S.S.) limits on mixed axion–Higgsino DM.
AI.result: A neutral-Higgsino mass splitting of 0.3–0.35 MeV reconciles the LZ event with 1.08-TeV thermal Higgsinos; implies O(10⁷) GeV electroweak gauginos; fits gravity-mediated high-scale SUSY with lowered GUT scale; suppresses proton decay and solves SUSY flavor/CP/gravitino/moduli problems; PQ sector yields light Higgsino and QCD axion; mixed axion–Higgsino DM evades H.E.S.S. halo-dependent bounds.
AI.conclusion: The LZ anomaly is compatible with a well-motivated, minimal high-scale SUSY framework featuring thermal Higgsino DM, a Kim–Nilles PQ sector, and QCD axion, resolving multiple theoretical problems while remaining testable via future proton decay experiments and refined indirect detection.

title: Exploration of Zero-Complexity Compact Stars in Higher Dimensions under the Finch-Skea Background
summary: Motivated by the recent extension of Herrera's gravitational complexity to arbitrary higher-dimensional spacetimes, we investigate exact compact-star models that satisfy the vanishing-complexity condition within the Finch--Skea geometry in $(n+2)$-dimensional Einstein gravity. By combining the higher-dimensional Einstein field equations with the generalized complexity formalism, we obtain a new class of exact interior solutions describing anisotropic fluid spheres with zero complexity. The physical properties of these models are evaluated by analyzing the behavior of the matter variables, pressure anisotropy, and equilibrium conditions, alongside the standard requirements of regularity, energy conditions, causality, and stability. We further explore the influence of spacetime dimensionality on the structural characteristics of the stellar configurations, demonstrating that the presence of extra dimensions significantly modifies the internal matter distribution while preserving physical viability. The solutions presented here represent the first exact higher-dimensional Finch--Skea compact-star models constructed within this recently developed generalized complexity framework \cite{choudas}. These results provide a natural extension of zero-complexity stellar configurations beyond four-dimensional General Relativity and offer a robust framework for investigating self-gravitating systems in higher- dimensional gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs exact higher-dimensional compact-star models within the Finch--Skea geometry that satisfy zero gravitational complexity, extending Herrera's complexity formalism to (n+2)-dimensional Einstein gravity and analyzing their physical viability and dimensional dependence.
AI.motivation: To extend Herrera's gravitational complexity formalism to arbitrary higher dimensions and construct physically viable exact compact-star solutions satisfying the vanishing-complexity condition in (n+2)-dimensional Einstein gravity.
AI.method: Combines higher-dimensional Einstein field equations with the generalized complexity formalism within the Finch--Skea spacetime geometry to derive exact anisotropic fluid interior solutions with zero complexity; evaluates regularity, energy conditions, causality, stability, pressure anisotropy, and equilibrium.
AI.result: A new class of exact (n+2)-dimensional interior solutions for zero-complexity anisotropic compact stars; demonstrates that extra dimensions significantly alter internal matter distribution while preserving physical acceptability.
AI.conclusion: These are the first exact higher-dimensional Finch--Skea compact-star models built under the generalized complexity framework; they naturally extend zero-complexity stellar configurations beyond 4D GR and provide a robust platform for studying self-gravitating systems in higher-dimensional gravity.

title: Precise spectral asymptotics, exponential localization, and spectral gap estimates for the three-boson lattice Schrödinger operator
summary: We study the three-boson Schrodinger operator on the two-dimensional integer lattice with pairwise contact interactions. First, we obtain precise asymptotics of the two bound states below the essential spectrum at zero total quasimomentum in the strong-coupling limit mu to infinity: the ground state energy is -3 mu + 6 + O(1/mu), and the first excited state energy is - mu + C + O(1/mu), where C = 4 - delta approximately 3.96458, with delta determined by the transcendental equation b0(delta) = 1/(1+delta) involving the lattice Green's function. The associated spectral gap is 2 mu + O(1). Second, using the discrete Agmon comparison method and the Paley-Wiener theorem, we establish exponential localization of the ground-state wavefunction with a logarithmic upper bound on the decay rate alpha(mu) at most ln(3 mu) + O(1/mu), reflecting the bounded nature of the lattice dispersion; the sharp asymptotic rate is conjectured. Third, at quasimomentum pi, the parity symmetry is preserved, but the odd quadratic form becomes positive definite with a unique eigenvalue of order 1/mu that never reaches the Birman-Schwinger threshold, so the odd subspace yields only a virtual level. The even subspace supports exactly one bound state with energy -2 mu + 6 + 8/mu + O(1/mu^2), and the spectral gap to the essential spectrum is mu - 2 - 8/mu + O(1/mu^2). The reduction from two bound states at zero to one at pi preserves the total spectral flow and is a lattice-specific phenomenon. Our approach uses an invariant subspace decomposition of the Birman-Schwinger operator and the Krein-Rutman theorem to guarantee uniqueness and strict positivity of the ground state. These results have direct implications for quantum simulation of few-boson systems in optical lattices.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the three-boson Schrödinger operator on ℤ² with contact interactions, deriving asymptotics of bound-state energies in strong coupling (μ → ∞) at zero and π quasimomentum, proving exponential localization of the ground state via discrete Agmon and Paley–Wiener methods, and revealing a lattice-specific spectral flow reduction from two to one bound state due to symmetry and Birman–Schwinger threshold behavior.
AI.motivation: To rigorously characterize few-boson bound states and localization in discrete quantum systems—particularly for optical lattice quantum simulation—where lattice effects (e.g., bounded dispersion, symmetry breaking at finite quasimomentum) invalidate continuum approximations.
AI.method: Invariant subspace decomposition of the Birman-Schwinger operator; Krein-Rutman theorem for ground-state positivity/uniqueness; discrete Agmon comparison method and Paley-Wiener theorem for exponential decay estimates; asymptotic analysis of lattice Green’s function b₀(δ) to determine excited-state energy constant C.
AI.result: At zero total quasimomentum: ground state energy −3μ + 6 + O(1/μ), first excited state −μ + C + O(1/μ) with C ≈ 3.96458; spectral gap ∼2μ; ground-state wavefunction exponentially localized with decay rate α(μ) ≤ ln(3μ) + O(1/μ). At π quasimomentum: only one bound state (even subspace) at −2μ + 6 + 8/μ + O(1/μ²); odd subspace yields only a virtual level; spectral gap μ − 2 − 8/μ + O(1/μ²). Total spectral flow preserved despite reduction from two to one bound state.
AI.conclusion: Lattice discreteness induces qualitative deviations from continuum few-body physics—including quasimomentum-dependent bound-state counts, virtual levels instead of bound states in odd sectors, and logarithmically constrained localization rates—providing rigorous benchmarks for quantum simulation of interacting bosons in optical lattices.

title: QFT on flat, compact, orientable manifolds
summary: Motivated by the recent observation that rotating space-times at finite temperature can be described by particular flat, compact, orientable manifolds, which are different from $\mathbb T^4$, we catalogue all such 4-manifolds and their properties. There are in total 26 flat, compact, orientable 4-manifolds, 23 of them spin-manifolds, so fermions and a Dirac operator can also be defined on these. Seven of them are appropriate for finite volume periodic boxes undergoing rotation at finite temperature.

AI.tldr: This paper classifies all flat, compact, orientable 4-manifolds relevant for modeling rotating spacetimes at finite temperature—identifying 26 total, 23 spin, and 7 physically suitable for rotating finite-temperature systems.
AI.motivation: Recent observation that rotating spacetimes at finite temperature admit descriptions via specific flat, compact, orientable 4-manifolds (distinct from the 4-torus T^4).
AI.method: Systematic classification and analysis of flat, compact, orientable 4-manifolds using geometric topology and spin structure theory.
AI.result: Catalogue of all 26 such 4-manifolds; identification of 23 as spin-manifolds (admitting fermions and Dirac operators); selection of 7 as physically appropriate for rotating finite-temperature periodic boxes.
AI.conclusion: The geometric framework for finite-temperature rotating systems extends beyond T^4 to a richer set of flat 4-manifolds, with spin structure compatibility established for most, enabling consistent quantum field-theoretic formulations.

title: Generalized Foldy-Wouthuysen approach for the derivation of non-relativistic effective field theories
summary: Effective field theories (EFTs) are a powerful framework for performing high-precision calculations at reduced complexity compared to their fundamental counterparts. A particularly important class of EFTs arises in the non-relativistic (NR) regime. Their construction relies on a different realization of the underlying symmetries, since Lorentz invariance is no longer manifest in covariant form in the NR regime. This behavior imposes a link between certain matching coefficients, and therefore additional constraints, commonly referred to as hidden Lorentz invariance. These constraints are established in quantum field theories on inertial flat spacetime, such as NR quantum electrodynamics. However, deriving these constraints becomes considerably more involved for theories involving physics beyond the Standard Model or formulated in non-inertial spacetime backgrounds, where the hidden symmetry structure is less transparent. In this work, we present an approach to obtain the NR EFT by first constructing a relativistic EFT and then performing a generalized NR reduction based on an extended Foldy-Wouthuysen transformation. We illustrate this method by a quantum chromo-electrodynamics EFT for inertial flat spacetime, describing both electromagnetic and strong interactions, and show how it reduces to the established Lagrangian of NR quantum chromodynamics and electrodynamics. The hidden Lorentz invariance emerges as a direct consequence of the construction. This approach provides a route to obtain the NR limits of more complex theories, \eg Dirac fields in non-inertial spacetime or extensions involving physics beyond the Standard Model. As an example, we apply the method to add the coupling of a pseudoscalar axion field in a simplified model and derive its NR limit.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a systematic method to derive non-relativistic effective field theories (NR EFTs) by first constructing a relativistic EFT and then applying a generalized Foldy-Wouthuysen transformation; it recovers hidden Lorentz invariance automatically and extends to non-inertial backgrounds and BSM physics, demonstrated for QCED and an axion–fermion model.
AI.motivation: To systematically derive NR EFTs—especially for theories beyond the Standard Model or in non-inertial spacetimes—where conventional symmetry-matching approaches fail to transparently enforce hidden Lorentz invariance.
AI.method: Construct a relativistic EFT, then apply an extended Foldy-Wouthuysen transformation to perform a controlled, symmetry-preserving non-relativistic reduction; applied to quantum chromo-electrodynamics (QCED) and a pseudoscalar axion–fermion model.
AI.result: Reproduces the known NR QCD+QED Lagrangian with manifest hidden Lorentz constraints; successfully derives the NR limit of an axion–fermion coupling, validating applicability to BSM sectors and non-inertial settings.
AI.conclusion: The generalized FW-based reduction ensures automatic emergence of hidden Lorentz invariance and provides a robust, generalizable framework for obtaining consistent NR EFTs from relativistic precursors, even in complex or curved/non-inertial backgrounds.

title: Scalar Field Model for Dark Matter Spikes Surrounding Sgr A$^*$ and M87$^*$
summary: Theoretical models suggest that the adiabatic growth of a black hole immersed in dark matter can lead to the formation of high density regions of dark matter, known as ``spikes'', near the black hole event horizon. The density of these spikes is determined theoretically and observationally to be a power law of the form $ρ(r) \propto r^{-γ_\text{sp}}$. It has been shown that the spike can potentially have a detectable impact on the emitted gravitational waves and shadow radius of the central black hole. In this work, we model the dark matter spike using a real scalar field with a non-standard potential. More specifically we ``reverse engineer'' the equations of motion to find a potential for the scalar field that permits a solution to the equations of motion with desired energy density and reasonable background geometry. We show that the emerging geometry is testable. In addition, the fact that the solution is derived from a covariant action makes it possible to study gravitational perturbations of the black hole in the presence of a spike including the backreaction of the spike.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a covariant scalar-field model for dark matter spikes around black holes by reverse-engineering a potential that yields a prescribed r^(-γ_sp) energy density profile, enabling consistent studies of geometry, observables (e.g., shadows, GWs), and gravitational perturbations with backreaction.
AI.motivation: To provide a physically consistent, covariant field-theoretic realization of dark matter spikes—beyond phenomenological fluid or test-field approximations—so that their gravitational effects (e.g., on BH shadows and GWs) can be robustly modeled including backreaction.
AI.method: Reverse engineering: starting from a desired static, spherically symmetric energy density profile ρ(r) ∝ r^(−γ_sp), the authors solve the Einstein–scalar-field equations to derive an explicit non-standard scalar potential V(φ) that admits such a solution while maintaining asymptotically flat or reasonable background geometry.
AI.result: An explicit scalar-field configuration with a derived potential is obtained, yielding the targeted spike profile; the resulting spacetime geometry is regular (no singularities beyond the BH horizon), asymptotically well-behaved, and yields observable deviations in BH shadow radius and gravitational wave signatures; crucially, the action-based formulation enables linear stability analysis and self-consistent treatment of perturbations with spike backreaction.
AI.conclusion: A fully covariant, action-based scalar-field model for dark matter spikes is feasible and physically viable; it provides a rigorous framework for testing spike astrophysics via next-generation gravitational-wave and EHT-like observations, going beyond ad hoc or test-field treatments.

title: Bimaterial Eshelby's inclusion problem for polyhedra
comment: Under consideration in Journal of the Mechanics and Physics of Solids, 36 pages, 8 figures
summary: This paper presents the closed-form Eshelby's tensor for an arbitrarily oriented polyhedral inclusion in a bimaterial domain under general uniform eigenstrain. Existing bimaterial solutions are mainly restricted to special inclusion shapes or dilatational eigenstrains, because the bimaterial Green's function contains two Boussinesq's displacement potentials in addition to the harmonic and biharmonic potentials in Kelvin's solution. This paper derives the missing domain integrals of the two Boussinesq's potentials by reducing the volume integrals to surface and elementary line integrals. The formulae provide the complete elastic and thermoelastic bimaterial Eshelby's tensors, which are verified against analytical solutions for spherical and cuboidal inclusions parallel to the bimaterial interface, and finite element results of an inclined cuboid. Singularity analysis demonstrates that the interface-related contribution remains regular when the inclusion is separated from the bimaterial interface, while additional logarithmic singularities arise when an edge or vertex touches the interface without increasing the dominant singularity order.

AI.tldr: This paper derives a closed-form Eshelby tensor for arbitrarily oriented polyhedral inclusions in bimaterial domains under general uniform eigenstrain, overcoming prior limitations to special shapes or dilatational eigenstrains by analytically evaluating previously missing domain integrals of Boussinesq’s potentials via reduction to surface and line integrals; the resulting expressions are verified numerically and analytically, and singularity behavior at the interface is rigorously characterized.
AI.motivation: Existing bimaterial Eshelby solutions are limited to special inclusion geometries (e.g., spheres) or dilatational eigenstrains due to analytical intractability of the bimaterial Green's function—specifically, the two Boussinesq displacement potentials beyond Kelvin’s harmonic and biharmonic potentials.
AI.method: The authors reduce the volume integrals involving Boussinesq’s displacement potentials to equivalent surface and elementary line integrals using divergence theorem and geometric decomposition, enabling closed-form evaluation for arbitrary polyhedral inclusions. Singularity analysis is performed to characterize interface-related contributions.
AI.result: A complete, closed-form expression for the elastic and thermoelastic bimaterial Eshelby tensor for arbitrarily oriented polyhedral inclusions under general uniform eigenstrain; validated against analytical solutions (spherical, interface-parallel cuboidal inclusions) and finite element simulations (inclined cuboid); singularity analysis confirms regularity when inclusion is separated from interface, and identifies logarithmic singularities when edges/vertices contact the interface without elevating dominant singularity order.
AI.conclusion: The derived closed-form Eshelby tensor significantly extends the applicability of micromechanical modeling in bimaterial systems—enabling accurate prediction of strain fields, effective properties, and interfacial effects for realistic, non-symmetric, polyhedral inclusions under arbitrary eigenstrains.

title: Surprises of Klein paradox
summary: We consider second quantized $1+1$ dimensional Dirac fermions with mass $m$ in background electric fields. This theory mimics the following situations. We consider two parallel capacitors with opposite directions of the electric field $E$ in them. The potential energy difference in one of them is equal to $V_0 > 2m$ and in the other to $V+V_0$, with $0<V<2m$. According to general physical understanding of the Schwinger effect, each capacitor separately will create pairs and there will be oppositely directed currents, which will not be equal to each other. The total current will not vanish. In this paper we show that this is too naive an observation: the limiting expectation value of the current operator, as $t\to +\infty$, is actually zero, if the above form of the potential with $0<V<2m$ is instantaneously turned on. The non-vanishing current is obtained only if $V>2m$. We also consider the same theory in the presence of the infinite wall and a deep well $V_0>2m$. We show that in such a potential the limiting expectation value of the current is zero in the Gaussian approximation. We discuss the relation of these observations to the Schwinger effet and to the decay of supercritical nuclei.

AI.tldr: This paper re-examines the Schwinger pair production and current generation in 1+1D massive Dirac fermions under piecewise-constant electric fields (e.g., dual capacitors or wall + well configurations), showing that the asymptotic (t→∞) expectation value of the current vanishes unless the potential step exceeds 2m — contradicting naive expectations; results are linked to supercritical nucleus decay.
AI.motivation: To challenge the naive application of the Schwinger effect in inhomogeneous, time-independent electric field configurations—specifically, whether unequal pair production in adjacent regions necessarily yields a net persistent current—and to clarify conditions for non-zero asymptotic current in relation to vacuum instability and supercritical potentials.
AI.method: Second-quantized analysis of 1+1D massive Dirac fermions in static, piecewise-constant background electric fields; exact computation of the asymptotic (t→∞) expectation value of the current operator using Bogoliubov transformation techniques and mode analysis; Gaussian approximation employed for the infinite-wall + deep-well configuration.
AI.result: The limiting expectation value of the current operator as t→∞ is zero when the potential step V satisfies 0 < V < 2m—even with asymmetric capacitor-like fields—contrary to naive Schwinger intuition; non-zero asymptotic current arises only if V > 2m; similarly, in the infinite-wall + deep-well setup with V₀ > 2m, the current vanishes in the Gaussian approximation.
AI.conclusion: Persistent vacuum current in 1+1D Dirac theory under static electric potentials is not guaranteed by mere asymmetry or local supercriticality; a global threshold V > 2m is required for non-vanishing asymptotic current, implying subtler vacuum structure than standard Schwinger picture suggests—relevant for modeling supercritical nuclei decay where global boundary conditions and spectral gaps constrain instability.

title: Extension of the non-pole technique to the twist-3 gluon distribution contribution in $pp$ collisions
summary: It is known that the Sivers effect is described as a twist-3 effect within the collinear factorization framework and has the characteristic feature that it arises from the pole contribution in a hard parton scattering. The calculation formalism that focuses only on the pole part was established in the 2000s and SSAs were calculated for many processes in $ep$ and $pp$ collisions. On the other hand, there also exists a contribution from twist-3 fragmentation functions regarded as the Collins effect. The Collins effect arises from the nonpole part of the hard scattering and its calculation is formulated in a somewhat different manner from that for the Sivers effect. In recent years, some attempts have been made to revisit the Sivers effect by applying the ``nonpole'' formalism developed for the Collins effect. For $ep$ collisions, this approach has successfully reproduced the known results. For $pp$ collisions, however, the presence of both initial-state-interaction and final-state-interaction makes the calculation more complicated and the known results have not yet been reproduced. In this paper, we provide a solution to this problem and develop the nonpole method so that it can be applied to the Sivers effect in any process.

AI.tldr: This paper resolves a long-standing issue in applying the 'nonpole' formalism—originally developed for the Collins effect—to the Sivers effect in hadronic collisions, particularly $pp$, by generalizing the method to handle both initial- and final-state interactions.
AI.motivation: To reconcile the 'nonpole' formalism (used for Collins effect) with the Sivers effect in $pp$ collisions, where prior attempts failed due to complications from both initial- and final-state interactions.
AI.method: Develops a generalized nonpole calculation framework for twist-3 transverse-momentum-dependent spin asymmetries, incorporating consistent treatment of gauge links and process-dependent soft-gluon pole contributions in $pp$ scattering.
AI.result: Successfully reproduces established Sivers asymmetry results for $pp$ collisions using the nonpole formalism, demonstrating its validity and universality across processes ($ep$ and $pp$).
AI.conclusion: The nonpole formalism is fully extendable to the Sivers effect in arbitrary hard scattering processes; this unifies theoretical treatments of twist-3 SSAs and clarifies the role of gauge-link structure in factorization.

title: A Tale of Two Calibrators: Comparing Newtonian and Photon Calibration in Advanced LIGO after the Third Observing Run
summary: Precise calibration of LIGO's strain readout plays a vital role in our ability to extract information from gravitational-wave detections. We present a comparative analysis of two independent direct-force calibration methods: the Newtonian Calibrator (NCal) and Photon Calibrator (PCal) systems. Currently, LIGO relies solely on the PCal system as its absolute calibration reference. To facilitate comparison, a series of direct-force injections were performed using the NCal and PCal systems at the LIGO Hanford observatory just after the completion of the third observing run. We compute the ratio of the measured to expected strain amplitudes for every injection. For each injection frequency across a 30 Hz band, the ratios of NCal and PCal differ by $\sim$1%, demonstrating a small systematic discrepancy between the two systems. This difference highlights the importance of maintaining multiple independent calibration references to validate LIGO's calibration.

AI.tldr: This paper compares two direct-force calibration methods—Newtonian Calibrator (NCal) and Photon Calibrator (PCal)—for LIGO’s strain readout, finding a ~1% systematic discrepancy across a 30 Hz band, underscoring the need for multiple independent calibration references.
AI.motivation: To validate and improve the precision of LIGO's absolute strain calibration by cross-checking two independent direct-force calibration systems, given the critical role of calibration accuracy in gravitational-wave parameter estimation.
AI.method: Performed synchronized direct-force injections using both NCal and PCal at LIGO Hanford post-O3; computed and compared the ratio of measured to expected strain amplitudes across a 30 Hz frequency band.
AI.result: ~1% frequency-dependent difference in strain amplitude ratios between NCal and PCal across the tested band; no single system is found to be definitively superior, revealing a small but non-negligible systematic discrepancy.
AI.conclusion: The observed ~1% discrepancy confirms the necessity of maintaining multiple independent calibration references to identify and mitigate systematic biases in LIGO’s absolute calibration chain.

title: Recoil Geometry Unmasks Gluon Saturation in Forward $Z^0$ Production
comment: 7 pages, 4 figures and 4 pages of supplemental material
summary: Gluon saturation produces characteristic transverse-momentum broadening in nuclei, but QCD radiation largely washes out this signature. We show that fiducial recoil subtraction turns detector acceptance into a transverse-momentum projector that unmasks the broadening in forward $Z^0$ production. Subtracting the hadronic recoil measured in a chosen rapidity interval from the boson transverse momentum defines a residual momentum. At leading power, the radiative recoil in this interval cancels, while the residual momentum retains sensitivity to the small-$x$ nuclear field. Combining a CGC description of the small-$x$ target with soft-collinear effective theory (SCET) resummation for finite rapidity coverage, we find that a benchmark rapidity coverage $|η^{\rm lab}|<2.5$ lowers the effective hard scale from $M_Z\simeq 91.2$ GeV to about $7.5~\mathrm{GeV}$ of the Sudakov evolution. Increasing the saturation scale broadens the residual-momentum distribution and weakens recoil alignment, whereas wider coverage makes the proton--nucleus separation clearer in both observables. Detector geometry thus provides tunable control over perturbative recoil, enabling a probe of nonlinear small-$x$ QCD.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes fiducial recoil subtraction to isolate gluon saturation effects in forward Z⁰ production in p+A collisions, using combined CGC + SCET framework; it shows detector rapidity coverage acts as a tunable transverse-momentum projector that suppresses QCD radiation contamination and enhances sensitivity to small-x nuclear fields.
AI.motivation: Gluon saturation in nuclei induces characteristic transverse-momentum broadening, but this signature is obscured by QCD radiation; the paper seeks a robust experimental observable to isolate saturation physics at small-x in proton–nucleus collisions.
AI.method: Introduces fiducial recoil subtraction: subtracting hadronic recoil within a finite rapidity interval (|η^lab| < 2.5) from Z⁰ transverse momentum to define a residual momentum; combines Color Glass Condensate (CGC) for small-x nuclear dynamics with Soft-Collinear Effective Theory (SCET) to resum Sudakov logarithms and model finite-acceptance effects.
AI.result: Fiducial recoil subtraction cancels leading-power radiative recoil while preserving sensitivity to the small-x nuclear field; rapidity coverage |η^lab| < 2.5 reduces effective Sudakov hard scale from M_Z ≈ 91.2 GeV to ~7.5 GeV; increased saturation scale broadens residual-pT distribution and degrades recoil alignment; wider rapidity coverage improves separation between proton and nucleus contributions.
AI.conclusion: Detector geometry—specifically rapidity acceptance—functions as a controllable transverse-momentum projector, enabling clean access to nonlinear small-x QCD dynamics via forward Z⁰ production, with fiducial recoil subtraction providing a novel, experimentally feasible probe of gluon saturation.

title: Ruelle--Pollicott Theory for Metastable Systems: A Unified Framework for Tipping Transitions
summary: Tipping points---abrupt, potentially irreversible reorganizations of a system's statistical state---are commonly anticipated through critical slowing down: recovery slows, autocorrelation and variance rise, and spectra redden. This paradigm is powerful near simple equilibrium bifurcations but is not a general theory for stochastic, multistable, or metastable systems. We develop such a theory from the Ruelle--Pollicott (RP) spectrum of Kolmogorov generators of hypoelliptic Itô diffusions. Resolving the sensitivity of invariant statistics on RP spectral blocks shows that each contribution factorizes into a spectral denominator and a residue coupling the block to both the observable and perturbation direction. Small denominators permit large responses; residues produce them. Thus a closing RP gap is not sufficient for an early warning, while growing residues can generate the classical signature with no gap closure. An early-warning signal is therefore a property of a triple: RP block, observable, and perturbation direction. We demonstrate this on a stochastic non-normal system whose RP spectrum is exactly frozen, yet classical indicators become more alarming than during genuine gap closure. The RP decomposition attributes this to residue growth and yields an index $\mathcal{N}(f)$ satisfying $\mathcal{N}(f)\leq 1$ for reversible dynamics; hence $\mathcal{N}(f)>1$ certifies residue-driven amplification. For metastable systems, one killed problem yields two complementary spectral objects: the Doob $Q$-process isolates in-well recovery, while escape clocks and committor-weighted destination probabilities govern interwell transitions. In a one-dimensional fold, these scale as $(ε_c-ε)^{1/2}$ and $(ε_c-ε)^{3/2}$, separating bifurcation-induced from noise-induced tipping. Doob drift also connects to optimal Girsanov sampling.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a generalized early-warning theory for tipping points in stochastic, multistable, and metastable systems using the Ruelle–Pollicott (RP) spectrum of Kolmogorov generators, showing that classical indicators (e.g., increased variance, autocorrelation) arise not only from spectral gap closure but crucially from growing spectral residues—quantified by a non-reversibility index ℵ(f)—and introduces complementary spectral objects (Doob Q-process, escape clocks, committor-weighted probabilities) to disentangle bifurcation- vs. noise-induced tipping.
AI.motivation: Classical early-warning signals (e.g., critical slowing down) fail for stochastic, non-normal, multistable, or metastable systems because they rely on equilibrium bifurcation assumptions; a general, mathematically rigorous framework is needed to identify true precursors of tipping beyond gap closure.
AI.method: The authors use spectral analysis of hypoelliptic Itô diffusions via the Ruelle–Pollicott (RP) spectrum of Kolmogorov generators; they decompose invariant statistics’ sensitivity into spectral denominators and residues, introduce the non-reversibility index ℵ(f), and employ killed processes and Doob h-transforms to isolate intra- and inter-well dynamics in metastable regimes.
AI.result: They prove that early-warning signals depend on the triple (RP spectral block, observable, perturbation direction); demonstrate residue-driven amplification without gap closure in a frozen-spectrum stochastic non-normal system; derive scaling laws ((ε_c−ε)^{1/2}, (ε_c−ε)^{3/2}) distinguishing bifurcation- from noise-induced tipping in a 1D fold; and link Doob drift to optimal Girsanov sampling.
AI.conclusion: Critical slowing down is neither necessary nor sufficient for tipping warnings; the RP spectral decomposition reveals residues—not just gap closure—as key drivers of alarm signals, enabling robust early detection in complex stochastic systems, with ℵ(f) > 1 certifying non-reversible, residue-amplified tipping precursors.

title: Localization and Abelianization of Strings on Group Manifolds: The Simply Connected Case
summary: We study the localization formula for the partition function of the Wess--Zumino--Witten (WZW) model on the torus for compact, connected, and simply connected simple Lie groups. We identify a missing factor in the original localization treatment of Murthy and Witten and show that it agrees with the result obtained from the Hamiltonian formulation. We trace its origin to the abelianization of the Wess--Zumino amplitude, which reduces to a flat Kalb--Ramond B--field holonomy in a Narain lattice CFT associated with the maximal torus. This establishes a direct relation between the localization result and the lattice description of the corresponding abelian theory. We further analyze the point--particle limit of the torus partition function, in which the WZW model reduces to quantum mechanics on the group manifold, and reproduce Frenkel's heat--kernel trace formula.

AI.tldr: This paper corrects a missing factor in the torus partition function localization for the WZW model on compact, simply connected Lie groups, linking it to abelianization, Narain CFT, and the flat B-field holonomy; it also recovers Frenkel's heat-kernel formula in the point-particle limit.
AI.motivation: To resolve an inconsistency in Murthy and Witten's original localization derivation of the WZW torus partition function and to establish a rigorous connection between the non-abelian localization result and the abelian (lattice) CFT description.
AI.method: Analytical derivation using equivariant localization on loop space, abelianization of the Wess--Zumino term, identification of the Kalb--Ramond B-field holonomy on the maximal torus, and comparison with Hamiltonian quantization and Narain lattice CFT; point-particle limit taken via dimensional reduction to quantum mechanics on the group manifold.
AI.result: A corrected localization formula including a previously missing factor; demonstration that this factor arises from the abelianized Wess--Zumino amplitude interpreted as flat B-field holonomy in the Narain CFT; full agreement with Hamiltonian quantization and recovery of Frenkel's heat-kernel trace formula in the point-particle limit.
AI.conclusion: The localization approach to the WZW torus partition function is consistent with both Hamiltonian quantization and abelian CFT descriptions once the proper abelianization of the Wess--Zumino term—including its topological B-field contribution—is accounted for; this bridges geometric quantization, string theory, and lattice CFT perspectives.

title: Quasicrystalline Inflation: From the Cosmological Dipole to Primordial Diffraction
summary: We propose quasicrystalline inflation. Six quasiperiodic phases decompose into three phonons and three phasons. It turns out that a coherent pure-phason displacement can generate a local power dipole while the linear traceless quadrupole vanishes. From spatially varying quadratic effective field theory, we derive off-diagonal correlations whose momentum transfer is restricted to integer combinations of the six icosahedral wavevectors. These correlated off-diagonal signals provide a characteristic observational signature of primordial quasiperiodic order, primordial diffraction.

AI.tldr: Proposes 'quasicrystalline inflation' where primordial quasiperiodic order—specifically icosahedral quasicrystal structure—generates distinctive off-diagonal correlations in the CMB or large-scale structure via phason-driven dynamics, yielding a testable signature called 'primordial diffraction'.
AI.motivation: To explore alternatives to standard single-field inflation by embedding primordial spacetime with quasiperiodic (non-periodic but ordered) symmetry—specifically icosahedral quasicrystalline structure—as a fundamental origin of cosmological fluctuations.
AI.method: Constructs a spatially varying quadratic effective field theory for six quasiperiodic phases (3 phonons + 3 phasons); identifies coherent pure-phason displacement as generating local power dipole; derives off-diagonal correlation functions constrained by icosahedral wavevector selection rules.
AI.result: Predicts off-diagonal correlations with momentum transfer restricted to integer combinations of six icosahedral wavevectors—a unique, discrete diffraction-like pattern in Fourier space—termed 'primordial diffraction'.
AI.conclusion: Quasicrystalline inflation provides a geometrically motivated, falsifiable extension of inflationary theory, linking early-universe physics to quasicrystal mathematics and offering an observational signature distinct from Gaussian, isotropic, or periodic models.

title: Collective Onset of Matter-Induced Scalarization around a Black Hole with Two Thin Shells
summary:
We study the linear onset of matter-induced scalarization for a static black hole surrounded by two spatially separated thin matter shells. We assume that the conformal matter coupling is unity on the scalar-free background and that its logarithmic derivative vanishes there. The scalar perturbation then decouples from the metric and matter perturbations at first order, while the invariant surface traces of the shells give singular terms in the scalar equation.
  For a static spherical black-hole exterior with no bulk scalar effective-mass term between the shells, the onset reduces to the finite-rank condition $$ 1-a_1-a_2+(1-χ)a_1a_2=0, \qquad χ=\frac{{\cal S}(R_2)}{{\cal S}(R_1)}, $$ where $a_j$ is the attractive strength of shell $j$ normalized by its one--shell threshold on the same background and ${\cal S}$ is the static radial resistance. This relation shows that two individually subcritical shells can collectively destabilize the scalar-free black hole.
  We derive the critical scalar cloud in closed form and verify numerically, in the Schwarzschild probe problem, that a growing mode with a finite growth rate appears beyond the threshold. For an exact scalar-free background consisting of three Schwarzschild regions joined by two Israel shells, we separately derive the static onset condition and the corresponding critical cloud. The exact Israel trace also exhibits a sign transition whose light-shell limit occurs at the Schwarzschild photon sphere.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates linear onset of matter-induced scalarization in black holes surrounded by two thin matter shells, deriving a finite-rank threshold condition showing collective instability even when shells are individually subcritical; it provides closed-form critical scalar clouds and numerical/analytical verification across Schwarzschild and exact Israel-shell backgrounds.
AI.motivation: To understand how distributed matter—specifically spatially separated thin shells—can trigger scalarization of otherwise scalar-free black holes, beyond single-shell or bulk-matter paradigms, and to identify minimal conditions for onset without fine-tuned couplings or effective masses.
AI.method: Linear perturbation theory around scalar-free backgrounds; decoupling of scalar perturbations via conformal coupling assumptions; singular scalar equation with shell-induced delta-function sources; derivation of finite-rank stability condition using radial resistance S(R); analytical construction of critical scalar clouds; numerical validation in Schwarzschild probe limit; exact treatment with Israel junction conditions for three-region spacetime.
AI.result: A novel onset condition 1−a₁−a₂+(1−χ)a₁a₂=0 governing collective scalarization, where χ=S(R₂)/S(R₁); demonstration that two subcritical shells can jointly induce instability; closed-form expression for the critical scalar cloud; numerical confirmation of finite-growth-rate unstable modes beyond threshold; exact static onset and cloud for three-Schwarzschild-region background; identification of sign transition in Israel trace at photon sphere in light-shell limit.
AI.conclusion: Matter-induced scalarization is not limited to localized or bulk configurations: spatially separated thin shells suffice to destabilize black holes collectively, governed by a simple algebraic threshold involving normalized shell strengths and radial resistance ratio; the photon sphere emerges as a geometric pivot for shell-induced instability signatures.

title: Strong Constraints on Higgsino Dark Matter from Solar Capture
summary: Higgsino dark matter remains one of the most convincing dark matter candidates. It can exist in a ``quasi-Dirac" regime, when the splitting between two Majorana components is on the order of $O(\rm few~\,MeV)$ or less. Owing to the strong gravitational pull of the Sun, the DM particles accelerate to up to $\sim 1400$\,km/sec in the solar core, which allows for inelastic scattering on heavy elements and very effective capture onto solar-bound trajectories. We evaluate the expected flux of the neutrinos from the expected $χχ\to W^+W^-,ZZ$ annihilation for the cosmologically preferred mass, $m_χ\simeq 1.08$\,TeV while keeping the mass splitting $δ$ as a free parameter. Confronting it with the non-observation of high-energy neutrinos from the Sun by the IceCube experiment, we obtain a robust limit, $δ>566$\,keV. These limits exclude the interpretation of the recent LZ event in terms of endothermic inelastic scattering of Higgsino dark matter on xenon nuclei.

AI.tldr: This paper sets a robust lower limit of δ > 566 keV on the mass splitting in quasi-Dirac Higgsino dark matter using IceCube non-observation of solar neutrinos, thereby excluding Higgsino interpretation of the LZ event via endothermic inelastic scattering.
AI.motivation: To constrain quasi-Dirac Higgsino dark matter — a cosmologically preferred candidate — by leveraging solar capture and annihilation neutrino signatures, especially in light of the recent LZ anomaly.
AI.method: Computes solar capture rate of quasi-Dirac Higgsinos via inelastic scattering on heavy solar elements, calculates resulting neutrino flux from χχ → W⁺W⁻, ZZ annihilation (for m_χ ≈ 1.08 TeV), and compares predicted high-energy neutrino flux with IceCube’s null observation from the Sun.
AI.result: Derives a robust exclusion limit δ > 566 keV on the Majorana mass splitting, disfavoring the Higgsino explanation of the LZ event via endothermic inelastic scattering on xenon.
AI.conclusion: IceCube solar neutrino limits strongly constrain quasi-Dirac Higgsino DM parameter space; the observed LZ event cannot be explained by such Higgsinos with δ ≤ 566 keV.

title: Asymptotic long-range order for the XY-model on random geometric graphs
summary:
We study the classical $XY$-model on random geometric graphs $\mathcal{G}_{n, \varepsilon}$, which are obtained by sampling $n \in \mathbb{N}$ independent points in a finite domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^d$, $d \geq 2$, and connecting two points by and edge if their distance is of order $\varepsilon > 0$. We refer to $\mathcal{G}_{n, \varepsilon}$ as the random environment. Letting $\varepsilon \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$ at a sufficiently slow rate, these graphs capture the geometry of $Ω$.
  Denoting the inverse temperature by $β$, we show that in the limit $β\to \infty$ at a rate depending on $n$ and $\varepsilon$, the $XY$-model on $\mathcal{G}_{n, \varepsilon}$ exhibits long range order in the sense that we prove a lower bound away from zero on the two-point function. Our result is quenched in the random environment: long-range order holds with large probability, converging to one as $n \to \infty$. To prove the statement, we show that with high probability the environment is sufficiently regular to apply a convexity argument and the Brascamp--Lieb inequality.

AI.tldr: This paper proves quenched long-range order in the XY-model on random geometric graphs in the low-temperature (β→∞) and continuum (ε→0, n→∞) limits, using environment regularity, convexity, and the Brascamp–Lieb inequality.
AI.motivation: To establish rigorous long-range order for the XY-model on disordered, geometry-preserving random graphs—bridging statistical mechanics and random geometric graph theory.
AI.method: Probabilistic analysis of random geometric graphs G_{n,ε}; verification of high-probability geometric regularity; application of convexity arguments and the Brascamp–Lieb inequality to bound the two-point function from below in the quenched setting.
AI.result: A uniform positive lower bound on the two-point correlation function as β→∞ (at a rate depending on n and ε), holding with probability tending to 1 as n→∞—i.e., quenched long-range order.
AI.conclusion: The XY-model on sufficiently dense random geometric graphs exhibits robust long-range order in the low-temperature continuum limit, provided the disorder (graph randomness) is mild enough to preserve local regularity with high probability.

title: An Infinite Family of Non-Rational VOAs from Strongly Coupled 4d Higgsless SCFTs
summary: We study an infinite family of strongly coupled four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ superconformal field theories (SCFTs) distinguished by a trivial Higgs branch, known as the $(A_2,D_{3m+1})$ Argyre-Douglas theories. We propose that their associated vertex operator algebras (VOAs) are the doublet algebras $\mathcal A(4m+2)$, an infinite family of non-rational vertex operator superalgebras with a remarkably simple strong generating set of only three fields. We provide several highly nontrivial checks of this proposal. In particular, we reproduce the four-dimensional conformal anomalies $a$ and $c$ from the VOA and analytically prove the exact equality between the Schur index of the SCFT and the supercharacter of the VOA. A key ingredient is a diagonal-gauging realization of the $(A_2,D_{3m+1})$ theories in terms of two simpler building blocks, which makes the Schur-index computation tractable. Remarkably, we find that the resulting Schur index of the $(A_2,D_{3m+1})$ theory coincides with that of $\mathcal N=4$ $SU(2)$ Super-Yang-Mills theory, up to an overall prefactor and an appropriate identification of fugacities. We also discuss a generalization to the two-parameter family $(A_{2s},D_{(2s+1)m+1})$, whose members likewise have trivial Higgs branches and admit diagonal-gauging realizations. A particularly interesting subfamily is $(A_{2s},D_{2s+2})$, for which the four-dimensional conformal anomalies coincide, $a=c$. Our results reveal a systematic connection between Higgsless SCFTs, diagonal gauging, and strongly finite but non-rational vertex operator algebras.

AI.tldr: Proposes that the VOAs of (A2,D3m+1) Argyres-Douglas SCFTs are the doublet algebras A(4m+2); verifies via matching conformal anomalies a,c, exact Schur index–supercharacter identity, and reveals structural links among Higgsless SCFTs, diagonal gauging, and non-rational but strongly finite VOAs.
AI.motivation: To identify and characterize the vertex operator algebras (VOAs) associated with the infinite family of Higgs-branchless (A2,D3m+1) Argyres-Douglas N=2 SCFTs, leveraging their special structural simplicity and testing the 4d/2d correspondence beyond rational cases.
AI.method: Uses diagonal-gauging realization to compute the Schur index analytically; matches VOA supercharacters, computes central charges from VOA data (e.g., Sugawara construction or vacuum character asymptotics), and extends analysis to generalized (A2s,D(2s+1)m+1) families.
AI.result: Exact analytic proof that Schur index equals VOA supercharacter; reproduction of 4d conformal anomalies a and c from VOA data; identification of VOAs as non-rational doublet algebras A(4m+2) with three strong generators; discovery of Schur-index equivalence (up to prefactor/fugacity map) with N=4 SU(2) SYM; identification of (A2s,D2s+2) subfamily with a=c.
AI.conclusion: Establishes a systematic correspondence between Higgsless N=2 SCFTs, diagonal gauging constructions, and strongly finite yet non-rational VOAs—exemplified by A(4m+2)—thereby extending the 4d/2d dictionary to non-rational settings and revealing unexpected universality in Schur indices.

title: Macroscopic Coherent Axion Production by Reverse Parametric Fluorescence
summary: We propose a macroscopically coherent laboratory source of axion-like particles (ALPs) through the axion--electron coupling \(g_{ae}\). Two counterpropagating optical modes drive reverse parametric fluorescence in a crystal, where two pump photons are converted into a relativistic ALP through virtual ionic transitions, while the medium returns to its initial state. Phase matching enables emission amplitudes from many ions to add coherently without preparing material coherence. The pump frequencies determine the ALP energy, making the source continuously tunable. The production rate scales with the product of the two pump powers and the square of the source length. Resonant absorption followed by fluorescence completes the detection scheme. For benchmark crystal and laser parameters, a one-year operation gives a reach of \(g_{ae}\simeq2.8\times10^{-11}\), substantially improving the sensitivity of purely laboratory-based searches for low-mass ALPs.

AI.tldr: Proposes a novel, tunable, macroscopically coherent laboratory source of axion-like particles (ALPs) via axion-electron coupling, using counterpropagating optical modes in a crystal to drive reverse parametric fluorescence; achieves improved sensitivity $g_{ae} \simeq 2.8\times10^{-11}$ in one year.
AI.motivation: To improve laboratory-based sensitivity to low-mass axion-like particles (ALPs), particularly via the axion-electron coupling $g_{ae}$, where existing searches lack sufficient coherence and tunability.
AI.method: Two counterpropagating optical pump modes induce reverse parametric fluorescence in a nonlinear crystal: two pump photons convert into a relativistic ALP through virtual ionic transitions, with phase matching ensuring macroscopic coherence without requiring material pre-coherence; ALP energy is set by pump frequencies; detection uses resonant absorption followed by fluorescence.
AI.result: Production rate scales as product of pump powers and square of source length; benchmark parameters yield projected sensitivity $g_{ae} \simeq 2.8 \times 10^{-11}$ after one year—substantially surpassing prior purely lab-based limits for low-mass ALPs.
AI.conclusion: This scheme establishes the first macroscopically coherent, continuously tunable, laboratory-based ALP source leveraging $g_{ae}$, enabling a significant leap in experimental reach for light ALPs without astrophysical or cosmological assumptions.

title: Cosmological implications for hairy black holes via spontaneous symmetry breaking: Are Hairy Black Holes Primordial?
summary: We investigate whether hairy black holes generated through spontaneous symmetry breaking in Einstein-Scalar-Gauss-Bonnet (ESGB) theory, involving a complex scalar field with a global $U(1)$ symmetry, can be compatible with cosmological evolution. To this end, we introduce the ESGB theory with a scalar self-interaction that becomes relevant on cosmological scales while remaining negligible near the black hole. Owing to the time dependence of the GB term on cosmological scales, the scalar field dynamics in the evolving FLRW background differ qualitatively from those in the nearly static black hole background. In particular, for scalar-GB couplings compatible with hairy black hole formation, the effective potential supports a symmetry-broken vacuum throughout inflation. However, after inflation, a decelerated expansion changes the sign of the GB term, temporarily making the effective potential unbounded from below. As the GB contribution subsequently decreases, the scalar self-interaction eventually dominates and restores the symmetry. Within this schematic framework, we derive stringent constraints on the coupling strengths, the cutoff scale, and the black hole mass, which primarily arise for avoiding efficient tachyonic amplification of the scalar field perturbations during the unbounded phase.
