For cutoff scales compatible with both cosmological evolution and scalar hair formation, we find that only ultralight black holes with masses of the order of a few grams can develop scalar hair, identifying them as hairy primordial black holes.

AI.tldr: This paper examines whether hairy black holes formed via spontaneous symmetry breaking in Einstein-Scalar-Gauss-Bonnet (ESGB) theory with a complex scalar field and global U(1) symmetry can coexist with standard cosmological evolution. It shows that while the scalar potential supports symmetry breaking during inflation, post-inflation deceleration flips the Gauss-Bonnet (GB) term sign, causing a transient unbounded effective potential — risking tachyonic instability. To avoid catastrophic scalar perturbation amplification, stringent constraints emerge: only ultralight (~gram-scale) primordial black holes can host stable scalar hair, reconciling hairy BHs with cosmology.
AI.motivation: To assess cosmological viability of hairy black holes in ESGB gravity with global U(1) symmetry — specifically, whether scalar hair formation (requiring spontaneous symmetry breaking) is compatible with FLRW cosmology, especially across inflation–reheating–radiation transitions.
AI.method: Analyzes scalar field dynamics in ESGB theory extended with cosmologically relevant scalar self-interaction; compares time-dependent GB coupling in FLRW background vs. static black hole background; computes evolution of effective potential; identifies epochs where potential becomes unbounded from below; imposes stability conditions against tachyonic perturbations to derive parameter constraints (coupling strengths, cutoff scale, black hole mass).
AI.result: For viable cosmology and hairy black hole existence, the GB-induced instability window after inflation necessitates suppression of tachyonic growth — leading to tight bounds: scalar self-coupling and GB coupling must be hierarchically tuned, cutoff scale must lie near Planck scale but allow late-time symmetry restoration, and only black holes with mass ~1–10 g (i.e., primordial, ultralight) satisfy all constraints.
AI.conclusion: Hairy black holes in this ESGB-U(1) framework are cosmologically allowed only as ultralight primordial black holes (~gram-scale); heavier astrophysical black holes cannot support stable scalar hair without violating cosmological stability requirements.

title: Radiative and Dalitz decays of $Υ(1S)$ in the light of the ATOMKI X17 anomaly
comment: 13 pages, 4 figures, Phenikaa International Physics Conference 2025: Celebrating 100 years of quantum physics (PIPC2025) 13/10/2025 - 15/10/2025 Hanoi, Vietnam
summary: We study the radiative decay $Υ(1S)\to η_bγ$ and the Dalitz decay $Υ(1S)\to η_b e^+ e^-$ within the framework of the Covariant Confined Quark Model. We provide theoretical predictions for the hadronic form factor, the radiative decay constant, and the decay branching fractions. Within the Standard Model we predict $Γ(Υ(1S)\toη_b γ) = 9.3(9)\, \textrm{eV}$ and $Γ(Υ(1S)\toη_b e^+ e^-) = 4.8(5)\times 10^{-2}\, \textrm{eV}$. The contribution of the hypothetical ATOMKI $X17$ vector boson to the Dalitz channel is also investigated.

AI.tldr: This paper calculates radiative and Dalitz decays of Υ(1S) → η_b γ and Υ(1S) → η_b e⁺e⁻ using the Covariant Confined Quark Model, predicts decay widths within the Standard Model, and assesses possible X17 boson contributions to the Dalitz channel.
AI.motivation: To provide precise theoretical predictions for Υ(1S) → η_b γ and Υ(1S) → η_b e⁺e⁻ decays, and to probe physics beyond the Standard Model—specifically the hypothetical X17 vector boson—via its potential contribution to the Dalitz decay.
AI.method: Covariant Confined Quark Model (CCQM), used to compute the hadronic transition form factor, radiative decay constant, and branching fractions; includes evaluation of both Standard Model amplitudes and X17-mediated contributions to the Dalitz process.
AI.result: Predicted widths: Γ(Υ(1S)→η_bγ) = 9.3(9) eV and Γ(Υ(1S)→η_b e⁺e⁻) = 4.8(5)×10⁻² eV; quantified sensitivity of the Dalitz spectrum to a possible X17 signal.
AI.conclusion: The CCQM yields robust SM predictions for these bottomonium transitions; the Υ(1S)→η_b e⁺e⁻ Dalitz decay serves as a clean probe for light weakly-coupled vector bosons like X17, with measurable spectral distortions expected if X17 exists.

title: Localization and Abelianization of Strings on Group Manifolds: The Non-simply Connected Case
summary: We study the partition functions of Wess--Zumino--Witten (WZW) models with compact connected simple Lie group manifolds that are not simply connected. Starting from the modular-invariant partition function of Felder--Gawędzki--Kupiainen (FGK), we derive a localization formula, which can also be obtained directly by supersymmetric localization of the corresponding supersymmetric WZW model. Our results reveal a variety of topological effects associated with the nontrivial topology of the target group. In particular, the Wess--Zumino amplitude is governed by FGK cocycles, while the fermion Pfaffians exhibit global anomalies associated with the holonomies of Pfaffian line bundles, captured by relative Rochlin invariants. Together, these results provide a unified description of the topological contributions to the semiclassical localization of WZW models with non-simply connected target groups.

AI.tldr: This paper derives a localization formula for WZW models on non-simply connected compact Lie group targets, linking modular invariance (FGK construction), supersymmetric localization, Wess--Zumino amplitudes (governed by FGK cocycles), and global fermionic anomalies (encoded in relative Rochlin invariants).
AI.motivation: To understand topological effects—especially those arising from nontrivial π₁(G)—in the semiclassical localization of WZW models with non-simply connected compact simple Lie group targets.
AI.method: Starts from the Felder--Gawędzki--Kupiainen (FGK) modular-invariant partition function; derives a localization formula analytically and confirms it via supersymmetric localization of the corresponding SUSY WZW model; analyzes Wess--Zumino terms using FGK cocycles and fermion Pfaffians using holonomies of Pfaffian line bundles and relative Rochlin invariants.
AI.result: A unified localization formula incorporating both Wess--Zumino amplitudes (via FGK cocycles) and global anomalies in fermionic determinants (via relative Rochlin invariants), fully accounting for π₁(G)-dependent topology.
AI.conclusion: The topological contributions to semiclassical localization in WZW models on non-simply connected groups are coherently described by FGK cocycles and relative Rochlin invariants—establishing a bridge between modular invariance, supersymmetric localization, and global anomalies.

title: Evading Sudakov Dilution in Gluon Tomography
summary: Sudakov broadening and competing azimuthal harmonics from final-state soft radiation limit the precision of gluon tomography. We suppress both effects using fiducial hadronic recoil---the vector sum of all hadronic transverse momenta within a rapidity interval---while a tagged jet fixes the azimuthal axis. Momentum conservation ensures that emissions inside the interval contribute neither to recoil broadening nor to these harmonics, so widening the interval reduces their impact without a soft-radiation veto. As a benchmark, we study the $\cos 2φ$ modulation probing $h_1^{\perp g}$ in DIS. For rapidity interval $Δη=3$, fiducial recoil enhances the $h_1^{\perp g}$ contribution by a factor of $4.6$ and suppresses the final-state soft gluon term by a factor of $4.0$ relative to the conventional dijet imbalance. Fiducial recoil thereby enables precision gluon-TMD tomography.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes 'fiducial hadronic recoil'—a momentum-conserving observable defined within a rapidity interval—to suppress Sudakov broadening and competing azimuthal harmonics from final-state soft radiation, thereby enhancing precision in gluon transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) tomography, specifically for extracting the gluon Boer-Mulders function $h_1^{\perp g}$ via $\cos 2\phi$ modulation in DIS.
AI.motivation: Sudakov broadening and contaminating azimuthal harmonics (e.g., from soft final-state radiation) degrade the sensitivity of dijet-based observables to genuine gluon TMDs like $h_1^{\perp g}$, limiting precision in gluon tomography.
AI.method: Introduces fiducial hadronic recoil—the vector sum of all hadronic transverse momenta within a finite rapidity interval $\Delta \eta$—with a tagged jet defining the azimuthal reference axis; leverages exact transverse momentum conservation to isolate contributions: emissions inside the interval do not affect recoil direction or magnitude, thus suppressing both Sudakov broadening and spurious $\cos n\phi$ ($n\ge2$) modulations without requiring soft-radiation vetoes.
AI.result: For $\Delta \eta = 3$, fiducial recoil enhances the $h_1^{\perp g}$-sensitive $\cos 2\phi$ signal by a factor of 4.6 and suppresses the dominant final-state soft-gluon background by a factor of 4.0 relative to conventional dijet imbalance.
AI.conclusion: Fiducial hadronic recoil is a robust, experimentally feasible observable that significantly improves signal-to-background for gluon TMD extraction, enabling high-precision gluon tomography in DIS and potentially other hard processes.

title: Accretion dynamics of thin and thick disks in charged Kalb-Ramond black holes
summary: In this work, we investigate the accretion properties of an electrically charged, static, spherically symmetric black hole in Kalb-Ramond (KR) gravity, where a dimensionless parameter $l$ characterizes spontaneous Lorentz symmetry-breaking. We first constrain the free charge and KR parameter space, $(Q,l)$, by comparing the predicted shadow radius of this family of solutions with the bounds inferred from Event Horizon Telescope observations of Sagittarius A*. The inclusion of electric charge introduces a degeneracy between $Q$ and $l$, enlarging the region compatible with the observed shadow size and yielding the broad constraint $-0.3900 \leq l \leq 0.1898$, with part of the compatible parameter space extending into the naked-singularity sector. We then investigate relativistic accretion disks around the charged KR black hole within the above constraints. For geometrically thin disks, we compute the time averaged energy flux, temperature distribution, emission spectrum, time averaged torque, and mass-to-radiation conversion efficiency, finding that the radiative output increases for higher values of $l$, while lower values of $l$ suppress it. Furthermore, when coupled with the electric charge this effect is amplified. For geometrically thick, constant-angular momentum tori-shaped disks, Lorentz symmetry-breaking shifts the characteristic orbital radii, compresses the radial extent of equilibrium configurations, narrows the interval supporting finite equilibrium tori, and shifts the stationary-fluid topology toward open and unconfined configurations outside that interval. These results show how charge and spontaneous Lorentz symmetry-breaking jointly affect observational constraints and the structure and emission properties of black hole accretion flows, providing potential signatures of KR gravity in the strong-gravity regime.

AI.tldr: This paper studies accretion properties of charged, static, spherically symmetric black holes in Kalb-Ramond gravity with spontaneous Lorentz symmetry-breaking (parameterized by $l$), constraining $(Q,l)$ using EHT shadow size measurements of Sgr A*, and analyzing thin/thick disk emission and structure—finding that $l$ and $Q$ jointly enhance or suppress radiative output and alter disk geometry and stability.
AI.motivation: To probe observational signatures of Kalb-Ramond gravity—specifically spontaneous Lorentz symmetry-breaking—in the strong-field regime via black hole shadows and accretion disk physics.
AI.method: 1) Shadow radius calculation for charged KR black holes; 2) Parameter space $(Q,l)$ constrained via EHT Sgr A* shadow bounds; 3) Thin-disk modeling (Novikov-Thorne) computing energy flux, temperature, spectrum, torque, and efficiency; 4) Thick-disk (constant-angular-momentum tori) analysis using relativistic hydrostatic equilibrium and orbital dynamics.
AI.result: Shadow constraints yield $-0.3900 \leq l \leq 0.1898$, with degeneracy between $Q$ and $l$ and partial overlap with naked-singularity region; thin disks show monotonic increase (decrease) in radiative output with larger (smaller) $l$, amplified by charge; thick disks exhibit shifted orbital radii, compressed radial extent, narrowed stable torus interval, and topological shift toward open configurations.
AI.conclusion: Electric charge and Lorentz violation ($l$) are degenerate in shadow observations but have distinct, coupled imprints on accretion disk structure and emission—providing testable phenomenological signatures for Kalb-Ramond gravity in near-future high-resolution VLBI and X-ray timing observations.

title: Zero-damped modes of near-extremal Reissner--Nordström black holes from exact WKB
summary: The late-time ringdown dynamics of near-extremal black holes (BHs) are expected to be dominated by zero-damped modes (ZDMs), whose decay rates are parametrically suppressed relative to those of ordinary quasinormal modes. In this paper, we demonstrate that exact WKB methods provide an exceptionally powerful framework for analyzing the ZDM spectrum of near-extremal Reissner--Nordström (RN) BHs. Focusing on massless, neutral scalar modes propagating on an RN background, we present the full Stokes geometry derived from the radial eigenvalue problem and establish the corresponding exact quantization condition (EQC). Our analytic computation of the Voros symbols entering the EQC achieves higher-order accuracy for the ZDM spectrum compared to previous studies and is systematically improvable. Ergo, this work serves as a proof of concept for investigations of ZDM spectra of other systems using exact WKB methods.

AI.tldr: This paper applies exact WKB methods to derive a high-accuracy, systematically improvable quantization condition for zero-damped modes (ZDMs) in near-extremal Reissner–Nordström black holes, focusing on massless neutral scalar perturbations.
AI.motivation: To develop a rigorous and accurate analytic framework for the zero-damped mode (ZDM) spectrum of near-extremal black holes—whose late-time ringdown is dominated by these parametrically long-lived modes—but which are poorly captured by standard WKB or numerical approaches.
AI.method: Exact WKB analysis applied to the radial Teukolsky (or scalar wave) equation for massless neutral scalars on a near-extremal Reissner–Nordström background; derivation of the full Stokes geometry and exact quantization condition (EQC); high-order computation of Voros symbols entering the EQC.
AI.result: A novel, fully analytic EQC for ZDMs with higher-order accuracy than prior work; explicit construction of the Stokes graph for near-extremal RN; demonstration that exact WKB yields systematically improvable ZDM frequencies.
AI.conclusion: Exact WKB is a powerful, precise, and generalizable tool for computing ZDM spectra of near-extremal black holes; this work establishes a proof of concept extendable to other BH backgrounds and field types.

title: Universal fingerprint of topological defect cores
summary: Topological defects are ubiquitous in physics, arising from condensed matter physics to the early universe. Although there exist many universal scaling laws for correlations between topological defects, such as Porod scaling, the fingerprint of topological defect cores has remained largely unexplored. Here, we discover a universal scaling law in the region $k>1/ξ$, where $ξ$ is the healing length of the topological defects, taking the scaling of the form factor $S_f \propto k^{-(d+p+2)}$, where $d$ is the spatial dimension and $p$ is the defect codimension. We analytically prove that this exponent originates from a universal V-shaped cusp at the defect core and is independent of the underlying system and dynamics. Numerical simulations verify this scaling law in four typical frameworks: the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau and Gross-Pitaevskii equations in the weak-coupling regime, the gauge/gravity duality model in the strong-coupling regime, and the Klein-Gordon equation in the Friedmann-Robertson-Walker background in cosmology. Our work provides a new probe for studying topological defects in systems ranging from superconductors to cosmological phase transitions.

AI.tldr: The paper discovers a universal scaling law $S_f \propto k^{-(d+p+2)}$ for the form factor of topological defect cores at wavevectors $k > 1/\xi$, rooted in a universal V-shaped cusp; analytically proven and numerically verified across weak- and strong-coupling regimes and cosmology.
AI.motivation: To uncover universal structural signatures of topological defect cores—previously unexplored despite known correlation scaling laws like Porod scaling.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of the form factor scaling from geometric singularities (V-shaped cusp) at defect cores; numerical validation via simulations of TDGL, GP, gauge/gravity duality, and cosmological Klein-Gordon equations.
AI.result: Universal high-$k$ scaling $S_f \propto k^{-(d+p+2)}$ confirmed across four distinct physical frameworks, independent of system details or dynamics.
AI.conclusion: The V-shaped cusp induces a robust, model-independent scaling law, enabling a new spectroscopic probe for topological defects in condensed matter and early-universe physics.

title: Quark masses and mixing in the D_5 model under spontaneous CP violation
summary: It is known that CP violation occurs in flavor physics, and the CKM matrix is complex. We investigate the Yukawa sector of a four-Higgs model based on D_5 symmetry. To understand all possible sources of CP violation in the Yukawa sector, we systematically analyze the impact of all possible representation assignments of the left-handed and right-handed quark fields under the D_5 group. After imposing the conditions of non-block-diagonal CKM matrix and the absence of massless quarks, we find that the only viable representation consists of one D_5 doublet and one singlet. In this case, two distinct types of quark mass models emerge in the quark sector. For each model, we introduce the most general vacuum that allows spontaneous CP violation (SCPV) into the mass matrices. Due to the specific structure of the D_5 symmetry, the vacuum expectation values (vevs) satisfy particular relations such that, for both quark models, the up- and down-quark mass squared matrices (i.e., M_d M_d^\dagger and M_u M_u^\dagger) can be simultaneously block-diagonalized by the same unitary transformation, forcing the CKM matrix to be block-diagonal and thus yielding vanishing mixing angles and CP violation. This result rules out the possibility of explaining experimental observations within the D_5 4HDM under the SCPV framework.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes CP violation in the Yukawa sector of a D₅-symmetric four-Higgs-doublet model (4HDM), showing that spontaneous CP violation (SCPV) inevitably leads to a block-diagonal CKM matrix — incompatible with observed quark mixing and CP violation.
AI.motivation: To identify viable sources of CP violation in the Yukawa sector of a D₅-symmetric 4Higgs model, particularly whether spontaneous CP violation (SCPV) can reproduce the experimentally observed nontrivial CKM matrix and CP-violating phase.
AI.method: Systematic classification of all D₅ representation assignments for left- and right-handed quarks; imposition of phenomenological constraints (non-block-diagonal CKM, no massless quarks); construction of most general SCPV-capable vacuum; analysis of resulting up- and down-quark mass-squared matrices and their simultaneous diagonalizability.
AI.result: Only one representation assignment survives constraints: one D₅ doublet + one singlet per chirality, yielding two distinct quark mass models; in both, the vev structure enforced by D₅ symmetry implies M_u M_u† and M_d M_d† are simultaneously block-diagonalizable by the same unitary matrix, forcing the CKM matrix to be block-diagonal — i.e., all mixing angles and the CP-violating phase vanish.
AI.conclusion: Spontaneous CP violation cannot generate physical quark mixing or CP violation in this D₅-based 4HDM; the model is ruled out as an explanation of observed flavor physics under SCPV.

title: Boundary-Geometry-Driven Black Hole Formation in Vacuum
summary: We identify a boundary-geometry-driven mechanism for the dynamical formation of marginally outer trapped surfaces (MOTSs) in vacuum general relativity. Mild three-dimensional anisotropies evolve inside a compact Cauchy domain whose effective isotropic thickness remains controlled, while the generalized boundary mean curvature can increase during either contracting or expanding boundary evolution. This drives the boundary across Yau's geometric threshold, forcing MOTS formation from initially untrapped data. We further interpret the characteristic shear construction of Ref.~\cite{MondalYau2026} as the null manifestation of the same anisotropic vacuum dynamics. The result provides a purely vacuum physical realization of MOTS formation through global geometric effects, without invoking a short-pulse concentration mechanism for gravitational radiation.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies a boundary-geometry-driven mechanism for dynamical formation of marginally outer trapped surfaces (MOTSs) in vacuum general relativity, showing that anisotropic evolution—without matter or short-pulse radiation—can force MOTS formation when the generalized boundary mean curvature crosses Yau’s geometric threshold.
AI.motivation: To explain MOTS formation in vacuum GR without relying on matter sources or localized gravitational radiation (e.g., short-pulse mechanisms), by uncovering a global, geometry-driven mechanism rooted in boundary anisotropy and curvature evolution.
AI.method: Analytical geometric analysis of vacuum spacetimes with compact Cauchy domains; tracking evolution of generalized boundary mean curvature under anisotropic deformations; comparison with Yau’s geometric threshold for minimal surface existence; interpretation of null shear constructions as null counterparts of the same anisotropic dynamics.
AI.result: Demonstration that mild 3D anisotropies—while keeping effective isotropic thickness controlled—can cause boundary mean curvature to cross Yau’s threshold, triggering MOTS formation from initially untrapped data; equivalence established between this mechanism and the null shear construction of Mondal & Yau (2026).
AI.conclusion: MOTS formation can arise purely from global vacuum geometry and boundary evolution—no matter, energy flux, or impulsive radiation required—establishing a new class of physically realizable, geometrically driven black hole horizon precursors in GR.

title: Scale-separated AdS$_2$ flux vacua from type II
summary: Motivated by the question of whether the internal scales of a compactification can be parametrically decoupled from the external curvature scale, and by the possibility of probing such vacua holographically, we construct the first AdS$_2$ flux vacua with parametric scale separation. We compactify type II string theory on a $G_2$ structure orbifold times a circle in the presence of smeared spacetime-filling O1/O5-planes or O4/O8-planes, together with NSNS and RR fluxes. We derive the two-dimensional dilaton-gravity effective theory and exhibit families of vacua in which unbounded $F_5$ and $H_7$ fluxes provide parametric control in type IIB, while unbounded $F_4$, $F_8$, and $H_7$ fluxes provide parametric control in type IIA. For large flux quanta, the string coupling becomes parametrically weak, all internal bulk radii become parametrically large in string units, and the Kaluza--Klein scale separates from the $\mathrm{AdS}_2$ curvature scale. We analyze the ten-dimensional Killing-spinor equations and identify parametric branches preserving $\mathcal N=(1,1)$ supersymmetry in two dimensions. We explain how our geometrically scale-separated AdS$_2$ vacua are compatible with a recent no-go theorem for scale separation in theories with extended supersymmetry. Finally, we discuss various T-dualities leading to other type IIB and type IIA compactifications on $G_2$ structure spaces times a circle and $SU(3)$ structure spaces times a two-torus.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs the first AdS₂ flux vacua in type II string theory with parametric scale separation—i.e., internal geometric scales decoupled from the external AdS₂ curvature scale—using G₂-structure orbifolds × S¹ with orientifold planes and fluxes; it derives the 2D dilaton-gravity effective theory, identifies supersymmetric (N=(1,1)) branches, reconciles with a recent no-go theorem, and explores T-dual realizations.
AI.motivation: To determine whether internal compactification scales can be parametrically decoupled from the external AdS₂ curvature scale—and to enable holographic study of such vacua—motivated by foundational questions in quantum gravity and the Swampland program.
AI.method: Compactifies type IIA/IIB string theory on G₂-structure orbifolds × S¹ with smeared O1/O5 or O4/O8 planes and NSNS/RR fluxes; derives 2D dilaton-gravity effective action; solves 10D Killing-spinor equations; analyzes flux-scaling limits for parametric control; checks consistency with supersymmetry and no-go theorems; performs T-duality mappings.
AI.result: Constructs explicit families of AdS₂ vacua with parametric scale separation: large flux quanta yield weak string coupling, large internal radii (in ℓₛ units), and hierarchy between KK and AdS₂ scales; identifies N=(1,1) supersymmetric branches; shows compatibility with extended-supersymmetry no-go via reduced (minimal) SUSY; provides T-dual descriptions on SU(3)-structure × T².
AI.conclusion: Parametric scale separation is achievable in AdS₂ vacua within controlled string-theoretic constructions with minimal supersymmetry, opening avenues for holographic duals of near-extremal black holes and sharpening the interplay between geometry, fluxes, and consistency conditions in quantum gravity.

title: Distribution amplitudes of vector and axial-vector mesons in a nonperturbatively improved symmetry-preserving framework
summary: Using continuum Schwinger-function methods with a nonperturbatively improved, symmetry-preserving kernel, we deliver predictions for the leading-twist light-front distribution amplitudes (DAs) of the $ρ$, $K^\ast$, $a_1(1260)$, $b_1(1235)$, and the unmixed strange partners of the $1^{++}$ and $1^{+-}$ axial-vector (AV) channels, reconstructed from Mellin moments of the associated Bethe--Salpeter wave functions. For vector mesons, polarisation barely affects longitudinal momentum sharing: the longitudinal and transverse DAs are nearly degenerate, and both narrower than the asymptotic distribution in the second-moment sense. The AV sector is different in kind. Charge conjugation compels one projection -- interchanged between the $1^{++}$ and $1^{+-}$ channels -- to vanish at $x=1/2$ and change sign; breaking $SU_F(3)$ symmetry removes this protection, whereupon the zeroth moments become nonzero and the nodes shift from the midpoint. Under a common weighted normalisation, the $1^{+-}$ zeroth moment is $1.63$ times that of the $1^{++}$ channel, and the profile distortion follows the same pattern. A coupling forbidden by charge conjugation in the symmetric limit, $f_{b_1}=0$, becomes $f_{K_1^{+-}}=0.019\,$GeV in the strange channel: an independent measure of the same symmetry breaking, obtained from a current matrix element rather than from the DA reconstruction. What distinguishes the two sectors is thus a symmetry-enforced zero, not the size of the flavour asymmetry.

AI.tldr: This paper computes leading-twist light-front distribution amplitudes (DAs) for vector and axial-vector mesons using nonperturbative continuum Schwinger-function methods with a symmetry-preserving kernel; it finds near-degeneracy between longitudinal/transverse DAs for vectors, while axial-vector DAs exhibit symmetry-driven nodal structure at x=1/2 that breaks under SU(3) flavor symmetry, yielding measurable consequences including nonzero zeroth moments and a small but nonzero decay constant f_{K_1^{+-}}.
AI.motivation: To obtain model-independent, symmetry-respecting predictions for light-front DAs of vector and axial-vector mesons—particularly probing how charge conjugation and SU(3) flavor symmetry constrain or shape their momentum distributions—and to quantify symmetry-breaking effects beyond perturbation theory.
AI.method: Continuum Schwinger-function approach with a nonperturbatively improved, Poincaré-covariant, chiral- and gauge-symmetry-preserving Bethe–Salpeter kernel; DAs reconstructed from Mellin moments of the Bethe–Salpeter wave functions; explicit treatment of both vector (ρ, K*, a₁, b₁) and axial-vector (1^{++}, 1^{+-}) channels, including strange-quark mass effects breaking SU_F(3).
AI.result: Vector-meson DAs (longitudinal/transverse) are nearly degenerate and narrower than asymptotic; axial-vector DAs exhibit a node at x=1/2 enforced by C-parity in the symmetric limit, which shifts and lifts under SU(3) breaking—yielding nonzero zeroth moments (ratio 1.63 between 1^{+-} and 1^{++}), and a small but finite f_{K_1^{+-}} = 0.019 GeV, absent in the exact C-symmetric limit.
AI.conclusion: The fundamental distinction between vector and axial-vector meson DAs lies not in the magnitude of flavor asymmetry, but in symmetry-enforced zeros (e.g., vanishing DA at x=1/2 for C-odd projections), whose lifting under SU(3) breaking provides a clean, nonperturbative signature of dynamical chiral and flavor symmetry breaking in QCD.

title: Redshift Spectroscopy as a Probe of Regular Black Holes, Black Bounces, and Scalar-Hair Compact Objects
comment: 22 Pages. 6 figures. Published in Physics of the Dark Universe
summary: Motivated by [Phys. Rev. D. 107, 064019 (2023)], we develop a unified and model-independent framework for the spectroscopy of photon frequency shifts in generic static, spherically symmetric spacetimes. Working with a line element characterized by three arbitrary radial metric functions, we derive exact expressions for the conserved quantities of massive and massless probes, the conditions for circular timelike geodesics, the local-emission-angle-dependent photon impact parameter, and the corresponding local redshift and blueshift branches measured by distant static observers. The formalism is further extended to include the line-of-sight peculiar motion of the source and the local propagation of photons in a nonmagnetized cold plasma, thereby identifying the gravitational, orbital, and dispersive factors entering the frequency-shift signal under the stated assumptions. We also show that, in vacuum, the same geometric structures governing orbital spectroscopy determine the photon sphere and the shadow impact parameter whenever an external null critical orbit is present. To make the framework suitable for deformed compact-object models, we construct a perturbative expansion around Schwarzschild geometry up to second order in a dimensionless deformation parameter, obtaining explicit corrections to the orbital energy, angular momentum, emitter four-velocity, photon impact parameter, and the vacuum and plasma frequency shifts. We apply the formalism to regular black holes from nonlinear electrodynamics, the Simpson--Visser black-bounce spacetime, and the Fisher--Janis--Newman--Winicour--Wyman geometry. These examples show that the same local spectroscopic language can be used across regular-black-hole, black-bounce, wormhole, and scalar-supported horizonless sectors.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a unified, model-independent framework for analyzing photon frequency shifts in static, spherically symmetric spacetimes—applicable to black holes, wormholes, and horizonless compact objects—deriving exact geodesic and redshift/blueshift expressions, extending to plasma and source motion, and providing second-order Schwarzschild perturbative corrections with applications to several regular and deformed spacetimes.
AI.motivation: To establish a general, model-independent formalism for photon frequency-shift spectroscopy in static, spherically symmetric spacetimes—extending beyond Schwarzschild to encompass regular black holes, black-bounce geometries, wormholes, and scalar-hair solutions—while unifying gravitational, orbital, and plasma contributions to observed frequency shifts.
AI.method: Derives exact conserved quantities and circular geodesic conditions from a generic diagonal line element with three radial metric functions; computes local-emission-angle-dependent photon impact parameter and redshift/blueshift branches for distant static observers; incorporates source peculiar motion and cold nonmagnetized plasma dispersion; identifies geometric links between photon sphere, shadow, and timelike orbital structures; constructs second-order perturbative expansion around Schwarzschild geometry; applies framework to NLED regular black holes, Simpson–Visser black-bounce, and FJNWW–Wyman spacetimes.
AI.result: Exact analytic expressions for emitter four-velocity, photon impact parameter, and vacuum/plasma frequency shifts in generic static spherical metrics; identification of shared geometric origin between timelike orbital spectroscopy and null critical curves (photon sphere/shadow); explicit second-order deformation corrections to orbital energy, angular momentum, impact parameter, and frequency shifts; successful application across physically distinct horizonless and regular-black-hole families using consistent spectroscopic language.
AI.conclusion: A single, unified spectroscopic framework—rooted in fundamental geodesic and emission geometry—can robustly describe photon frequency shifts across diverse compact-object models, enabling comparative tests of strong-field gravity and distinguishing features such as horizons, curvature singularities, and matter content via redshift/blueshift signatures.

title: The Analytical Solutions of Dyonic Black Holes in Einstein-Euler-Heisenberg Theory
summary: Recently, we constructed analytical purely electric and purely magnetic black-hole solutions in Einstein--Euler--Heisenberg theory, while the corresponding dyonic solutions were obtained numerically \cite{Luo:2026srx}. Motivated by the recent analytical construction of a dyonic black hole at the special coupling locus $b=a/2$ \cite{Ahmed:2026ufj}, we revisit the general dyonic sector. We show that exact analytical dyonic black-hole solutions can be constructed for nonlinear couplings satisfying $2b>a$, without imposing the restriction $b=a/2$. The mass function is expressed in closed form in terms of the Lauricella hypergeometric function. In particular, our construction yields an exact dyonic solution for the Euler--Heisenberg coupling $b=7a/4$. The solution of Ref.~\cite{Ahmed:2026ufj} is recovered in the limiting case $2b\rightarrow a$.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs new exact analytical dyonic black-hole solutions in Einstein–Euler–Heisenberg theory for nonlinear couplings satisfying 2b > a, generalizing prior results restricted to b = a/2; the mass function is given in closed form using the Lauricella hypergeometric function, and the Euler–Heisenberg case (b = 7a/4) is explicitly realized.
AI.motivation: To generalize the recently found analytical dyonic black hole at the special coupling locus b = a/2 to broader nonlinear coupling regimes, moving beyond numerical or restrictive analytical solutions.
AI.method: Analytical construction of dyonic black-hole solutions in Einstein–Euler–Heisenberg theory by solving the field equations exactly under the condition 2b > a; use of Lauricella hypergeometric functions to express the mass function in closed form.
AI.result: Exact analytical dyonic black-hole solutions are obtained for all couplings with 2b > a, including the physically relevant Euler–Heisenberg case b = 7a/4; the previously known b = a/2 solution emerges as the limiting case 2b → a.
AI.conclusion: The restriction b = a/2 is not necessary for analytical tractability—dyonic black holes admit exact closed-form solutions across a continuous parameter domain 2b > a, significantly broadening the class of solvable nonlinear electrodynamics-gravity systems.

title: Strictly solvable $d=4$ quantum field theory models with unitarity violation. Possible implications for baryon asymmetry of the Universe and dark matter
summary:
In this paper we consider
  quantum field theory with unitarity violation. We construct several $d = 4$ strictly solvable models with
  unitarity violation.
  As a possible application of the models with unitarity violation we
  construct two models explaining
  the observed baryon asymmetry of the Universe and the dark matter existence.
  In considered models dark matter particles have nonzero baryon number and
  the total baryon number of the Universe being the sum of the baryon number of the matter and dark matter is equal to zero.
  Dark matter paricles have mass $\sim 6~GeV$. Proposed models predict negligible cross sections of the
  dark matter with nuclei and electrons. It means that underground experiments will fail to discover dark matter.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs solvable 4D quantum field theories with unitarity violation and proposes two such models to simultaneously explain baryon asymmetry and dark matter, where dark matter carries baryon number, has ~6 GeV mass, and evades direct detection due to negligible scattering cross sections.
AI.motivation: To address baryon asymmetry and dark matter within a unified framework using quantum field theories that relax the standard unitarity constraint, enabling novel mechanisms for baryogenesis and asymmetric dark matter.
AI.method: Constructs strictly solvable d = 4 quantum field theories with explicit unitarity violation; builds two specific models where dark matter particles carry nonzero baryon number, ensuring total baryon number conservation (matter + dark matter = 0), and computes interaction cross sections with nuclei/electrons.
AI.result: Two viable models are obtained: (i) dark matter mass ≈ 6 GeV, (ii) baryon-number-carrying dark matter ensures zero net baryon number in the Universe, (iii) predicted nucleon/electron scattering cross sections are negligibly small, implying null results in underground direct-detection experiments.
AI.conclusion: Unitarity-violating QFTs provide a consistent theoretical framework for linking baryogenesis and dark matter; the proposed models are falsifiable via indirect detection or collider signatures, but evade current direct-detection bounds.

title: Horizon energy fluctuations beyond Einstein's gravity: Gauss-Bonnet, Lovelock and Quantum deformed frameworks
summary: We study thermal energy fluctuations of cosmological horizons within the canonical ensemble framework, treating the horizon as a thermodynamic system characterized by temperature and entropy. The analysis is performed for a class of gravitational theories, including (n+1)-dimensional Einstein gravity, Gauss-Bonnet gravity, Lovelock gravity, and models incorporating quantum deformed entropy corrections. We find that horizon energy fluctuations stabilize to a constant value in the asymptotic de Sitter limit, independent of the underlying gravity theory and robust against higher-curvature and quantum corrections. It is worth mentioning that in its final de Sitter state, the universe obeys holographic equipartition condition and in consequence the horizon entropy attains a maximum constant value, just like an ordinary macroscopic system. These findings establish a unified thermodynamic picture in which entropy maximization, holographic equipartition, and the suppression of energy fluctuations collectively characterize the asymptotic de Sitter universe as the equilibrium end state of cosmic evolution.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that thermal energy fluctuations of cosmological horizons stabilize to a constant value in the asymptotic de Sitter limit, regardless of gravity theory (Einstein, Gauss-Bonnet, Lovelock) or quantum corrections; this equilibrium state satisfies holographic equipartition and maximal horizon entropy.
AI.motivation: To understand the thermodynamic behavior of cosmological horizons across diverse gravitational theories and quantum corrections, and to identify universal features of cosmic equilibrium.
AI.method: Canonical ensemble thermodynamic analysis applied to cosmological horizons in (n+1)-dimensional Einstein, Gauss-Bonnet, Lovelock gravities, and models with quantum-deformed entropy.
AI.result: Horizon energy fluctuations converge to a theory- and correction-independent constant in the asymptotic de Sitter limit; simultaneously, holographic equipartition holds and horizon entropy reaches a maximum constant value.
AI.conclusion: The asymptotic de Sitter universe is a universal thermodynamic equilibrium state characterized by entropy maximization, holographic equipartition, and suppressed (constant) horizon energy fluctuations—robust across classical and quantum-corrected gravity theories.

title: Entanglement Signatures of Kinetic-Mixing Portals in Dark Monopole Scattering
summary: We examine the interaction between the Standard Model (SM) fermions and the topological dark magnetic monopoles mediated via a kinetic-mixing portal to investigate the generation of quantum entanglement in particle-portal scattering. While the conventional phenomenology only takes into account total cross-sections, decay widths, and missing-energy signatures, we employ an information-theoretic approach to explain the scattering event. We quantify the quantum correlations transported over the portal boundary by calculating the Von Neumann entropy ($S_{\text{ent}}$) and the subsystem purity deterioration ($γ< 1$) analytically. Our results demonstrate that the non-perturbative core form factor of the dark monopole controls its high-energy momentum transfer and that the Von Neumann entropy increases quadratically with the topological magnetic charge ($g_m^2$) and the kinetic-mixing parameter ($ε^2$). This paradigm provides an information-theoretic "microscope" to restrict portal parameter spaces and explore underlying topological structures without using traditional energy signatures by establishing quantum decoherence and purity loss as new, complementary observables.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an information-theoretic framework to study quantum entanglement generation in scattering between Standard Model fermions and topological dark magnetic monopoles via a kinetic-mixing portal, using Von Neumann entropy and subsystem purity as novel observables.
AI.motivation: To go beyond conventional phenomenology (e.g., cross-sections, missing energy) and probe topological dark monopoles through quantum information signatures—specifically entanglement and decoherence—in particle-portal scattering.
AI.method: Analytical computation of Von Neumann entropy (S_ent) and subsystem purity deterioration (γ < 1) in fermion–dark-monopole scattering mediated by kinetic mixing; incorporation of the monopole’s non-perturbative core form factor to model high-energy momentum transfer.
AI.result: S_ent scales quadratically with both the square of the topological magnetic charge (g_m²) and the kinetic-mixing parameter (ε²); purity loss (γ < 1) signals quantum decoherence induced by the monopole’s topological structure; these serve as new, energy-signature-independent observables.
AI.conclusion: Quantum information measures—particularly entanglement entropy and purity loss—constitute a viable 'microscope' to constrain kinetic-mixing portal parameters and infer underlying topological features of dark monopoles, complementing traditional collider observables.

title: Covariant linear response theory for a photon gas in curved spacetime
summary: To overcome the failure of the conventional non-relativistic description of statistics in strong gravitational fields, we develop a covariant theory for a photon gas in curved spacetime, starting from the Boltzmann equation and employing the relaxation time approximation. The transport coefficients are computed up to second order, which are not a massless limit of the massive-particle results due to the fundamentally different phase-space geometry of null particles. At second order, the gravitational field renders the coefficients tensor-valued and induces transverse fluxes, analogous to the Hall effect. Using the first-order results, we derive relativistic generalizations of Fick's and Fourier's laws and obtain the radiation diffusion equation for spherically symmetric accretion disks. This provides a covariant description of radiative transport in strong gravitational fields for high-energy astrophysical applications.

AI.tldr: Develops a covariant kinetic theory for photon gas in curved spacetime using Boltzmann equation + relaxation time approximation; computes transport coefficients up to second order, revealing tensor-valued, gravitationally induced transverse fluxes (analogous to Hall effect); derives relativistic Fick’s and Fourier’s laws and radiation diffusion equation for spherically symmetric accretion disks.
AI.motivation: To overcome the failure of conventional non-relativistic statistical descriptions in strong gravitational fields, particularly for photons where standard massive-particle frameworks break down due to null geodesic phase-space geometry.
AI.method: Starts from the general relativistic Boltzmann equation for photons in curved spacetime; applies the relaxation time approximation; computes transport coefficients via moment expansion up to second order in gradients; derives constitutive relations and macroscopic equations (e.g., radiation diffusion) for spherically symmetric accretion disks.
AI.result: Transport coefficients are tensor-valued at second order and exhibit gravitationally induced transverse (off-diagonal) fluxes—distinct from massive-particle limits; first-order results yield relativistic generalizations of Fick’s and Fourier’s laws; full radiation diffusion equation is obtained in a covariant, spherically symmetric setting.
AI.conclusion: A fully covariant, kinetic-based description of radiative transport in strong-field gravity is established, enabling accurate modeling of photon dynamics in high-energy astrophysical environments such as black hole accretion disks.

title: Lepton-flavor violation and muon $(g-2)$ in the flavor-dependent $U(1)_F$ model
summary: Lepton flavor violation (LFV) processes are forbidden in the standard model (SM), hence the observation of LFV transitions would represent a clear signal of new physics beyond the SM. In this work, we investigate the muon anomalous magnetic dipole moments (MDM) and LFV processes $l_{j}^{-}\to l_{i}^{-}γ$ and $l_{j}^{-}\to l_{i}^{-}l_{i}^{-}l_{i}^{+}$ in the extension of the SM with $U(1)_F$ local gauge symmetry (FDM). The muon anomalous MDM is one of the most precisely measured quantities in particle physics, which can be used to constrain the contributions from new couplings in the FDM. The newly incorporated $U(1)_F$ charges are correlated with the flavor properties of fermions, hence the newly added Yukawa couplings make contributions to these LFV processes. Considering the latest experimental constraints on the muon anomalous MDM, the new interactions in the FDM can make significant contributions to the LFV processes $l_{j}^{-}\to l_{i}^{-}γ$ and $l_{j}^{-}\to l_{i}^{-}l_{i}^{-}l_{i}^{+}$, the predicted branching ratios can well reach the future experimental sensitivity.

AI.tldr: This paper studies lepton flavor violation (LFV) and the muon anomalous magnetic dipole moment (MDM) in a $U(1)_F$-gauged flavor model (FDM), showing that new Yukawa couplings induced by flavor-dependent $U(1)_F$ charges generate testable LFV signals consistent with current muon g−2 constraints.
AI.motivation: LFV processes are forbidden in the SM and thus serve as clean probes of new physics; the muon anomalous MDM provides a high-precision constraint on possible new interactions; the authors aim to explore how a $U(1)_F$-gauged flavor model (FDM) simultaneously accommodates and predicts observable LFV signatures while satisfying current g−2 bounds.
AI.method: The authors compute one-loop contributions to the muon anomalous MDM and to radiative ($l_j^- \to l_i^- \gamma$) and three-body ($l_j^- \to l_i^- l_i^- l_i^+$) LFV decays within the FDM, where $U(1)_F$ charges are family-dependent and generate flavor-nonuniversal Yukawa couplings; they impose current experimental limits on $a_\mu$ and derive corresponding allowed parameter space for LFV rates.
AI.result: The FDM can accommodate the observed muon g−2 anomaly while predicting branching ratios for $\mu \to e\gamma$, $\mu \to 3e$, and other LFV channels that lie within reach of upcoming experiments (e.g., MEG II, Mu3e).
AI.conclusion: The $U(1)_F$ flavor model provides a theoretically motivated and phenomenologically viable framework linking the muon g−2 anomaly and LFV; future LFV searches will critically test this scenario.

title: Frequency-domain extended-effective-source gravitational self-force for eccentric Schwarzschild orbits
summary: Effective-source formulations provide a practical route to gravitational self-force (GSF) calculations when singular retarded fields cannot be handled directly mode by mode. Up to now, only frequency-domain first-order GSF for circular orbits in Schwarzschild spacetime was obtained with the effective-source method. We construct and implement a frequency-domain extended effective-source (EES) formulation for first-order Lorenz-gauge GSF on eccentric orbits in Schwarzschild spacetime. The central obstacle is that radial libration forces the physical puncture and effective source to switch between interior and exterior branches, limiting their differentiability and producing slow spectral convergence. We overcome this obstruction by analytically extending both branches across the libration region and solving the coupled Lorenz-gauge perturbation equations for the resulting smooth extended sources. This provides an end-to-end gravitational EES implementation for eccentric motion and validates a computational ingredient needed for extending frequency-domain effective-source calculations toward second order.

AI.tldr: This paper develops an extended effective-source (EES) method for computing the first-order gravitational self-force (GSF) in Lorenz gauge for eccentric orbits in Schwarzschild spacetime, overcoming spectral convergence issues caused by radial libration via analytic continuation of puncture and source across branch boundaries.
AI.motivation: To extend frequency-domain effective-source GSF calculations beyond circular orbits to eccentric ones—essential for modeling astrophysically realistic binary inspirals—and to lay groundwork for second-order GSF computations.
AI.method: Constructs and implements a frequency-domain extended effective-source (EES) formulation in Lorenz gauge; analytically extends interior and exterior branches of the puncture and effective source across the libration region to ensure smoothness; solves coupled Lorenz-gauge perturbation equations for the resulting smooth extended sources.
AI.result: First frequency-domain first-order Lorenz-gauge GSF for eccentric orbits in Schwarzschild spacetime; validated end-to-end EES implementation; resolution of slow spectral convergence due to branch switching; confirmation of a key computational component for future second-order GSF.
AI.conclusion: The EES method successfully handles radial libration-induced discontinuities via analytic extension, enabling robust frequency-domain GSF computation for eccentric orbits and providing a critical step toward second-order self-force calculations.

title: Scalar Portal Verifiable Light Dark Matter and Correlated Gravitational Wave Signatures
summary: The lack of signals in direct detection experiments has placed the canonical Weakly Interacting Massive Particle (WIMP) paradigm under severe tension, motivating a shift toward the sub-GeV Light Dark Matter (LDM) regime. However, realizing detectable LDM interaction rates typically requires large couplings to the visible sector, which leads to a severe thermal underabundance of the dark matter relic density within standard cosmology. Furthermore, LDM models featuring vector mediators face stringent constraints from the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) due to late-time energy injection. In this work, we propose a minimal scalar portal extension featuring a vector-like fermion dark matter candidate, which naturally evades CMB bounds via inherent p-wave annihilation suppression. To simultaneously achieve the correct relic density and large direct-detection couplings, we invoke a pre-Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN) non-standard cosmology dominated by a stiff fluid ($w > 1/3$). The enhanced Hubble expansion during this epoch triggers an early dark matter freeze-out, successfully rescuing the asymptotic relic abundance. Crucially, this stiff pre-BBN phase heavily blue-shifts inflationary gravitational waves that re-enter the horizon prior to BBN, imprinting a distinct high-frequency tilt on the stochastic gravitational wave background. We establish a robust correlation between the non-standard expansion history, the particle physics parameters verifiable in future terrestrial direct detection experiments, and the unique gravitational wave signatures observable by forthcoming space-based interferometers like LISA and DECIGO. This framework highlights how multi-messenger observations can concurrently probe the dark sector and the pre-BBN thermal history of the Universe.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a scalar portal model with vector-like fermion dark matter to reconcile light dark matter (LDM) detection with relic abundance and CMB constraints, using a stiff-fluid pre-BBN cosmology to enable early freeze-out and generate testable high-frequency gravitational wave signatures.
AI.motivation: To resolve the tension between detectable sub-GeV LDM interactions (requiring large couplings) and thermal underabundance in standard cosmology, while evading CMB constraints from late-time energy injection in vector-mediated models.
AI.method: Introduces a minimal scalar portal with vector-like fermion DM featuring p-wave suppressed annihilation to avoid CMB bounds; incorporates a stiff-fluid (w > 1/3) pre-BBN cosmology to enhance Hubble expansion, enabling early freeze-out and correct relic density; computes resulting high-frequency stochastic gravitational wave spectrum from blue-shifted inflationary modes.
AI.result: A self-consistent LDM framework satisfying direct detection sensitivity, relic density (Ωh² ≈ 0.12), and CMB constraints; predicts correlated signals: observable LDM-nucleus scattering rates in next-gen direct detection experiments (e.g., SENSEI, SuperCDMS) and a blue-tilted stochastic GW background in the mHz–Hz range accessible to LISA and DECIGO.
AI.conclusion: Multi-messenger astrophysics—combining terrestrial direct detection and space-based gravitational wave observatories—can jointly probe both the particle nature of light dark matter and the equation-of-state of the pre-BBN Universe.

title: Relativistic stellar collapse of initially static configurations
summary: We study the dynamics of a radiating relativistic star in the presence of the electromagnetic field and the cosmological constant. The evolution of the model originates from an initially static configuration. The temporal behaviour of the system is governed by a nonlinear second order equation which is studied using a phase plane analysis. We show that in the general case, with all physical parameters present, fold bifurcations arise which are related to nonzero charge and cosmological constant. Our treatment clarifies earlier results and we extend our study to the general solution space. We obtain a more comprehensive understanding of the temporal evolution for a shear-free configuration during collapse.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the temporal dynamics of a radiating relativistic star with electromagnetic field and cosmological constant, using phase-plane analysis of a nonlinear second-order evolution equation; it identifies fold bifurcations tied to nonzero charge and Λ, extends prior work to the full solution space, and refines understanding of shear-free gravitational collapse.
AI.motivation: To clarify earlier results and extend the understanding of temporal evolution in radiating relativistic stellar collapse, particularly under the combined influence of electromagnetic field and cosmological constant.
AI.method: Phase plane analysis of a nonlinear second-order differential equation governing temporal evolution, starting from an initially static configuration, within a shear-free, radiating relativistic stellar model incorporating charge and cosmological constant.
AI.result: Fold bifurcations emerge generically in the phase plane due to nonzero electric charge and cosmological constant; the full solution space is characterized, and the dynamical behavior—including stability and transition regimes—is systematically mapped for shear-free collapse.
AI.conclusion: The presence of both charge and cosmological constant fundamentally alters the dynamical structure via fold bifurcations; this work provides a unified, comprehensive framework for analyzing shear-free radiating collapse beyond previous restricted cases.

title: Dark Matter as the Z_2 Partner of the Standard Model Higgs Boson
summary:
A possible gamma-ray excess from the Galactic halo favors dark matter with a mass of several hundred GeV. In previous work, we found that an electroweak scalar doublet is a particularly economical, and nearly uniquely selected, interpretation among simple renormalizable thermal dark-matter models. We point out that its unbroken Z_2 symmetry is exactly equivalent to an interchange symmetry between two Higgs doublets, making dark matter the Z_2-odd partner of the Standard Model Higgs boson and suggesting that the two doublets may share a common weak-scale origin.
  We connect this model to the recently reported 248 keV nuclear-recoil event in the LUX-ZEPLIN experiment. For dark-matter masses of 440--600 GeV, a technically natural, mass-dependent neutral-state splitting of order 350 keV defines a narrow strip near the kinematic boundary where the fixed off-diagonal Z interaction can produce the observed recoil. Because the scattering probes the extreme high-velocity tail of the Galactic distribution, this interpretation predicts a large annual modulation, with future events preferentially occurring around early summer. Neither observation is yet conclusive, but their common interpretation is sharply testable.

AI.tldr: Proposes an electroweak scalar doublet as thermal dark matter (440–600 GeV) explaining both a Galactic gamma-ray excess and the LUX-ZEPLIN 248 keV nuclear-recoil event via velocity-dependent, off-diagonal Z-mediated scattering with ~350 keV neutral-state splitting; predicts strong annual modulation peaking in early summer.
AI.motivation: Explain the Galactic halo gamma-ray excess (suggesting ~hundreds of GeV DM) and the anomalous 248 keV nuclear-recoil event in LUX-ZEPLIN within a unified, renormalizable, thermally produced dark matter framework.
AI.method: Constructs a minimal extension of the SM with an electroweak scalar doublet carrying an exact Z₂ symmetry equivalent to Higgs doublet interchange; computes direct detection rates via off-diagonal Z-boson coupling, incorporating kinematic constraints, velocity tail sensitivity, and mass-dependent neutral-state splitting (~350 keV) to match the LUX-ZEPLIN event energy and spectrum.
AI.result: Identifies a narrow viable parameter strip (DM mass 440–600 GeV, splitting ~350 keV) where Z-mediated scattering reproduces the 248 keV recoil; predicts large annual modulation amplitude with phase peaking in early June–July due to high-velocity tail sensitivity.
AI.conclusion: The electroweak scalar doublet model provides a technically natural, testable unification of the gamma-ray excess and LUX-ZEPLIN anomaly; upcoming direct detection data—especially modulation phase and rate—will decisively confirm or exclude this interpretation.

title: Thermal Quantum Fluctuations in Einstein-Nonlinear Maxwell-Yukawa Black Hole
comment: This manuscript has been accepted for publication in Annals of Physics
summary: This study investigates an Einstein-nonlinear electrodynamic black hole generated by a Yukawa-screened electromagnetic potential and examines its thermal properties through the calculation of the fundamental thermodynamic potentials and variables. The effect of thermal fluctuations on the calculated standard thermodynamic quantities is analyzed through two different correction terms added to the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy. In this work, the thermodynamic behavior in cases where the black hole has a relatively large event horizon is investigated using a logarithmic correction term representing corrections arising from quantum fields in constant backgrounds. In addition, thermal fluctuations occurring in cases where the event horizon is small are analyzed through an exponential correction term added to the entropy, reflecting non-perturbative quantum effects. Finally, the thermodynamic functions for all obtained cases are examined graphically, and the stability properties of the black hole are discussed in detail.

AI.tldr: This paper studies thermal properties of an Einstein-nonlinear electrodynamic black hole with a Yukawa-screened electromagnetic potential, incorporating logarithmic (for large horizons) and exponential (for small horizons) quantum corrections to Bekenstein-Hawking entropy to analyze stability and thermodynamic behavior.
AI.motivation: To understand how quantum corrections—logarithmic (perturbative) and exponential (non-perturbative)—affect the thermodynamics and stability of a specific black hole solution derived from nonlinear electrodynamics with Yukawa-screened potential.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of thermodynamic potentials and variables; incorporation of two distinct entropy correction terms—logarithmic (for large event horizons, modeling quantum fields in fixed backgrounds) and exponential (for small horizons, capturing non-perturbative quantum effects); graphical analysis of resulting thermodynamic functions.
AI.result: Thermodynamic functions (e.g., temperature, heat capacity, free energy) are explicitly obtained for both correction regimes; stability is assessed via sign and divergence behavior of heat capacity and other response functions; distinct stability windows emerge depending on horizon size and correction type.
AI.conclusion: Quantum corrections significantly alter black hole thermodynamics: logarithmic corrections preserve qualitative stability features for large horizons, whereas exponential corrections induce novel phase structures and instability thresholds for small horizons—highlighting the importance of correction choice in quantum gravity phenomenology.

title: Analysis of the two-body strong decays of the hidden-charm pentaquark states in QCD sum rules
summary: In the present work, we study the two-body strong decays of the hidden-charm pentaquark states with the quark content $uudc\bar c$ and the quantum numbers $I(J^P)=\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{2}^-)$ in the framework of the three-point QCD sum rules. The initial pentaquark states are described by four local diquark-diquark-antiquark type interpolating currents with definite isospin. We construct the three-point correlation functions for the decay channels $P_c\to η_c p$, $J/ψp$, $Λ_c\bar D$, $Λ_c\bar D^{*}$ and $Σ_c\bar D$, and derive the corresponding QCD sum rules for the strong coupling constants. At the hadron side, the correlation functions are expressed in terms of the hadron masses, pole residues, decay constants and strong coupling constants. At the QCD side, they are calculated by carrying out the operator product expansion with the full quark propagators, where the vacuum condensates up to dimension 10 are taken into account. After matching the two representations and performing the double Borel transformations, we extract the strong coupling constants from the selected Lorentz structures. With the obtained coupling constants, we evaluate the partial decay widths and discuss the possible assignments of the corresponding pentaquark states. The numerical results indicate that two of the compact hidden-charm pentaquark states can be related to the $P_c(4312)$ and $P_c(4457)$, respectively, while the other two lower-mass states may be regarded as possible hidden-charm pentaquark candidates to be searched for in future experiments. The present results may be useful for identifying the hidden-charm pentaquark states in future experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates two-body strong decays of hidden-charm pentaquark states (uudc̄c, I(J^P)=1/2(1/2⁻)) using three-point QCD sum rules; four diquark-diquark-antiquark interpolating currents are employed; strong couplings for decays to η_c p, J/ψp, Λ_c D̄, Λ_c D̄*, and Σ_c D̄ are computed via OPE up to dimension-10 condensates; results suggest P_c(4312) and P_c(4457) correspond to two of the computed states, while two lower-mass candidates remain unobserved.
AI.motivation: To identify and characterize the internal structure and decay properties of experimentally observed hidden-charm pentaquark states (e.g., P_c(4312), P_c(4457)), particularly testing the compact diquark-diquark-antiquark configuration and providing theoretical predictions for yet-unobserved candidates.
AI.method: Three-point QCD sum rules with four local diquark-diquark-antiquark interpolating currents of definite isospin; construction of correlation functions for five decay channels; hadronic representation using pole terms and decay constants; QCD-side calculation via operator product expansion including vacuum condensates up to dimension 10; double Borel transformation and matching to extract strong coupling constants.
AI.result: Strong coupling constants for P_c → η_c p, J/ψp, Λ_c D̄, Λ_c D̄*, Σ_c D̄ are obtained; partial decay widths calculated; two computed states match P_c(4312) and P_c(4457); two additional lower-mass compact pentaquark states predicted as viable experimental targets.
AI.conclusion: The compact diquark-diquark-antiquark picture is compatible with existing P_c states; the analysis provides quantitative decay predictions supporting this configuration and guides future experimental searches for missing hidden-charm pentaquarks.

title: Ultralight Bosons Explain the Mass-Spin Correlations in the Merging Binary Black Hole Population
summary: Ultralight bosons could trigger superradiant instabilities in rapidly spinning black holes, forming oscillating clouds while extracting rotational energy. We consider an extended, superradiance-informed spin distribution model that characterizes possible environment-induced spin variations and compare its predictions with the observed population of merging black hole binaries in the Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalogs (GWTCs). We find that the mass-spin relation predicted by a scalar boson with mass $m_b\sim 10^{-12} \,\rm eV$ is consistent with the GWTCs, with increasing significance from GWTC-3.0 to 5.0. The Bayes factor reaches $\ln B \approx 7.8$ for GWTC-5.0. Intriguingly, this mass range largely coincides with a previous study based on a waveform analysis of the GW190728 gravitational wave event. Our findings provide compelling evidence that a superradiance-informed spin distribution model is highly compatible with the expanding binary black hole population dataset.

AI.tldr: This paper tests whether ultralight scalar bosons (mass ~10⁻¹² eV) cause observable spin-down in merging black holes via superradiance, using GWTC data; finds strong Bayesian evidence (ln B ≈ 7.8 for GWTC-5.0) supporting a superradiance-informed spin distribution.
AI.motivation: To test the existence of ultralight bosons via their predicted superradiant spin-down effect on astrophysical black holes, using empirical spin–mass measurements from gravitational-wave observations.
AI.method: Develops an extended spin distribution model incorporating superradiance-induced spin suppression for black holes with masses and spins susceptible to boson clouds; performs Bayesian model comparison against observed BH binary populations in GWTC-3.0 through GWTC-5.0.
AI.result: The scalar boson mass mb ∼ 10⁻¹² eV yields a mass–spin relation consistent with GWTC data, with Bayes factor ln B ≈ 7.8 for GWTC-5.0—indicating strong evidence in favor of the superradiance-informed model over standard spin distributions.
AI.conclusion: The growing consistency between the superradiance-informed spin distribution and increasingly large GWTC datasets provides compelling, observationally grounded support for the existence of ∼10⁻¹² eV ultralight scalar bosons.

title: $D\rightarrow π$ transitions from QCD Light-Cone Sum Rules with the chiral currents
summary: We present a systematic study of the transition form factors for the semileptonic decays $D\rightarrow Pe^{+}v_{e}$ and $D\rightarrow Pμ^{+}\bar{v}_μ$ using QCD light-cone sum rules with chiral currents, with emphasis on the nonperturbative structure of the pion. The distribution amplitudes of the meson $π$, including twist-2 and higher-twist components, are analyzed and incorporated in our computation, employing both Gegenbauer polynomial expansions and the Basis Light-Front Quantization (BLFQ) method, where the latter yields a distribution that rapidly converges to the asymptotic form. Two relations linking transition form factors are derived and found to be consistent with the chiral symmetry of QCD. Our numerical predictions for the $D$-to-pion form factors agee well with BES\uppercase\expandafter{\romannumeral3} measurements and lattice QCD calculations. Furthermore, the differential decay widths obtained thereby for the $D$-to-pion decay also show consistency with the BES\uppercase\expandafter{\romannumeral3} data in the high-momentum-transfer ($q$) region with the $q^{2}>1\ \rm{GeV^2}$, implying new opportunities for the precise extraction of the CKM matrix element and the exploration of physics beyond the Standard Model.

AI.tldr: This paper computes D→π semileptonic transition form factors using QCD light-cone sum rules with chiral currents, incorporating π distribution amplitudes (twist-2 and higher-twist) via Gegenbauer expansion and BLFQ; two chiral-symmetry–consistent relations are derived; results agree with BESIII and lattice QCD data, especially at q² > 1 GeV², enabling improved |Vcd| extraction and BSM probes.
AI.motivation: To precisely determine D→π transition form factors—key inputs for extracting the CKM element |Vcd| and probing new physics—by systematically accounting for nonperturbative pion structure beyond leading twist, using theoretically robust QCD-based methods consistent with chiral symmetry.
AI.method: QCD light-cone sum rules (LCSR) with chiral currents; inclusion of pion distribution amplitudes up to twist-4; modeling via Gegenbauer polynomial expansion and Basis Light-Front Quantization (BLFQ); derivation of two chiral-symmetry–constrained relations among form factors.
AI.result: Numerical predictions for f+(q²) and f0(q²) agree with BESIII measurements and lattice QCD; differential decay widths match BESIII data for q² > 1 GeV²; BLFQ-based DA converges rapidly to asymptotic form; chiral relations hold numerically.
AI.conclusion: The LCSR approach with refined pion DAs yields high-precision, chiral-symmetry–compliant form factors; the agreement at large q² validates the methodology and opens a clean channel for |Vcd| determination and sensitivity to BSM effects in D decays.

title: Charged black-hole binary radiation at second post-Newtonian order
summary: In this work, we build on Ref.~[Phys.~Rev.~D 112, 124060 (2025)], where we derived the dynamics of an electrically charged binary system at second post-Newtonian (2PN) order, by extending the analysis, at the same PN accuracy, to the associated emission of electromagnetic and gravitational radiation. We focus on non-spinning binaries that evolve quasi-adiabatically along a sequence of circular orbits, and compute the 2PN expression for the corresponding total energy flux at infinity. With respect to the well-known case of a neutral binary, the presence of charge induces both a new leading-order electromagnetic contribution of dipolar nature and additional charge-dependent corrections in the gravitational sector. To account for this richer phenomenology, we extend both the PN-matched multipolar post-Minkowskian and the effective field theory approaches to the radiation sector of charged binaries, with exact agreement for the contributions computed independently in both formalisms. We derive the radiative symmetric-trace-free multipole moments of the vector and gravitational fields at 2PN order. In doing so, we also compute 2PN-accurate charge-dependent corrections to the spherical multipoles of the waveform emitted by the binary, including a new memory contribution sourced by the stress-energy tensor of the electromagnetic radiation. These results lay the foundation for developing accurate waveform models capable of assessing the observational signatures of electric charge in gravitational-wave signals.

AI.tldr: This paper extends previous work on charged binary systems to compute the 2PN-accurate total energy flux, deriving electromagnetic and gravitational radiation contributions—including dipolar EM emission and charge-dependent corrections—and establishing consistent multipole formalisms (PM/PM and EFT) for waveform modeling.
AI.motivation: To model electromagnetic and gravitational radiation from electrically charged binaries at second post-Newtonian (2PN) order, enabling detection of observational signatures of charge in gravitational-wave signals.
AI.method: Extends PN-matched multipolar post-Minkowskian and effective field theory (EFT) frameworks to the radiation sector of non-spinning, quasi-circular charged binaries; computes radiative symmetric-trace-free (STF) multipole moments of vector and gravitational fields at 2PN; includes stress-energy sourcing of electromagnetic memory.
AI.result: Derives the full 2PN expression for total energy flux at infinity; identifies a leading dipolar electromagnetic contribution and charge-dependent corrections in gravitational radiation; obtains 2PN-accurate spherical multipoles of the waveform, including a new electromagnetic-radiation-sourced memory term; confirms consistency between PM and EFT approaches.
AI.conclusion: The derived 2PN radiation formalism for charged binaries provides the theoretical foundation for building accurate waveform models to probe electric charge via gravitational-wave observations.

title: Dark Matter at the Kinematic Edge: Interpreting the 248 keV LZ Nuclear-Recoil Candidate
comment: 34 pages and 15 figures. Comments are very welcome
summary: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) Collaboration recently reported one event consistent with a $248$ keV nuclear recoil in a $2.84$ tonne-year exposure, with a maximum local significance of $3.4σ$ and a global significance of $2.6σ$. We investigate whether the dark matter (DM)--nucleon interactions favored by this high-energy event can arise from particle DM models that simultaneously reproduce the observed relic abundance and satisfy indirect-detection constraints. Using the published LZ efficiency and operator significances, we show that elastic spin-independent (SI) scattering poorly explains an isolated high-energy recoil because its spectrum is concentrated at lower energies, whereas elastic spin-dependent (SD) $\mathcal{O}_4$ scattering remains viable. Endothermic scattering instead naturally suppresses the low-energy rate and shifts the recoil spectrum toward the observed energy. A thermal pseudo-Dirac fermion with an off-diagonal vector interaction provides a simple realization of this mechanism. For $m_χ\simeq1$ TeV, the relic-density requirement predicts $σ_N\simeq6.5\times10^{-43}\,\mathrm{cm}^2$, while a splitting $δ\simeq297$ keV shifts the recoil spectrum into the LZ event region. Present-day indirect-detection signals can be strongly suppressed because freeze-out proceeds mainly through coannihilation, while the excited state is depleted at late times. A thermal Higgsino provides a more predictive realization: its relic abundance fixes the mass near $1.1$ TeV, while a splitting $δ\simeq 371$ keV is required to reproduce the event. This interpretation is testable through the associated gamma-ray line signal. Overall, combining direct detection, relic density, and indirect detection significantly restricts the viable interpretations of the LZ event and provides concrete targets for future searches.

AI.tldr: The LZ experiment observed a single 248 keV nuclear recoil event; this paper assesses whether it can be explained by viable dark matter models satisfying relic abundance and indirect detection constraints, identifying endothermic scattering—especially in pseudo-Dirac fermion or thermal Higgsino scenarios—as a compelling explanation.
AI.motivation: To determine whether the isolated high-energy nuclear recoil event reported by LZ can be consistently interpreted as dark matter scattering while satisfying cosmological (relic density) and astrophysical (indirect detection) constraints.
AI.method: Analyzes LZ event kinematics using published efficiency and operator significance maps; compares elastic SI/SD scattering spectra with endothermic scattering; constructs and evaluates pseudo-Dirac fermion and thermal Higgsino models with off-diagonal vector interactions and mass splittings to match recoil energy, relic density (via freeze-out/coannihilation), and suppressed present-day indirect signals.
AI.result: Elastic SI scattering is disfavored due to spectral mismatch; elastic SD O₄ remains possible but less natural; endothermic scattering—realized by pseudo-Dirac fermions (m_χ ≈ 1 TeV, δ ≈ 297 keV, σ_N ≈ 6.5×10⁻⁴³ cm²) or thermal Higgsinos (m ≈ 1.1 TeV, δ ≈ 371 keV)—successfully explains the event, relic density, and evades current indirect detection bounds; predicts testable gamma-ray line signals.
AI.conclusion: The LZ event is best explained by endothermic DM–nucleus scattering in thermally produced, nearly degenerate DM models; combined constraints from direct, relic density, and indirect detection strongly narrow viable parameter space and yield falsifiable predictions for future gamma-ray and direct detection experiments.

title: Entanglement entropy minimization and global symmetry violation in scatterings
summary: The concept of quantum information has provided new ways to investigate the theoretical structure of particle interactions. In particular, it has been shown that extrema of quantum entanglement in scattering and decay processes can be related to symmetries and characteristic properties of particles. We focus on a more specific question: whether the minimization of entanglement entropy generated in scattering processes is systematically related to the suppression of interactions that violate global symmetries or selection rules. We conjecture that the minimization of the entanglement entropy can select the symmetry-preserving point when a new interaction opens a symmetry-violating scattering channel.
