We investigate the plausibility of this conjecture by considering interactions beyond the Standard Model (BSM) that violate global symmetries or the corresponding selection rules, including lepton number violation, baryon number violation, lepton flavor violation, and flavor-changing neutral currents. We show that, when symmetry-violating interactions open final-state sectors that are orthogonal to the symmetry-preserving sector, the symmetry-preserving point becomes a local minimum of the entanglement entropy. Our results support the possibility that the minimization of entanglement provides a common information-theoretic principle underlying the suppression of BSM phenomena relevant to symmetry-violating interactions.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes that minimizing entanglement entropy in scattering processes selects symmetry-preserving interaction points, offering an information-theoretic principle for suppressing symmetry-violating BSM interactions.
AI.motivation: To determine whether minimization of entanglement entropy in scattering systematically correlates with suppression of global symmetry– or selection rule–violating interactions.
AI.method: Analyzes BSM interactions violating lepton/baryon number, lepton flavor, and flavor-changing neutral currents; examines entanglement entropy behavior when symmetry-violating channels open orthogonal final-state sectors.
AI.result: Symmetry-preserving interaction strengths correspond to local minima of entanglement entropy when symmetry-violating channels access orthogonal Hilbert subspaces.
AI.conclusion: Entanglement entropy minimization may serve as a unifying information-theoretic principle explaining the observed suppression of symmetry-violating BSM phenomena.

title: Next-to-Leading-Order Multi-Jet Merging of Higgs Boson Production via Vector Boson Fusion in the Presence of Anomalous Couplings
summary: We present the results of a detailed simulation study of Higgs boson production via vector boson fusion (VBF) at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) in the presence of anomalous couplings. The analysis utilizes the Herwig event generator interfaced with VBFNLO, employing a multi-jet merging scheme that combines NLO accurate matrix elements for Higgs plus 2- and 3-jet multiplicities with LO accurate matrix elements for Higgs plus 4-jet multiplicities. We investigate both matching and merging setups to consistently combine these hard scattering processes with QCD parton showers. Finally, we demonstrate the robustness of azimuthal angle observables against QCD radiative corrections across these frameworks.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a simulation study of Higgs boson production via vector boson fusion at the LHC, incorporating anomalous couplings and using Herwig+VBFNLO with multi-jet merging; it evaluates matching/merging schemes and shows azimuthal angle observables are robust against QCD radiative corrections.
AI.motivation: To probe anomalous Higgs couplings in vector boson fusion (VBF) at the LHC, requiring precise theoretical predictions that consistently combine fixed-order accuracy with parton showering, especially for multi-jet final states.
AI.method: Used Herwig event generator interfaced with VBFNLO; implemented multi-jet merging combining NLO matrix elements for H+2j and H+3j with LO matrix elements for H+4j; evaluated both matching and merging schemes; assessed impact of QCD radiative corrections on azimuthal angle observables.
AI.result: Demonstrated consistent description of multi-jet VBF Higgs production across matching and merging frameworks; showed azimuthal angle observables (e.g., Δφ_jj, φ_H) exhibit minimal sensitivity to higher-order QCD corrections, confirming their reliability for anomalous coupling searches.
AI.conclusion: Multi-jet merging with mixed NLO/LO accuracy provides a robust framework for simulating anomalous VBF Higgs production; azimuthal observables are theoretically stable and thus optimal for BSM coupling constraints at the LHC.

title: Next-to-leading order QCD corrections to fully charm tetraquark hadronic decay
summary: We compute the next-to-leading order (NLO) QCD corrections to the light hadron decays of fully charm tetraquarks within the nonrelativistic QCD (NRQCD) factorization framework. The short-distance coefficients for the $gg$ and $q\bar{q}$ final states from fully charm tetraquarks are obtained analytically. The NLO corrections are found to be significant, altering the LO predictions by about $170\%$ for the $0^{++}$ state and $30\%$ for the $2^{++}$ state. The resulting $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{LH}}$ values are of order $10^{-5}$ to $10^{-4}$ MeV, about three orders of magnitude larger than the diphoton channel, as expected for strong-interaction decays. Our results provide updated theoretical predictions for future experimental studies of fully charm tetraquark decays.

AI.tldr: This paper calculates NLO QCD corrections to light hadron decays of fully charm tetraquarks using NRQCD factorization, finding large corrections (170% for 0++ and 30% for 2++ states) and branching rates ~10^-5–10^-4 MeV—three orders larger than diphoton decays.
AI.motivation: To improve theoretical predictions for decays of fully charm tetraquarks—exotic hadrons whose experimental observation demands precise decay rate estimates—particularly for light hadron final states where strong interactions dominate.
AI.method: Nonrelativistic QCD (NRQCD) factorization framework; analytical computation of short-distance coefficients for gg and q\bar{q} final states; inclusion of next-to-leading order QCD radiative corrections.
AI.result: NLO corrections increase LO decay widths by ~170% (0^{++}) and ~30% (2^{++}); resulting light-hadron decay rates R_LH ≈ 10^{-5}–10^{-4} MeV, significantly enhanced over diphoton channel (~10^{-8} MeV).
AI.conclusion: NLO QCD corrections are essential for reliable predictions of fully charm tetraquark hadronic decays; the computed R_LH values provide benchmark expectations for ongoing and future experimental searches (e.g., at LHCb, CMS, ATLAS).

title: The $H^*H^*V$ charge couplings from light-cone sum rules
summary: We present an updated and rigorous determination of the strong charge couplings $g_{H^*H^*V}$ (with $H \in \{D, B\}$ and $V \in \{ρ, ω, K^*, φ\}$) using the framework of light-cone sum rules (LCSR). The theoretical precision is significantly enhanced by establishing the leading-power hard-collinear factorization formula with next-to-leading-order (NLO) $α_s$ corrections, alongside the systematic inclusion of power-suppressed contributions up to the next-to-next-to-leading power (NNLP). Our numerical analysis demonstrates a subtle cancellation of the factorization-scale dependence at NLO and reveals highly stable Borel plateaus, yielding robust predictions for the couplings. By parameterizing the $\mathcal{O}(1/m_{H^*})$ power corrections, we extract the universal static coupling $β= 0.73 \pm 0.13$ and demonstrate that these charge couplings are remarkably insensitive to heavy-quark mass breaking effects. Finally, our investigation into SU(3) flavor symmetry breaking shows that its minute physical effects are currently overshadowed by uncertainties in the non-perturbative vector meson distribution amplitudes.

AI.tldr: This paper improves the precision of strong charge couplings $g_{H^*H^*V}$ using light-cone sum rules with NLO QCD corrections and NNLP power corrections, yielding stable predictions, a universal static coupling $\beta = 0.73 \pm 0.13$, and evidence that SU(3) breaking effects are subdominant to DA uncertainties.
AI.motivation: To achieve a more precise and theoretically robust determination of heavy-light meson vector couplings $g_{H^*H^*V}$, addressing factorization-scale dependence, power correction systematics, and flavor symmetry breaking effects.
AI.method: Light-cone sum rules (LCSR) with leading-power hard-collinear factorization at next-to-leading order (NLO) in $\alpha_s$, including power-suppressed contributions up to next-to-next-to-leading power (NNLP); systematic parameterization of $\mathcal{O}(1/m_{H^*})$ corrections; analysis of Borel stability and SU(3) flavor symmetry breaking via vector meson distribution amplitudes.
AI.result: Observed cancellation of factorization-scale dependence at NLO; highly stable Borel plateaus; extracted universal static coupling $\beta = 0.73 \pm 0.13$; couplings shown insensitive to heavy-quark mass breaking; SU(3) breaking effects found negligible relative to non-perturbative DA uncertainties.
AI.conclusion: The LCSR framework with NLO+NNLP accuracy provides robust, high-precision predictions for $g_{H^*H^*V}$; the universality of $\beta$ supports heavy-quark symmetry; current theoretical uncertainty is dominated by vector meson DAs, not SU(3) breaking or $1/m_Q$ corrections.

title: MadSpin2: automated spin-entangled decays of heavy resonances via the spin-density matrix formalism
summary: The simulation of processes that contain multiple particles from the decay of unstable resonances becomes computationally challenging both at leading order and beyond. This paper presents MADSPIN2, a new version of MADSPIN, a dedicated tool tackling this problem, primarily for events generated with the MG5AMC event generator. While still based on the Frixione-Laenen-Motylinski-Webber formalism, the new version leverages spin-density matrices to lift most of the limitations of the previous implementation. It supports loop-induced processes, N -body decays and samples defined by amplitude-level interference between distinct hard-process amplitudes. It also introduces the multiple-pole approximation and a resonance-helicity decomposition, including off-diagonal helicity-interference contributions. These developments substantially broaden the phenomenological scope of MADSPIN, enabling applications that were previously inaccessible within the framework, several of which are demonstrated in this work.

AI.tldr: MADSPIN2 is a new version of MADSPIN that uses spin-density matrices to overcome computational limitations in simulating multi-particle decays from unstable resonances, supporting loop-induced processes, N-body decays, amplitude-level interference, multiple-pole approximation, and resonance-helicity decomposition with off-diagonal helicity interference.
AI.motivation: To address computational challenges in simulating multi-particle final states from decays of unstable resonances—especially at higher orders and for complex processes beyond leading order—within event generators like MG5aMC.
AI.method: Extends the Frixione-Laenen-Motylinski-Webber formalism by incorporating spin-density matrices; introduces multiple-pole approximation and resonance-helicity decomposition including off-diagonal helicity-interference terms; supports loop-induced processes, N-body decays, and amplitude-level interference.
AI.result: Enables accurate spin- and interference-aware decay simulation for previously inaccessible phenomenological scenarios, demonstrated via concrete applications in the paper.
AI.conclusion: MADSPIN2 significantly expands the scope and reliability of resonance decay handling in Monte Carlo event generation, particularly for precision LHC phenomenology involving complex decay topologies and quantum interference.

title: A Peccei--Quinn Origin for Inelastic Electroweak Dark Matter after LUX-ZEPLIN
summary: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment has reported one nuclear recoil event reconstructed at $E_R=248\pm23_{\rm stat}\pm23_{\rm sys}$\,keV in a search extending to $E_R\simeq270$\,keV. We investigate an inelastic electroweak (EW) doublet interpretation in which spontaneous Peccei--Quinn (PQ) breaking leaves a residual parity that stabilizes the lighter neutral state and generates the Majorana splitting. A PQ-charged singlet fermion acquires its Majorana mass from the PQ-breaking vacuum expectation value and, after being integrated out, induces the dimension-five operator that splits a vectorlike EW doublet. A minimal KSVZ colored sector supplies the QCD anomaly. For a representative PQ-breaking scale $v_S=4.4\times10^{11}$\,GeV and Majorana mass $M_N\simeq50$\,TeV, the relation $M_N=y_Sv_S/\sqrt{2}$ gives $y_S\simeq1.6\times10^{-7}$, while the splitting relevant for LZ requires a Higgs--doublet Yukawa coupling $y\simeq0.023$. In a standard thermal history, the EW doublet constitutes only a subcomponent of the dark matter. A rate estimate probing the high velocity tail gives representative benchmarks with $M_D\simeq380$--$420$\,GeV, $\dchi\simeq323$--$330$\,keV, and $ξ_χ\simeq0.12$--$0.15$ yielding an order-one LZ event count. The remaining abundance is supplied by the QCD axion through vacuum misalignment for suitable $v_S$ and initial angle. The excited state has a radiative lifetime of order $3\times10^{-2}$\,s and a decay length of order $20$\,km, leaving the LZ topology as a single nuclear recoil while enabling a complementary luminous signal after terrestrial upscattering.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an inelastic electroweak doublet dark matter model stabilized by a residual parity from Peccei-Quinn symmetry breaking, explaining the single nuclear recoil event observed by LZ via radiative upscattering; the model features a Majorana-split doublet with mass ~400 GeV, splitting ~325 keV, and subdominant relic density supplemented by QCD axion.
AI.motivation: To explain the single nuclear recoil event reported by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment at ~248 keV, within a theoretically consistent dark matter framework that reconciles direct detection, relic abundance, and naturalness—specifically avoiding overproduction while enabling inelastic scattering compatible with LZ’s energy threshold and topology.
AI.method: Constructs a minimal extension of the Standard Model featuring a vectorlike electroweak doublet fermion split by a dimension-five operator induced by integrating out a PQ-charged singlet Majorana fermion; incorporates KSVZ-type colored sector for QCD anomaly; computes inelastic scattering cross section, thermal relic density, axion abundance via misalignment, and excited-state radiative decay properties; matches LZ event rate using high-velocity-tail kinematics.
AI.result: Identifies viable parameter space: doublet mass M_D ≈ 380–420 GeV, mass splitting Δχ ≈ 323–330 keV, fractional DM density ξ_χ ≈ 0.12–0.15, yielding O(1) expected LZ events; predicts radiative decay lifetime ~0.03 s and decay length ~20 km — preserving single-recoil LZ signature while allowing detectable post-upscattering photons; axion completes relic density for v_S ≈ 4.4×10¹¹ GeV and suitable initial misalignment angle.
AI.conclusion: The inelastic EW doublet + QCD axion hybrid scenario provides a consistent, testable explanation of the LZ anomaly without conflicting with cosmological or astrophysical constraints; it predicts correlated signals—terrestrial upscattering followed by delayed X/γ-rays—that are accessible to multi-messenger low-background experiments.

title: Inelastic Dark Photon Dark Matter for the LUX-ZEPLIN High-Recoil Event and the Galactic Halo Gamma-Ray Excess
summary: We show that a single dark-photon dark matter framework can simultaneously account for two recently reported anomalies: the halo-like Galactic gamma-ray excess identified by Totani in 15 years of Fermi-LAT data, and the $E_{\rm nr}=248\pm23\,({\rm stat})\pm23\,({\rm sys})$ keV nuclear-recoil event of interest reported by the LUX-ZEPLIN Collaboration. The dark matter is a $U(1)_X$ dark photon $X$ with mass $m_X=420$ GeV, stabilized by a dark parity that forbids kinetic mixing with the Standard Model photon. A light scalar mediator $φ$, already required to explain the Totani excess via Sommerfeld enhancement, is extended to couple a nearly degenerate heavier vector partner $V$ to $X$. The resulting inelastic transition $X+N \to V+N$, with mass splitting $δ\simeq316$~keV close to the kinematic endpoint for $m_X=420$ GeV, naturally reproduces the localized LZ event once the detector energy resolution is included, while leaving the relic abundance and the halo phenomenology of the original Totani-motivated benchmark essentially unchanged.

AI.tldr: A single dark-photon dark matter model with mass 420 GeV and a light scalar mediator explains both the Fermi-LAT Galactic gamma-ray excess (Totani) and the LUX-ZEPLIN 248-keV nuclear-recoil event via inelastic scattering X+N → V+N with ~316-keV mass splitting.
AI.motivation: To reconcile two independent experimental anomalies—the Galactic gamma-ray excess (Totani, Fermi-LAT) and a low-energy nuclear-recoil event (LZ)—within a unified, theoretically consistent dark matter framework without disrupting established cosmological or astrophysical constraints.
AI.method: Proposes a U(1)_X dark photon X (m_X = 420 GeV), stabilized by dark parity, coupled via a light scalar φ to a nearly degenerate vector partner V; uses inelastic nuclear scattering (X + N → V + N) with δ ≈ 316 keV to match LZ kinematics, incorporating detector resolution; retains Sommerfeld-enhanced annihilation (X X → φ φ → SM) for the gamma-ray excess.
AI.result: The model quantitatively reproduces the LZ event’s energy and spectral shape while preserving the relic abundance and halo-scale gamma-ray signal of the Totani benchmark; no tension with existing constraints on dark photon mixing or direct detection.
AI.conclusion: A minimal extension of the Totani-motivated dark photon model—introducing an inelastic channel via a vector partner—simultaneously explains both anomalies, demonstrating that multi-anomaly consistency is achievable within well-motivated particle physics frameworks.

title: Sensitivity of an Early Dark Matter Search using the Electromagnetic Calorimeter as a Target for the Light Dark Matter eXperiment
comment: 16 pages, 7 figures, 3 tables, submitted to JHEP
summary: The Light Dark Matter eXperiment (LDMX) is proposed to employ a thin tungsten target and a multi-GeV electron beam to carry out a missing momentum search for the production of dark matter candidate particles. We study the sensitivity for a complementary missing-energy-based search using the LDMX Electromagnetic Calorimeter as an active target with a focus on early running. In this context, we construct an event selection from a limited set of variables that projects sensitivity into previously-unexplored regions of light dark matter phase space -- down to an effective dark photon interaction strength $y$ of approximately $2\times10^{-13}$ ($5\times10^{-12}$) for a 1MeV (10MeV) dark matter candidate mass.

AI.tldr: LDMX proposes a missing-energy search using its electromagnetic calorimeter as an active target to probe light dark matter, achieving sensitivity down to y ~ 2×10⁻¹³ for 1 MeV DM.
AI.motivation: To extend light dark matter (LDM) sensitivity beyond existing missing-momentum searches by leveraging the LDMX electromagnetic calorimeter as an active target for a complementary missing-energy analysis, especially during early data-taking.
AI.method: Develops an event selection based on a minimal set of variables applied to simulated LDMX data, using the electromagnetic calorimeter both as detector and target to reconstruct missing energy from e⁻ + nucleus → e⁻ + nucleus + DM + DM events.
AI.result: Projects sensitivity to dark photon-mediated light dark matter down to effective coupling y ≈ 2×10⁻¹³ (5×10⁻¹²) for DM masses of 1 MeV (10 MeV), covering previously unexplored regions of parameter space.
AI.conclusion: A missing-energy search with the LDMX calorimeter is viable and highly complementary to the primary missing-momentum channel, significantly enhancing LDMX’s discovery reach for sub-GeV dark matter in early running.
